audits.purpose: An Android-first in-app browser built on react-native-webview 13.16.1. Features: an omnibox with history/bookmark/recent-search suggestions, up to 8 tabs (only 2 WebViews are kept alive at once and the rest are reloaded when reopened), a Home start page with quick-site tiles, back/forward/home/reload, a per-tab Desktop Site toggle, an error overlay, handling of intent:// and custom schemes (TikTok snssdk and app-link bounces are blocked or kept inside the app), link long-press actions, and tab/session persistence in MMKV. It also connects every WebView to media detection in three ways: two injected JS scripts (chrome bridge + media observer) sharing onMessage, a URL-extension check in onShouldStartLoadWithRequest, and a native per-request observer. The native observer comes from scripts/apply-webview-media-hook.js, which patches RNCWebViewClient.shouldInterceptRequest to call MediaNetworkBridge.observeRequest by reflection.
audits.architecture:
Entry point: src/app/(app)/(tabs)/browser.tsx re-exports src/browser/BrowserScreen.tsx.

BrowserScreen
- useBrowserEngine() (hooks/useBrowserEngine.ts) is a facade. It returns the active tab's controller from tabControllerRegistry (tabs/tab-controller-registry.ts), or a no-op controller until one registers.
- It provides that controller via BrowserEngineProvider (engine/BrowserEngineContext.tsx).
- BrowserScreenBody renders BrowserHeader (AddressBar + SuggestionOverlay modal + ReloadStopButton + BrowserTabBadge + BrowserOverflowControls), BrowserProgressBar, BrowserContainer, BrowserMediaDownloadBar (out of scope), BrowserToolbar (Back/Forward/Home) and BrowserTabSwitcher (modal).
- A useFocusEffect consumes pendingNavigationService so History, Bookmarks, quality flow and Home quick access can open URLs in the browser.

BrowserContainer
- Maps store.mountedTabIds (at most MAX_MOUNTED_WEBVIEWS = 2, tabs/constants.ts:3) to MountedTabWebView, keyed by tabId.
- Each MountedTabWebView calls useTabScopedBrowserEngine(tabId) (hooks/useTabScopedBrowserEngine.ts). That creates the per-tab controller (webViewRef, sourceUri state, 8 mutable refs, loadUrl/goBack/goForward/reload/stop/goHome) and registers it in the registry.
- It nests a second BrowserEngineProvider, wires useBrowserChromeBridge (long-press, scroll, pull-to-refresh, SPA URL) and renders BrowserWebView.

BrowserWebView (components/BrowserContainer/BrowserWebView.tsx)
- Consumes useBrowserEngineEvents() (975-line hook that turns WebView callbacks into store updates).
- Consumes useMediaDetectionBridge() (media-detection).
- Concatenates the chrome and media injected scripts, demultiplexes onMessage (chrome channel first, media only when isActive), handles onOpenWindow by loading popups into the same tab, and binds a native observation scope (viewTag to tab/epoch/pageUrl) so MediaNetworkBridge events can be attributed.
- Owns a ~250-line Desktop-mode state machine (appliedDesktopMode, cacheMode, 6 refs, 5 effects) that changes the userAgent prop and then reloads.

State
- One zustand store (stores/browserStore). It holds tabs[], activeTabId and mountedTabIds, plus a duplicated "chrome mirror" of the active tab (currentUrl, isLoading, progress, error, canGoBack, desktopMode...).
- Tab mutations go through pure reducers (tabs/tab-operations.ts, mount-pool.ts). patchTab/updateTab mirror chrome fields only when the tab is active.
- Tab metadata is persisted debounced to MMKV (tabs/tab-persistence.service.ts). A second, legacy single-URL session store (session/session-persistence.service.ts) holds scroll positions, the last successful URL, and a flush to an async adapter.

Commands and policy
- Toolbar, header, error view and hardware Back go through services/active-tab-navigation.service.ts, which resolves the registry controller by tabId.
- Navigation policy is split across browser-navigation-policy.ts (pure classifier), intent-uri-resolver.ts, intent-navigation.service.ts, external-navigation.service.ts, popup-navigation.service.ts and services/navigation.service.ts.
- Diagnostics: every handler calls logBrowser* (diagnostics/browser-runtime-diagnostics.service.ts, DEV-only console.log).

Native
- A postinstall script string-patches node_modules RNCWebViewClient.java in two ways:
  1. It adds shouldInterceptRequest, which calls com.anonymous.vidorax.mediadetection.MediaNetworkBridge.observeRequest by reflection.
  2. It changes the shouldOverrideUrlLoading lock timeout to deny non-http schemes.
- Cookies rely on the process-wide Android CookieManager. incognito is never set and thirdPartyCookiesEnabled=true.
audits.endToEndTrace:
Flow A: type "instagram.com" in the omnibox and press Go.
1. AddressBar.tsx:126 inline TextInput onFocus runs useAddressBar.onFocus (useAddressBar.ts:92) and sets isFocused. SuggestionOverlay (SuggestionOverlay.tsx:142) opens a Modal with its own TextInput and focuses it after 40ms.
2. Submit goes to useAddressBar.submit (useAddressBar.ts:110), then navigationService.resolveSubmission, then classifyNavigationInput (utils/url.ts:189), which returns https://instagram.com.
3. navigateTo calls loadUrlActiveTab (active-tab-navigation.service.ts:165), then loadUrlForTab (:138), then controller.loadUrl (useTabScopedBrowserEngine.ts:174).
4. loadUrl:
   - skips when the URL is the same document as tab.url (:197);
   - applies the platform desktop recommendation (:207-224; dead, since every adapter returns prefersDesktopWebView:false);
   - pushes chromeNavRef (never read);
   - bumps the epoch and sets tab {url, loading:true, progress:0.02} (:242);
   - persists the session (:249);
   - calls setSourceUri(trimmed) (:251). Navigation happens only if this React state actually changes. FRAGILE: if sourceUri already equals the URL (you typed the site you originally opened, then clicked around inside it), nothing loads but loading stays true, so the spinner is stuck, and reload() refuses to run while loading (:141).
5. The value change re-registers the controller (:304-306). The registry emits, BrowserScreen re-renders the whole chrome via uSES (useBrowserEngine.ts:15).
6. BrowserWebView gets a new source prop (:428). RN applies the props, then loadSource in onAfterUpdateTransaction.
7. The patched RNCWebViewClient.shouldOverrideUrlLoading blocks on JS, then onShouldStartLoadWithRequest (useBrowserEngineEvents.ts:842):
   - classifyBrowserNavigation returns INTERNAL_WEB;
   - the extension regex decides whether to call mediaDetectionEngine.observeUrl;
   - returns allow.
   Non-whitelisted custom schemes never reach this callback. RN's WebViewShared.tsx:53-65 hands them to Linking.openURL first.
8. onLoadStart (:426) sets loading true and handleLoadStart binds the native scope (BrowserWebView.tsx:479-486). onLoadProgress (:587) is throttled and clears loading at >=0.99. onNavigationStateChange (:297) applies url/title/canGoBack through updateTab. onLoadEnd (:472) clears loading, calls browserSyncService.onSuccessfulPage, recordSuccessfulVisit (history), and scrollPositionService.scheduleRestore.
9. At onPageFinished RN runs injectedJavaScript: the chrome bridge (browser-chrome.injected.ts) plus the media observer (fetch/XHR/MSE hooks at media-detection/observers/injected-script.ts:518-564). These run late and in the main frame only, so first-load video requests and iframe players are missed by the JS layer. The before-content script only starts a PerformanceObserver and is itself run from onPageStarted via evaluateJavascript (RNCWebViewClient.java:90), so it is not guaranteed to run first.
10. In parallel, every subresource hits the patched shouldInterceptRequest (RNCWebViewClient.java:168) → reflection → MediaNetworkBridge.observeRequestFrom (@Synchronized, MediaNetworkBridge.kt:132) → DeviceEventEmitter 'VidoraMediaNetworkCandidate' → native-network.contract.ts:149 resolveNativeObservationScope(parentViewId), which matches the tag registered in BrowserWebView.tsx:138-150.
11. SPA navigation inside Instagram/TikTok: RNCWebViewClient.doUpdateVisitedHistory (RNCWebViewClient.java:74-81) dispatches TopLoadingStartEvent, so onLoadStart sets loading true and onNavigationStateChange immediately sets it false. canGoBack is updated correctly. The chrome bridge's spa_navigation message also rewrites the tab URL (useBrowserChromeBridge.ts:93-118). onLoadEnd never fires, so SPA pages are not recorded in history.

Flow B: Android hardware Back on a web page.
- useBrowserHardwareBack (useBrowserHardwareBack.ts:38) registers a BackHandler through useAndroidBackHandler, which uses expo-router useFocusEffect (a React.useEffect).
- TabsLayout (_layout.tsx:31) also calls useTabExitBackHandler (use-tab-exit-back-handler.ts:34). That handler is enabled when pathname === '/browser' and always returns true (toast "Press back again to exit" / exitApp).
- React runs child effects before parent effects, and the exit handler also re-registers whenever pathname changes. So it is registered after the browser handler.
- RN BackHandler dispatches last-registered first (BackHandler.android.js:30). BREAKS: Back on the browser tab never reaches goBackForTab. The user gets the exit toast instead of going back in web history.

Flow C: page fails offline, then user taps Retry.
- onError (useBrowserEngineEvents.ts:636) → setError; retryUrl = failing URL (browser-failure.service.ts:25-36). BrowserContainer hides the WebView and BrowserErrorView shows.
- Retry (BrowserErrorView.tsx:25-35) → controller.loadUrl(retryUrl). tab.url already equals retryUrl, so loadUrl returns at the same_document guard (useTabScopedBrowserEngine.ts:197-205) without clearing the error.
- BREAKS: Retry does nothing. Only the header Reload button (reloadForTab → webView.reload) or Home recovers. Pull-to-refresh is also disabled while error != null (useBrowserChromeBridge.ts:87).

Flow D: Home, then quick site, then Back.
- goHome (useTabScopedBrowserEngine.ts:74) injects location.replace('about:blank'), calls clearHistory, sets sourceUri=about:blank and hides the WebView (opacity 0).
- Tile → loadUrl → the page loads on top of the about:blank entry.
- Back → WebView goBack to about:blank → onNavigationStateChange hits the 'ignore_transient_blank' early return (useBrowserEngineEvents.ts:320-331), because sourceUri is a real URL.
- LIKELY BREAKS: blank page, address bar still shows the site, flags stale. The "leftover blank → goBack/goHome" branch (:333-347) is effectively unreachable.

Flow E: cold start.
- The store state initializer hydrates tabs from MMKV (stores/browserStore/state.ts:22) and mounts only the active tab, which loads tab.url.
- useBrowserSessionContinuity (useBrowserSessionContinuity.ts:27) runs its one-shot effect with the no-op facade loadUrl captured during the first render, before the tab controller has registered. The async restore is therefore dead.
- It still calls setPageTitle(restorable.title) when the active tab is Home (:77-81), so the Home tab is renamed to the last visited page's title and that name is persisted.

Flow F: Desktop Site toggle.
- browser-menu-actions.ts:161 → setDesktopMode(user, tabId).
- BrowserWebView transition effect (:309) → executeDesktopReload sets appliedDesktopMode + LOAD_NO_CACHE → commit → effect (:282) → reload().
- Works in the simple case. Toggling mid-load and then navigating can cause a redundant second reload (deferredDesktopReloadRef is not cleared by the [sourceUri] effect at :225).
audits.verdictRationale:
The browser looks polished, and the WebView configuration choices behind login persistence are correct: no incognito, third-party cookies on, the shared Android CookieManager, stock mobile UA, snssdk/app-link containment, and no branding token in the UA. Instagram and TikTok should load and stay logged in; I did not run it on a device.

The core engine, though, is an over-built pile of refs, epochs and "generation" guards: useTabScopedBrowserEngine plus a 975-line useBrowserEngineEvents plus a 250-line desktop-mode state machine in BrowserWebView. It still has user-visible bugs in the most basic flows:
- Android hardware Back is swallowed by the tab-exit handler.
- The error screen's Retry is a no-op.
- Re-typing a URL leaves a stuck spinner with nothing loading.
- Back after Home can land on about:blank.
- Popups replace the current page and break OAuth.
- HTML5 fullscreen video is off.

The pure modules are good and testable: URL classification, navigation/intent policy, tab reducers and persistence, the URL sanitizer and the chrome bridge parser. Keep those. Rewrite the engine/event layer as one simple per-tab controller with an imperative loadUrl. Delete the dead UI, the verify-only "contract" exports, the legacy session store and most diagnostics. Refactor the native hook to be cheap and fail loudly.

keepWorthy.why: A pure, well-bounded omnibox classifier: URL vs search vs invalid vs blocked, plus localhost/IPv4/TLD heuristics, security level and display formatting. No side effects, and easy to unit test.

A pure classifier for website-originated navigations: social native-app schemes including every snssdk* id, market:, intent:, dangerous schemes, mailto/tel. It correctly generates an originWhitelist so RN WebView does not auto-launch those apps. Trim the duplicate isBrowserHomeUrl and the verify-only helpers.

A careful, pure intent:// parser. It prefers S.browser_fallback_url, reconstructs http(s) URLs safely, ignores component/extras and fingerprints for loop protection. Together with intent-loop-guard.ts it solves the real Instagram applink / TikTok intent bounce loops.
Pure create/close/switch/update reducers with explicit result types (CREATED/LIMIT_REACHED/REPLACED_HOME...). Correct neighbour selection when closing the active tab. Testable as-is.
A small pure LRU mount-pool reconcile that protects the active tab. The concept is right for capping WebView memory; raise the cap.

Defensive hydrate: schema version, sanitize each entry, dedupe, cap to MAX_OPEN_TABS, recover to a Home tab and never throw. The debounced MMKV write is fine. Drop the legacy-session migration once the session store is removed.
Strips OAuth codes/tokens and credentials from URLs before persisting. A cheap privacy win worth keeping, though 'session' and 'auth' may be too aggressive.
A strict parser for the chrome channel: size cap, channel check, per-type payload validation, scheme allowlist. A good pattern for demultiplexing WebView messages.
A compact, idempotent page script for link long-press, throttled scroll, Android pull-to-refresh and pushState/replaceState SPA URL tracking. Works on Instagram/TikTok-style SPAs.

Centralizes WebView props, and the cookie/session decisions are correct for staying logged in: no incognito, thirdPartyCookiesEnabled, domStorage, no custom applicationName, desktop UA only on demand. Keep the file; add allowsFullscreenVideo and turn off mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction.
A simple, working bottom-sheet tab list with close/new/limit handling. It unmounts when hidden, which works around Android transparent-Modal touch leaks.

The focused omnibox sheet with its own TextInput, Enter-key fallback for Android keyboards inside Modal, and a keyboard-persisting suggestion list. The UX is solid. Simplify the dual-TextInput handoff in AddressBar.
Works: indexes history, bookmarks and recent searches with ranking, caching and debouncing. Somewhat heavy (527 lines) but self-contained, and nothing in it touches the WebView.
A clean Chrome-like reanimated progress bar driven only by store selectors.
Straightforward menu model: bookmark, copy, share, desktop toggle, open external, downloads/library deep links. Captures tabId at press time. Easy to keep.

Both ideas are right and needed. Passive shouldInterceptRequest observation is the only way to see media requests from any site, including iframes and service workers. Denying custom schemes on the shouldOverrideUrlLoading timeout fixes real TikTok snssdk hangs. The implementation should become a committed patch-package diff that calls MediaNetworkBridge directly, with no per-request reflection.

bugs.description: Android hardware Back on the browser tab never reaches the browser's own handler. TabsLayout (src/app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:31) registers useTabExitBackHandler, which is enabled when pathname==='/browser' and always returns true. useBrowserHardwareBack (src/browser/hooks/useBrowserHardwareBack.ts:38) registers through the same useFocusEffect/useEffect path. Parent effects run after child effects, and the exit handler also re-registers on every pathname change, so it is the most recent subscription. RN BackHandler dispatches last-registered first (react-native/Libraries/Utilities/BackHandler.android.js:30), so the exit handler always wins.
bugs.userImpact: Pressing Back while reading Instagram or any site shows 'Press back again to exit' (and a second press exits the app) instead of going back a page. On Android this is the main navigation gesture.

bugs.description: Retry calls controller.loadUrl(retryUrl), and retryUrl is the failing URL (browser-failure.service.ts:25-36). tab.url already equals that URL, so loadUrl hits the same_document early return (useTabScopedBrowserEngine.ts:197-205). The error is never cleared and nothing reloads. Even without that guard, setSourceUri to the same value would not reload. Pull-to-refresh is also disabled while an error is set (useBrowserChromeBridge.ts:87).
bugs.userImpact: After an offline/DNS/timeout failure, the big Retry button does nothing. Users have to find the small header reload icon, go Home, or type a different URL.

bugs.description: Navigation depends on the React state setSourceUri(trimmed) changing. When the URL equals the current sourceUri (the last chrome-loaded URL) but the WebView has since navigated elsewhere by link or SPA, React bails out and no load is issued. updateTab already set {url, loading:true, progress:0.02} at :242, so the store shows a load that never happens. reload() then refuses to run because tab.loading is true (:141). The same path is used by the omnibox, history/bookmark pendingNavigation (BrowserScreen.tsx:103-106) and home tiles.
bugs.userImpact: Open instagram.com, browse to a reel, then type instagram.com again: the spinner and 2% progress bar never finish, the address bar shows instagram.com while the page still shows the reel, and Reload is blocked until the user taps Stop.

bugs.description: goHome (useTabScopedBrowserEngine.ts:74-98) leaves about:blank in WebView history: it injects location.replace, calls clearHistory before that commits, and sets sourceUri to about:blank. After the user opens a site from Home, native canGoBack is true and Back returns to about:blank. onNavigationStateChange returns early with 'ignore_transient_blank' whenever sourceUri is a real URL, so neither the store nor the canGoBack refs update, and onLoadStart/onLoadEnd also ignore about:blank. The recovery branch at :333-347 is unreachable in this state. (Plausible; confirm on device.)
bugs.userImpact: Home → tap a quick site → Back shows a white page while the address bar still shows the site; another Back is needed.

bugs.description: onOpenWindow loads every window.open / target=_blank URL into the current tab (loadUrl). The opener page is destroyed, which breaks window.opener/postMessage popup flows such as 'Sign in with Google/Apple/Facebook' popups and payment popups. Tabs exist, but popups never create one. The link long-press 'Open in New Tab' is also hard-disabled (actions/builtins/open-in-new-tab.action.ts:12, no-op callback at hooks/useBrowserLongPressActions.ts:58).
bugs.userImpact: Popup-based logins fail or loop, and 'open in new tab' links replace the video page the user was about to download from.

bugs.description: allowsFullscreenVideo is never passed. RN WebView Android defaults mAllowsFullscreenVideo=false (RNCWebViewManagerImpl.kt:41), so onShowCustomView is not implemented and HTML5 requestFullscreen is ignored. Separately, webview-configuration.ts:75 sets mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction=true, which maps to WebSettings.mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture (RNCWebViewManagerImpl.kt:537). In Android WebView that likely blocks muted autoplay as well (confirm on device).
bugs.userImpact: The fullscreen button in web video players does nothing. Instagram Reels and TikTok feeds may not autoplay, and native media detection only sees the stream after the user taps play.

bugs.description: The one-shot hydrate effect captures loadUrl from the context value of the first render. That value is the no-op facade from createNoopTabController, because the tab controller registers later in a child effect and hydratedRef blocks a re-run. The async restore never loads anything. It still runs setPageTitle(restorable.title) when the active tab is Home (:79-81), overwriting and persisting the Home tab's title with the last visited page's title.
bugs.userImpact: After restarting on a Home tab, the tab switcher shows a stale title (e.g. 'Instagram') for that Home tab. The 'async session restore' safety net silently does nothing.

bugs.description: The injected shouldInterceptRequest does Class.forName + getMethod + invoke by reflection on every subresource request. MediaNetworkBridge.observeRequestFrom (android/.../MediaNetworkBridge.kt:132) is @Synchronized and runs about 10 regexes per request, compiling new Regex objects per request in instagramLooksMedia (:392) and pathClassOf (:467). All WebView network interception threads are serialized through one monitor.
bugs.userImpact: Slower page and feed loading on request-heavy sites (Instagram/TikTok make hundreds of requests), which gets worse with two mounted WebViews plus the service-worker client.

bugs.description: The media observer's fetch/XHR/MediaSource hooks live in injectedJavaScript (media-detection/observers/injected-script.ts:518-564), which RN Android runs at onPageFinished. The before-content script only starts a PerformanceObserver and is itself run via evaluateJavascript in onPageStarted (RNCWebViewClient.java:90, no addDocumentStartJavaScript), so it is not guaranteed to run first. injectedJavaScriptForMainFrameOnly keeps its default true (RNCWebView.java:66).
bugs.userImpact: The JS layer misses video manifests and requests fired during initial load and every iframe-embedded player (YouTube/Vimeo/JW embeds on arbitrary sites). 'Download from any site' then depends entirely on the fragile native URL heuristics.

bugs.description: Navigation policy is split. RN WebView's JS (node_modules/react-native-webview/src/WebViewShared.tsx:53-65) calls Linking.openURL for any URL whose scheme is not in originWhitelist, before onShouldStartLoadWithRequest runs. So whatsapp:, tg:, spotify: etc. launch external apps unclassified, while whitelisted-but-unclassified schemes (geo:, maps:, itms-apps:, googlechrome:) fall into BLOCK_UNKNOWN_SCHEME and are silently dropped.
bugs.userImpact: Behaviour is inconsistent: WhatsApp share buttons open WhatsApp, but 'Open in Maps' links do nothing, with no feedback.

bugs.description: Both patches use exact multi-line string anchors, and on mismatch they only console.warn and continue (also at :102-105). Any react-native-webview upgrade or whitespace change silently disables native media observation and the custom-scheme timeout containment. Nothing fails at build time.
bugs.userImpact: After a dependency bump, detection on 'any site' quietly degrades and TikTok snssdk hangs can return, with no signal to the developer.

bugs.description: RN Android emits TopLoadingStartEvent from doUpdateVisitedHistory (RNCWebViewClient.java:74-81), so every pushState/replaceState (each Reel/TikTok URL change) runs onLoadStart, which sets loading true. Correctness then depends on React batching it with the immediate loading=false from onNavigationStateChange. It also resets the scroll-restore guard and persists the session on every SPA hop. Because onLoadEnd never fires for SPA navigations, recordSuccessfulVisit never records them.
bugs.userImpact: Browser history misses most Instagram/TikTok pages the user actually viewed. Loading state can flicker if batching does not apply.

bugs.description: When loadUrl applies a platform desktop recommendation, the new source prop commits with the old appliedDesktopMode. The [sourceUri] effect sets appliedDesktopMode one commit later, so the UA changes mid-load, the exact TikTok abort the comment at :216-219 warns about. This is currently latent because every platform adapter returns prefersDesktopWebView:false. Separately, deferredDesktopReloadRef is not cleared when a new URL is loaded, which causes an extra reload after toggling mid-load.
bugs.userImpact: Latent. Re-enabling platform desktop mode would break loads again, and toggling Desktop Site while a page loads can reload twice.

bugs.description: goHome calls clearHistory and blanks the WebView, making Home destructive. Back on Home returns false (useBrowserHardwareBack.ts:20-23), so there is no way back to the page.
bugs.userImpact: Tapping Home by accident loses the page and its history, unlike Chrome.

bugs.description: This is the only eslint error in scope (react-hooks/set-state-in-effect). The draft/focus state is reset in an effect keyed on activeTabId, which causes cascading renders on every tab switch.
bugs.userImpact: Minor extra renders; not user-visible.

overEngineering.description:
Controlling one WebView takes 8 mutable refs: navigationEpoch, loadStartEpoch, loadStartUrl, chromeNavRef, nativeCanGoBack/Forward, suppressNextAbortError, webViewInstanceGeneration. Plus stale-event heuristics (isStaleEvent, isStaleMainFrameError with 5 branches) and 975 lines of handlers.
- webViewInstanceGenerationRef starts at 1 and never increments, so every 'generation' guard is just a mounted flag.
- withOwningTabGuard's post-call check does nothing (useBrowserEngineEvents.ts:106-119).
- chromeNavRef is pushed but never used for navigation.
- Every `if (!tabId)` global-store branch is unreachable because tabId is always set.

6 refs, 2 state variables and 5 interacting effects (transition, deferred-after-load, activate-reconcile, UA-commit-reload, source pairing) plus a cacheMode swap, all to change a userAgent and reload. A simpler design (UA applied, then one reload in a single effect, or remounting the tab's WebView with a key) would remove the latent mid-load UA bug.

Toolbar → useBrowserNavigation → active-tab-navigation.service (resolveLiveController + generation re-check) → tabControllerRegistry → controller.goBack → browser-engine.service goBackWebView → webView.goBack(). On top of that, useBrowserEngine builds a registry facade with a no-op controller and a useSyncExternalStore version counter that re-renders all chrome on every loadUrl.

overEngineering.area: Duplicated chrome mirror in the store
overEngineering.description: Active-tab fields (currentUrl, isLoading, progress, error, canGoBack, desktopMode...) are stored twice, in tabs[] and at the top level. They are kept in sync by patchTab/updateTab/chromeFromTab/syncChromeFromActiveTab, with two parallel mutation APIs: the global setLoading/setError/applyNavigationState and updateTab. Placeholder fields (downloads, history, bookmarks as never[], readerMode, incognito:false) add noise.

tabs/tab-persistence.service.ts (the real tab restore) coexists with session/session-persistence.service.ts: a legacy single-URL session with lastSuccessfulUrl, a scroll LRU, dual MMKV plus async adapter writes, mmkv-vs-full write modes and a flush on background. Its only live uses are scroll restore and a one-time migration; the async restore path is dead. browserSyncService writes it on every navigation, success, error and SPA hop.

browser-navigation-policy.ts, external-navigation.service.ts, intent-navigation.service.ts, popup-navigation.service.ts, services/navigation.service.ts and utils/url.ts overlap. There are two 'should load in browser' predicates (classifyBrowserNavigation vs navigationService.shouldHandleInBrowser, both checked in onShouldStartLoadWithRequest), isBrowserHomeUrl is duplicated, and the RN originWhitelist workaround exists to feed the classifier.

Nearly every handler emits logBrowserNav/Load/Session/Desktop/WebView calls with dozens of documentary fields (cookieAuthority, androidSharedCookiesPropIsNoop, webview_mount_shared_cookie_jar...). There is a phase6aSessionContinuityPolicy object used only for logs, and @internal 'contract' exports that exist for scripts/verify-*.ts: browserWebViewConfigurationContract, browserFailureContract, browserRuntimeDiagnosticsContract, BROWSER_WEBVIEW_INCOGNITO_PROP_FORBIDDEN, BROWSER_WEBVIEW_PLATFORM. 25 browser/session verify scripts and 18 docs/browser/*.md phase documents describe it.

The BrowserFailure → BrowserErrorState mapping has 11 categories and 11 codes, with CATEGORY_COPY and ERROR_COPY tables where every title and message is the same string. The UI ignores them and uses i18n keys. Five-way stale-error correlation heuristics feed a single overlay.

overEngineering.area: Extensibility registries for tiny feature sets
overEngineering.description: browserActionRegistry for 4 long-press actions (one permanently disabled). toolbar-config with 5 disabled placeholder items (downloads/tabs/menu/ai/settings). chrome-actions constants that are never rendered. Leading/trailing 'future slot' props on the header.

deadCode: src/browser/components/BrowserHome/BrowserHomeTabs.tsx (never rendered)
src/browser/components/BrowserHome/BrowserBookmarkGrid.tsx and BookmarkSiteCard.tsx (grid never rendered; the card is only used by the grid)
src/browser/components/BrowserHome/BrowserHistorySection.tsx and BrowserHomeHistoryRow.tsx (section never rendered; the row is only used by the section)
src/browser/components/BrowserHeader/BrowserBookmarkControls.tsx and BrowserLabeledAction.tsx (controls never rendered; the labeled action is only used by the controls)
src/browser/components/QuickAccess/QuickAccessSection.tsx (only used by the hidden legacy src/screens/home route, together with src/browser/hooks/useQuickAccessHandoff.ts)
src/browser/constants/chrome-actions.ts (BROWSER_CHROME_ACTIONS / getBrowserChromeActions only re-exported, never used)
src/browser/navigation/intent-native-launcher.ts (openAndroidIntentUri / canOpenAndroidIntentUri never called; intents are always contained)
src/browser/session/desktop-mode.service.ts: readInitialDesktopState, applyPlatformDesktopRecommendation, canApplyPlatformDesktop, readGlobalDesktopDefault (only resolveEffectiveDesktopMode is used)
src/browser/hooks/useTabScopedBrowserEngine.ts:207-224 platform auto-desktop branch (all platform adapters return prefersDesktopWebView:false)
src/browser/hooks/useBrowserEngineEvents.ts: all `if (!tabId)` global-store branches, and the leftover-blank recovery at :333-347 (unreachable)
src/browser/hooks/useBrowserSessionContinuity.ts:55-83 async restore (always calls the no-op loadUrl)
src/browser/session/session-continuity-policy.ts (phase6aSessionContinuityPolicy used only for log fields)
src/browser/actions/builtins/open-in-new-tab.action.ts (enabled:false, filtered out by BrowserLinkActionSheet)

capabilityGaps: No handoff of web-triggered file downloads: Content-Disposition, non-HTML responses and <a download> go to RN WebView's built-in DownloadListener (RNCWebViewManagerImpl.kt:94), which uses Android DownloadManager into public Downloads, bypassing the VidoraX download pipeline and library. blob: navigations are blocked outright.
No fullscreen HTML5 video (allowsFullscreenVideo not set), and autoplay is likely blocked (mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction=true). Both are poor fits for a video-centric browser.
Popups and target=_blank never open tabs, and long-press 'Open in New Tab' is disabled, so multi-tab browsing is only possible via the tab switcher's New Tab button.

Only 2 live WebViews (MAX_MOUNTED_WEBVIEWS=2). Switching to a third tab destroys the least-recently-used WebView, which loses back history, scroll/feed position and playing video, and forces a reload.
Home is destructive (clearHistory). There is no 'back to page' from the start page, and Android Back on Home triggers app exit.
The JS media observer runs only in the main frame and only after onPageFinished, so embedded iframe players on arbitrary sites and first-load manifests depend solely on native URL heuristics.

Google/Apple sign-in and other OAuth flows: the mobile UA is the stock WebView UA with 'wv' (Google rejects embedded WebViews), and popup-based flows are broken by same-tab popup loading. Sites that require them (e.g. TikTok 'Continue with Google') will not log in.

No cookie flush on app background (RNCWebView.onHostPause is empty and nothing calls CookieManager.flush). A login made seconds before the process is killed may not persist. Instagram/TikTok sessions otherwise persist via the shared CookieManager.
No per-site permissions, find-in-page, text zoom, clear-browsing-data or incognito tab. The incognito prop is deliberately forbidden, so private browsing is impossible.
History does not record SPA navigations (most Instagram/TikTok pages), so the 'recently visited' reel cannot be found again.
Unknown app schemes (whatsapp:, tg:) are launched by RN's Linking fallback without user confirmation, while geo:/maps: links are silently blocked.
audits.crossSubsystemCoupling:
Coupling is tight and mostly two-way.

Media detection (src/media-detection):
- BrowserWebView imports useMediaDetectionBridge and registerNativeObservationScope.
- useBrowserEngineEvents calls mediaDetectionEngine.observeUrl.
- useBrowserSessionContinuity calls mediaDetectionEngine.setAppActive.
- BrowserScreen mounts MediaDetectionHost and uses isSameDocumentUrl from media-detection/utils.
- useTabScopedBrowserEngine uses describePlatformPage from media-detection/platform.
- The browser store's closeTab cleanup (stores/browserStore/actions.ts:97-132) directly clears socialPageContextStore, generalPageMediaContextStore, mediaDetectionEngine, verification-session and social-source refresh state.
- native-network.contract.ts depends on the viewTag scope that BrowserWebView registers.

Media actions (src/browser/media-actions):
- The store calls browserMediaActionService.setActiveTab/suspendTab/clearTab on every tab operation and at store creation (stores/browserStore/index.ts:14).

Downloads/quality (src/screens/downloads/quality):
- BrowserScreen registers loadUrl into browser-load-bridge and consumes useQualitySelectionContext.
- useQualitySelection, QualitySelectionProvider and usePendingMediaResolution push URLs back via pendingNavigationService.

Other screens:
- Bookmarks and History screens use pendingNavigationService.set with activeTabId from useBrowserStore.
- The hidden Home screen uses useQuickAccessHandoff and QuickAccessGrid.
- History/bookmarks/recent-searches stores feed suggestions, and browserSyncService writes history.

Navigation:
- use-tab-exit-back-handler conflicts with useBrowserHardwareBack.

Native:
- The postinstall patch hard-codes the com.anonymous.vidorax.mediadetection.MediaNetworkBridge class name (reflection), and 49 verify scripts import browser internals.

What replacing the engine would break:
- Any rewrite must preserve: the store API (tabs, activeTabId, updateTab, switchTab/closeTab plus the cleanup hooks), pendingNavigationService (or an equivalent 'open URL in browser' API), the native observation scope binding (tabId/epoch/pageUrl per viewTag) and the WebView onMessage/injected-script contract used by media detection.
- The verify scripts would break but are disposable.
audits.recommendations:
Target design, in order of payoff.

1) Fix the three flow-breaking bugs now, independent of any rewrite.
- (a) Make useTabExitBackHandler defer to the browser. Either have it return false unless the active tab is on Home with no history, or call goBackForTab inside it; or register one combined handler.
- (b) Make loadUrl imperative. Keep sourceUri only as the initial URL, and navigate with webViewRef.current.injectJavaScript(`location.assign(url)`), or better, a small native `loadUrl` command via a patch (RN WebView exposes none on Android). Alternatively bump a `sourceKey` counter so every call yields a new source object `{uri, headers:{'X-Nav':n}}`. Remove the same-document early return for explicit user actions.
- (c) Retry must clear the error and call webView.reload(), or run the fixed loadUrl.

2) Replace useTabScopedBrowserEngine + useBrowserEngineEvents + the desktop state machine with one `useTabWebView(tabId)` hook, about 300 lines.
- State lives only on the tab record: url, title, loading, progress, canGoBack, canGoForward, error, desktopMode.
- Handlers:
  - onLoadStart sets loading=true (skip when url === 'about:blank').
  - onLoadProgress sets progress.
  - onLoadEnd / onNavigationStateChange write url/title/canGoBack/canGoForward and loading=false.
  - onError sets an error only when isTopFrame and the URL matches the current navigation.
- Use one monotonic navigation id, only to drop errors from superseded loads.
- Desktop Site: store desktopMode on the tab, pass userAgent, and on toggle call reload() in a single effect after the prop commits. Or give the WebView `key={tabId+desktopMode}`, which is acceptable because cookies are shared.
- Drop the registry facade. Keep a plain `Map<tabId, WebView ref + commands>` and have chrome call `browserCommands.back(activeTabId)`.
- Remove the duplicated chrome mirror from the store; derive the active tab with a selector.

3) Home: do not blank or clear history. Render the Home view over the WebView and keep the page loaded underneath (like Chrome's NTP overlay). Then Back from Home returns to the page, and the about:blank history bug disappears.

4) WebView props:
- allowsFullscreenVideo=true (wire orientation);
- mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction=false;
- injectedJavaScriptForMainFrameOnly=false for the media observer (keep chrome UI messages main-frame only by checking window===top inside the script);
- consider mixedContentMode='compatibility';
- keep thirdPartyCookiesEnabled / no incognito / stock mobile UA.
- Add a CookieManager.flush() call on AppState background (tiny native module or patch).
- Implement onOpenWindow as 'open in new tab', and wire long-press 'Open in new tab'.

5) Downloads: intercept the WebView DownloadListener. Patch RNCWebViewManagerImpl to emit an onFileDownload-style event with url, contentDisposition, mimetype, userAgent and cookies, and route it into the VidoraX download pipeline instead of DownloadManager.

6) Native hook:
- Convert apply-webview-media-hook.js to a committed patch-package diff that fails the build on mismatch.
- Call MediaNetworkBridge directly (the app module can register a static callback into RNCWebViewClient) instead of reflection.
- Remove @Synchronized; do the cheap host/extension prefilter lock-free and hand candidates to the existing single-thread executor.
- Precompile every Regex.
- Keep the custom-scheme timeout containment.
- For early JS hooks, add document-start injection with WebViewCompat.addDocumentStartJavaScript (a native patch) so fetch/XHR/MSE hooks install before page scripts.

7) Persistence: keep tab-persistence.service (plus the sanitizer) as the only session store. Move the scroll LRU into it or drop scroll restore; delete session-persistence.service, browserSyncService, useBrowserSessionContinuity's async restore, and the legacy migration after one release.

8) Keep and consolidate policy into two files. navigation-policy.ts: the classifier plus originWhitelist plus the intent resolver and loop guard. url.ts: omnibox classification. Decide explicitly whether unknown app schemes prompt the user; show a confirm sheet instead of RN's silent Linking.openURL.

9) Delete: the dead components (BrowserHomeTabs, BrowserBookmarkGrid, BookmarkSiteCard, BrowserHistorySection, BrowserHomeHistoryRow, BrowserBookmarkControls, BrowserLabeledAction), chrome-actions, intent-native-launcher, unused desktop-mode helpers, toolbar placeholders, the action registry (inline the 3 actions), @internal verify contracts, diagnostics beyond a single DEV logger, the 25 browser verify scripts and docs/browser phase docs. Replace them with a handful of Jest unit tests for url.ts, navigation-policy, intent-uri-resolver, tab-operations and tab-persistence.

10) Raise MAX_MOUNTED_WEBVIEWS to 3–4 with memory-pressure eviction (onTrimMemory / onRenderProcessGone), and persist per-tab scroll so evicted tabs restore closer to where the user was.
