audits.purpose:
This subsystem turns a selected media URL into a saved file and handles that file afterwards. It covers:
- **Analysis:** probing the URL on-device and listing HLS variants (`src/downloads/analyze`).
- **Quality options:** turning analysis results into options and a create payload (`src/downloads/quality`).
- **HLS downloads:** a JavaScript HLS transfer worker that parses playlists, downloads segments one at a time, concatenates them and validates the result (`engine/hls`).
- **Finished files:** naming, MIME and extension, open/share, copying to MediaStore, and delete (`src/downloads/completed-file` plus the Kotlin FileActions and MediaExport modules).
- **Notifications:** per-download progress and result notifications (`src/downloads/notifications` plus a Kotlin module).
- **Settings:** Wi-Fi-only, auto-resume, concurrency and notification preferences (`src/downloads/settings`).

HLS output is a raw byte concatenation: MPEG-TS segments become `.ts`, and fMP4 becomes init segment plus fragments saved as `.mp4`. Nothing is remuxed. AES-128, SAMPLE-AES, byte-range, live and DASH streams are all refused, and separate audio renditions are silently dropped. Finished files live only in the app sandbox (`filesDir/VidoraXDownloads/{downloadId}/`) until the user taps "Save to device", which copies them into MediaStore.
audits.architecture:
ANALYZE
- `analyze/analyze-url.ts:186` `analyzeMediaUrl` calls `probe.ts:109` `inspectSource` (HEAD, falling back to a GET with Range 0-0).
- If `isPlaylistOrStreamUrl` (`engine/resource-guard.ts:46`, which also matches `.mpd`) or the MIME looks like HLS, it runs `analyzeHls` (`analyze-url.ts:67`). That calls `engine/hls/fetch-playlist.ts:36` then `playlist.ts:439` `parseHlsPlaylist`.
- For a master playlist, each variant becomes a `MediaAnalysisVariant` whose `sourceUrl` is the variant's media playlist URL (`analyze-url.ts:94-140`). `estimatedFileSize` is always null because duration is passed as null (line 113-116).
- The browser fast path, `analyze-from-verification.ts:47`, only ever emits PROGRESSIVE or AUDIO.

QUALITY
- `quality/normalize.ts` sorts options (`sortQualityOptions`, line 370) and picks the highest as default.
- `quality/to-create-input.ts:157` builds the create payload. For an HLS container the file name ends in `.ts` (line 72-75). `fileSize` falls back to 0 (line 191). Thumbnails fall back to a google.com favicon URL (line 85-98).
- `download-metadata.ts:86` produces the name stem.

ENGINE HLS
- `engine/manager.ts:2886` creates `HlsTransferWorker` when `shouldUseHlsTransfer` (`resource-guard.ts:68`) is true.
- `worker.ts:172` `run()`:
  - disk precheck (189);
  - workspace-reuse decision (279);
  - local record upsert (331);
  - `resolveMediaPlaylist` (610): fetch master, `selectHlsVariant` (667), fetch child;
  - `ensureOutputFileName` (91 and 380);
  - `resolveDestinationFile` (`file-paths.ts:34`);
  - `downloadHlsSegments` (`segment-transfer.ts:236`): sequential `File.downloadFileAsync` per segment into `.hls/segment-000123`, with retry and auth retry;
  - `assembleHlsOutput` (414): synchronous 256 KB `readBytes`/`writeBytes` loop into `.hls/assemble.tmp`;
  - `copyHlsAssembledFile` (457): a second synchronous full copy to the final path;
  - `complete()` (867): `validateFinalDownloadFile` (`finalize-download.ts:42`) uses `verifyDownloadedMediaContent` (`media-validation.ts:12`), `sniffMediaSignature` and `classifyMp4Container`. It then runs `cleanupHlsWorkspace`, `applyCompletedFileIdentity` (`completed-file/apply-identity.ts:49`, rename via `File.move`), upserts the record and emits a `completed` event carrying `mimeType`/`container`.
- State owners:
  - `LocalDownloadRecord.hlsTransfer` is persisted in AsyncStorage (`engine/persistence.ts`).
  - Segment files on disk are the real resume truth: reuse is decided purely by file existence and size.

COMPLETED-FILE
- Naming and MIME are pure functions: `sanitize.ts`, `extension.ts` (evidence priority), `naming.ts`, `descriptor.ts`.
- Runtime services, all called by downloadId:
  - `action-service.ts`: play, open and share. It resolves `file.contentUri` (Expo `FileSystemFileProvider`, `files-path` ".") and calls `VidoraFileActionsModule.kt`.
  - `export/export-service.ts` saves to the device. It uses `destination.ts` (collection mapping), `public-name.ts`, `receipt-store.ts` (MMKV) and `VidoraMediaExportModule.kt`.
  - `delete/delete-service.ts` handles delete.
- `operation-lock.ts` serializes export and delete per id.
- `phase7c.ts` and `index.ts` are pure barrels that exist for the Node verify scripts.

NOTIFICATIONS
- `ensure-bridge.ts:67` subscribes to engine events, progress and queue changes.
  - `presentFromStore` calls `service.ts:283` `presentLifecycle`, which calls `native-download-notifications.ts`, which calls `VidoraDownloadNotificationsModule.kt`. If the native module is missing it falls back to expo-notifications.
  - Terminal notifications go through `notifyCompleted`/`notifyFailed`, gated by an MMKV dedupe store (`dedupe.ts`).
- `FgsSummaryPublisher` (`fgs-summary.ts`) pushes summaries to `execution/android-controller.ts`, which expects `NativeModules.VidoraXDownloadForeground`. That module does not exist.
- Deep link: the PendingIntent uses `vidorax://downloads/{id}`; `deep-link.ts` handles expo-notifications taps.

SETTINGS
- `settings/policy.ts` treats the Zustand settings store as authoritative.
- `persist.ts` mirrors it to individual MMKV keys plus a versioned JSON envelope.
- Listeners notify the engine.

NATIVE
- Four `ReactContextBaseJavaModule`s are registered manually in `MainApplication.kt:25-30`: VidoraFileActions, VidoraMediaExport, VidoraDownloadNotifications and VidoraIntentLauncher (the last is used by `browser/navigation/intent-native-launcher.ts`).
- `AndroidManifest.xml` declares INTERNET, POST_NOTIFICATIONS, SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, VIBRATE and READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdk 32), plus a `<queries>` block for VIEW/SEND of video, audio and `*/*`.
- There is no FOREGROUND_SERVICE permission and no `<service>` element; the merged debug manifest confirms this.
audits.endToEndTrace:
Main flow: user picks an HLS quality in the sheet, then downloads, plays, opens, shares and saves.

1. `useQualitySelection` calls `analyzeMediaUrl` (`analyze-url.ts:186`). The HEAD probe (`probe.ts:130`) runs, `looksLikeHls` is true (228-234), and `analyzeHls` calls `fetchAndParseHlsPlaylist` (`fetch-playlist.ts:36`).
   - `parseHlsPlaylist` (`playlist.ts:439`) runs `rejectUnsupportedConstructs` (211) first. Any `#EXT-X-KEY METHOD=AES-128` or `#EXT-X-SESSION-KEY` anywhere, even in the master, fails the whole analysis with UNSUPPORTED_HLS_ENCRYPTION.
   - `parseMasterPlaylist` (279) reads only `#EXT-X-STREAM-INF`. `#EXT-X-MEDIA TYPE=AUDIO` groups are ignored; the whole repo only mentions them in `media-detection/parsers/hls.parser.ts:68`.
   - FRAGILE: a `.mpd` URL also matches `isPlaylistOrStreamUrl` (`resource-guard.ts:46-61`). It goes down the HLS path, fails `isPlausibleHlsManifestPrefix` because it starts with `<?xml`, and is reported as UNSUPPORTED_STREAM.
2. Each variant option carries the variant media-playlist URL (`analyze-url.ts:103`). `toCreateDownloadInput` (`to-create-input.ts:157`) sets `fileName` to "Title.ts" and `fileSize` to 0.
3. `manager.ts:2886` routes to `HlsTransferWorker` because `streamType` is HLS. Its `run` is wrapped in `void (async () => { try { await worker.run } finally {...} })()` (`manager.ts:2937-2958`), which has NO catch.
   - BREAKS: `worker.ts:189` `assertEnoughDiskSpace` throws outside the worker's try. That becomes an unhandled rejection, and no FAILED state or event is ever emitted.
4. `worker.ts:279-291` decides workspace reuse from `existing.sourceUrl` and `completedSegments > 0` only; there is no playlist fingerprint.
5. `resolveMediaPlaylist` (610): because the source is already a media playlist, it returns directly.
   - If a master URL is enqueued (retry or refresh paths), `selectHlsVariant(variants, sourceUrl)` (667) passes the master URL as `preferredUri`. That never matches a variant, so the worker always takes the highest BANDWIDTH regardless of codec.
6. `downloadHlsSegments` (`segment-transfer.ts:299-346`) runs one segment at a time.
   - BREAKS on resume: `isReusableHlsFile` (`paths.ts:43-54`) accepts any file with 0 < size <= 32 MB.
   - `downloadToFile` streams directly into the final segment path. Expo `FileSystemDownload.kt` writes straight into `FileOutputStream(destination)`, and the catch at `segment-transfer.ts:139-152` never deletes the partial file.
   - So a pause, network-policy hold, timeout abort or app kill mid-segment leaves a truncated segment. The next attempt treats it as complete, which corrupts the output silently.
7. `assembleHlsOutput` (414-449) is a synchronous JSI loop on the JS thread. For a 1 GB VOD that is about 4,000 256 KB round-trips.
   - `copyHlsAssembledFile` (457-516) then does the same again to the final path.
   - The JS thread stays blocked through both copies. Pause and cancel taps, progress updates and the WebView bridge freeze, and peak disk use is about 3x the video size.
8. `complete()` (`worker.ts:897`) calls `validateFinalDownloadFile`, then `verifyDownloadedMediaContent` (`media-validation.ts:41-45`, `requireStandaloneMp4: true`).
   - TS passes on the 0x47 sync byte (`media-signature.ts:143`).
   - BREAKS for fMP4/CMAF whose media segments start with `styp`: `mp4-box-classify.ts:159` returns MEDIA_FRAGMENT whenever `types.has('styp')`, before the FRAGMENTED_COMPLETE check. The file is deleted (`worker.ts:905-918`) and FINAL_FILE_INVALID is recorded.
   - The workspace is kept, so every retry re-assembles and fails again.
9. `applyCompletedFileIdentity` (`apply-identity.ts:49`) renames to the stem plus the evidence extension. `evidence.containerHint` is 'mp4' or 'ts' (`worker.ts:944`).
   - Title sanitizing (`download-metadata.ts:45`, `sanitize.ts:55`, both `[^\w.\- ]`) strips all non-ASCII. CJK, Arabic or emoji titles become `VidoraX_Video_YYYYMMDD_HHMM.ts`.
10. The record is upserted as complete, the `completed` event is emitted, and `bind-engine-to-store.ts:138` stores `mimeType`/`container`.
11. Notifications: `ensure-bridge.ts:179` fires on each progress tick, then `presentFromStore`, then `service.ts:311-327`.
    - For HLS, `transfer.totalBytes` is always null (`segment-transfer.ts:288`) and `item.fileSize` is 0, so the notification bar stays indeterminate for the whole download even though the in-app UI shows a segment-ratio percentage.
    - The first tick can pop the POST_NOTIFICATIONS system dialog (`service.ts:505-509`).
    - On completion, `notifyCompleted` is gated by `canEmitTerminalNotification` (`dedupe.ts:29`) with a 7-day TTL per downloadId.
12. Background: `ensure-bridge.ts:81` `getBackgroundExecutionController`. `android-controller.ts:34-51` finds no `VidoraXDownloadForeground` module and falls back to a no-op.
    - There is no FGS permission or service in the manifest. If the user leaves the app during a long HLS job, the process gets cached and frozen, and the download stalls or dies.
13. Play: `action-service.ts:274` checks the file and returns the player route.
14. Open with: `action-service.ts:292` gets `file.contentUri` (`JavaFile.kt:48`, `${packageName}.FileSystemFileProvider`), then `VidoraFileActionsModule.kt:53`.
    - For `.ts` the MIME is video/mp2t. `hasCompatibleViewHandler` (167) finds no handler on many stock devices (Google Photos, OEM players), so the user gets NO_COMPATIBLE_APP.
15. Share: `VidoraFileActionsModule.kt:77`. `grantReadToSendTargets` (205-219) grants a persistent read permission to EVERY app that can receive ACTION_SEND.
16. Save to device: `export-service.ts:63`, then `destination.ts:42-54`. TS files go to `Download/VidoraX` (not Movies, so they never show in the Gallery); MP4 goes to `Movies/VidoraX`. `VidoraMediaExportModule.kt:163-234` does the MediaStore IS_PENDING insert, a 64 KB copy, a byte-count check and publish. That part is correct. It is a copy, so storage doubles.
17. Delete: `delete-service.ts:78` works only for COMPLETED (`plan.ts:49`). It deletes the private folder and the catalog row; the MediaStore copy is intentionally kept.
audits.verdictRationale:
Some pieces are worth keeping:
- The pure HLS playlist parser and bounded fetcher.
- The media-signature sniffing that rejects HTML/JSON error pages.
- The small Kotlin modules for MediaStore export, content:// open/share and notifications. They follow correct Android 10–16 patterns.

The transfer, format and file pipeline does not meet the owner's goals and has real runtime defects:
- Truncated segments are reused on resume and silently corrupt the output.
- Demuxed HLS audio is dropped, producing silent videos.
- CMAF fMP4 is rejected after a full download.
- Two full synchronous copies on the JS thread freeze the app and need about 3x disk.
- There is no foreground service, so long downloads die in the background.
- There is no AES-128, DASH or muxing at all, so "any format from any site" is impossible by design.

The completed-file, notifications and settings layers mostly work, but they are 3–5x bigger than needed and full of verifier-only exports and reconcile logic that can never do anything.

Recommendation: rewrite the format and transfer core natively on Media3, which expo-video already bundles, and keep or simplify the parser, the Kotlin export/open/share modules and the pure naming helpers.

keepWorthy.why: Pure, testable HLS parser. It handles attribute lists with quoted commas, BOM, relative URL resolution with an SSRF guard (resolveSafeHlsUrl), ENDLIST/TARGETDURATION structure checks, and RESOLUTION/FRAME-RATE/BANDWIDTH validation. It is a good base to extend with EXT-X-MEDIA, EXT-X-KEY (AES-128 IV/URI), BYTERANGE and multiple EXT-X-MAP instead of rejecting them.

Bounded, timeout-aware manifest fetch. It validates redirects manually with per-hop headers, enforces a size limit and rejects HTML/JSON responses. Correct and reusable for analysis and for any native handoff.

Rejects HTML and JSON error pages disguised as media and recognizes MP4, MOV, WebM, AVI, WMV, TS and MP3 signatures. Worth keeping for progressive downloads. The one rule that needs relaxing is `styp` → MEDIA_FRAGMENT in mp4-box-classify.ts:159, which wrongly rejects assembled CMAF files.

Correct scoped-storage export for API 29+: MediaStore insert with RELATIVE_PATH and IS_PENDING=1, stream copy on an IO executor, byte-count verification, publish, and cleanup on failure. No storage permission needed. Includes a SAF fallback for API 24–28 and managed-path canonicalization. Keep it and add DURATION/WIDTH/HEIGHT/DATE_TAKEN metadata plus an optional move mode.

Uses the correct Android 11+ pattern for open and share: ACTION_VIEW/ACTION_SEND with ClipData and FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION, an authority allowlist, and a handler check before startActivity. Keep it, but delete the grantReadToSendTargets loop (lines 205-219).

Simple and correct channel creation, FLAG_IMMUTABLE PendingIntent to the vidorax://downloads/{id} deep link, determinate/indeterminate progress, and a safe no-op when the permission is denied. A good seed for a service-owned notification with pause/cancel actions.
Safe intent:// handoff that strips component and selector and blocks file/content/javascript schemes. Used by browser/navigation/intent-native-launcher.ts. Small and correct.
Pure, easy-to-read mapping from MIME/extension to a MediaStore collection and relative path. Directly reusable.

Sensible priority order for container, extension and MIME: structural signature, then verified MIME, then hint, then response MIME, then file extension, then URL. It never lets playlist extensions become final extensions. Keep a trimmed version.
Tiny, correct per-id mutex that stops export and delete from racing on the same file.
Bounded HEAD probe with a Range 0-0 GET fallback when HEAD is rejected, and validation of the final URL after redirects. Reusable for classifying progressive sources.
Pure status-to-presentation mapping with a throttle policy. Small and testable; it survives any rewrite of the notification layer.
Types only. It is the shared contract for more than 10 media-detection files; keep as-is.

bugs.description: Resumed HLS downloads reuse truncated segments. isReusableHlsFile (paths.ts:43-54) accepts any existing segment file with 0 < size <= 32 MB as complete. downloadToFile writes straight into the final segment path: expo FileSystemDownload.kt streams into FileOutputStream(destination), and the library's own docs (File.ts:45-48) warn that partial files remain on failure. The catch block at lines 139-152 never deletes that partial file. Any pause (worker.ts:722), Wi-Fi-only hold (746), stall-watchdog abort, network drop or app kill mid-segment leaves a truncated segment-NNNNNN that the next attempt treats as done.
bugs.userImpact: The finished video has glitches, green frames, audio dropouts or broken timestamps with no error shown. Final validation only sniffs the first 256 KB, so the corrupted file is marked COMPLETED.

bugs.description: parseMasterPlaylist only reads #EXT-X-STREAM-INF and ignores #EXT-X-MEDIA TYPE=AUDIO/SUBTITLES renditions (the AUDIO="group" attribute). The worker downloads only the video variant's media playlist and there is no muxing step. Audio-only renditions are never offered in analysis either (analyze-url.ts:94-140).
bugs.userImpact: Videos from hosts that use separate audio renditions (common for modern CDN/CMAF packaging, e.g. Vimeo and X/Twitter) download without sound. The user only finds out on playback.

bugs.description: classifyMp4Container returns MEDIA_FRAGMENT whenever any top-level `styp` box is present, and this check runs before the FRAGMENTED_COMPLETE check. verifyDownloadedMediaContent calls it with requireStandaloneMp4: true (media-validation.ts:44). An assembled CMAF/fMP4 HLS file is ftyp+moov+styp+moof+mdat..., so it is rejected. worker.ts:904-919 then deletes the output and records FINAL_FILE_INVALID, but the segment workspace is kept.
bugs.userImpact: fMP4 HLS streams whose segments start with `styp` fail only after the entire video has downloaded. Every retry re-assembles the same bytes and fails the same way.

bugs.description: Both assembleHlsOutput (414-449) and copyHlsAssembledFile (457-516) are fully synchronous loops of 256 KB FileHandle.readBytes/writeBytes JSI calls on the JS thread, and they run back to back (worker.ts:495-515). Every chunk crosses the JSI boundary. Peak disk use is segments + assemble.tmp + final, about 3x the video size. The disk precheck passes 0 bytes for HLS (worker.ts:188-191; fileSize is 0 per to-create-input.ts:191). The copy is pointless because both paths are on the same volume and File.move exists (used in apply-identity.ts:98).
bugs.userImpact: The app freezes for seconds or minutes at the end of a large HLS download: pause, cancel, the browser and progress all stop responding. On near-full devices the download fails at the very end with a storage error after hundreds of MB were transferred.

bugs.description: Background protection looks for NativeModules.VidoraXDownloadForeground. No such Kotlin module exists in android/app/src. Neither the source manifest nor the merged manifest (build/intermediates/merged_manifest/debug) declares FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC or any VidoraX <service>. The controller silently falls back to no-op. notifications/service.ts:3 and fgs-summary.ts describe a 'native VidoraXDownloadService' that does not exist.
bugs.userImpact: Downloads only progress while the app is in the foreground. Leaving the app during a long HLS or large progressive download lets Android freeze or kill the JS runtime and OkHttp calls, so downloads stall or die.

bugs.description: assertEnoughDiskSpace runs before the try block and before this.active is set. manager.ts:2937-2941 wraps worker.run in try/finally with no catch. An INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE throw therefore becomes an unhandled promise rejection: fail() never runs, and no FAILED record, backend sync or event is produced.
bugs.userImpact: On low storage the download gets stuck at 'Preparing'/QUEUED with no error message and no retry prompt.

bugs.description: selectHlsVariant(first.playlist.variants, sourceUrl) passes the master URL as preferredUri, which can never equal a variant URL. It always falls through to the highest BANDWIDTH (playlist.ts:520) and ignores CODECS (hvc1/dvh1/av01) and the user's selected quality. This path is used whenever a master URL is enqueued: retry, social refresh, or direct handoff.
bugs.userImpact: The downloaded quality can differ from what the user chose, and may be an HEVC/Dolby Vision/AV1 rendition the device or Gallery cannot decode.

bugs.description: isPlaylistOrStreamUrl treats .mpd (DASH) like .m3u8. analyze-url.ts:228-234 sends DASH manifests into analyzeHls, and shouldUseHlsTransfer (68-77) routes them to HlsTransferWorker. Both fail with INVALID_HLS_PLAYLIST, which isUnrecoverableHlsCode (segment-retry.ts:28-40) treats as a reason to wipe the workspace. EnqueueInput.streamType includes 'DASH' (engine/types.ts:198) but nothing handles it.
bugs.userImpact: DASH sources show a generic 'unsupported stream' or 'invalid playlist' error instead of a clear 'DASH not supported', and they can never be downloaded.

bugs.description: MPEG-TS HLS is saved as raw concatenated .ts (video/mp2t) with no remux. #EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY is ignored, so timestamp resets from ad or period boundaries are concatenated as-is. destination.ts:42-54 sends TS exports to Download/VidoraX rather than Movies. VidoraFileActionsModule.kt:62 rejects Open when no app handles video/mp2t.
bugs.userImpact: HLS downloads do not appear in the Gallery after 'Save to device'. 'Open with' fails on many stock phones. Duration and seeking are wrong for streams with discontinuities.

bugs.description: grantReadToSendTargets calls Context.grantUriPermission for every package that can handle ACTION_SEND for the MIME, before the user picks a target. These grants are not tied to an activity and are never revoked. ClipData + FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION on the intent already covers the chosen target.
bugs.userImpact: Privacy leak: every installed share-capable app (messengers, social apps and so on) keeps read access to the downloaded video's content URI after a share, even apps the user never chose.

bugs.description: placeholderThumbnail falls back to https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=<host>. That URL is stored as the download's thumbnailUrl and loaded every time the library renders. There is no local thumbnail extraction anywhere (no MediaMetadataRetriever or expo-video-thumbnails). Real thumbnails are remote, often signed, IG/TikTok CDN URLs that expire.
bugs.userImpact: The library leaks the domains of downloaded sites to Google, and thumbnails break after CDN URLs expire, leaving an unorganized grid of favicons or blanks.

bugs.description: indeterminate is forced whenever totalBytes is unknown. For HLS, segment-transfer.ts:288 always reports totalBytes null and the create payload's fileSize is 0, so ensure-bridge.ts:57-62 never supplies a total. The engine does compute a real segment-ratio percentage (worker.ts:441-474), but the notification ignores it.
bugs.userImpact: HLS download notifications show an endless spinner with no percentage, while the in-app list shows real progress.

bugs.description: Terminal notifications are deduped by downloadId + event with a 7-day TTL (DEFAULT_TTL_MS, line 11), and emitTerminal checks this (service.ts:418). Manual retry keeps the same downloadId.
bugs.userImpact: If a user retries a failed download and it fails again, or succeeds after an earlier success record, within 7 days, no notification appears.

bugs.description: maybeRequestPermissionOnce runs from ensurePresentationAllowed on the first progress tick, not from a user gesture. It writes the 'prompted' MMKV flag before requesting (line 576). If the app is backgrounded or the request fails, the flag is still burned.
bugs.userImpact: A system permission dialog appears mid-download without context. If it was missed, notifications never get requested again unless the user finds the Settings toggle.

bugs.description: presentLifecycle checks its throttle, then awaits ensurePresentationAllowed (a native permission query) and publishActive. It never re-checks whether a terminal notification was posted in the meantime. Both paths use the same Android notification id (notification-id.ts:25). A progress tick that starts just before notifyCompleted/notifyFailed can land after it. (Plausible race; not reproduced.)
bugs.userImpact: Occasionally a finished download leaves a stuck, ongoing 'Downloading 99%' notification instead of 'Download complete'.

bugs.description: sanitizeFileBase (and sanitizeCompletedFileName, sanitize.ts:55) removes every character outside [A-Za-z0-9_.- ], because JS \w has no u flag, so all non-Latin scripts and emoji are stripped. Line 101 also skips appending the extension if the title contains a dot. Names like 'Mr. Robot' pass through a .bin intermediate, and 'Episode 1.5' ends up as 'Episode_1.ts'.
bugs.userImpact: Videos with non-English titles are saved and exported as 'VidoraX_Video_20260915_1030.mp4', and titles containing dots get mangled. The library and Gallery folder are not cleanly named.

bugs.description: maxSegments: 2_500 hard-rejects longer VODs (playlist.ts:412, planner.ts:63) as HLS_UNSUPPORTED. With 2-second segments that caps downloads at about 83 minutes.
bugs.userImpact: Full-length movies and long streams fail with 'too many segments to download safely'.

bugs.description: Only the last #EXT-X-MAP is kept (initSegmentUrl is overwritten) and it is written once at the front. Playlists with several init segments across discontinuity periods produce a file where earlier fragments are paired with the wrong init.
bugs.userImpact: Broken or unplayable output for fMP4 streams with ad breaks or multiple periods.

bugs.description: Workspace reuse is keyed only on sourceUrl equality and completedSegments > 0; there is no playlist or variant fingerprint. Segments are addressed only by index. If the master resolves to a different top variant, or the CDN re-segments between attempts, segments from different renditions get mixed.
bugs.userImpact: Rarely, a resumed download produces a mixed-resolution or corrupted file.

bugs.description: beginExportTransaction records a synthetic 'pending:${id}' marker. The real MediaStore pending URI is never sent back from native. reconcilePendingExports (250-274) skips synthetic markers, so it can never delete an orphaned IS_PENDING row after a crash mid-copy.
bugs.userImpact: A crash during 'Save to device' leaves a hidden pending MediaStore entry until Android purges it after about 7 days. The reconcile code gives false confidence.

bugs.description: The API 24–28 SAF path stores a single pendingSaf slot. A second export started before the first picker returns overwrites it, so the first JS promise never settles. The operation lock is per downloadId, so two different downloads can overlap.
bugs.userImpact: On Android 7–9, saving two videos quickly can leave the first save spinner stuck forever.

bugs.description:
The manifest has several problems for a downloader:
- It declares SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, a Play-sensitive permission that isn't used here, plus READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, which neither the MediaStore (29+) nor the SAF (24–28) paths need.
- It lacks FOREGROUND_SERVICE and a typed FGS.
- MainActivity is hard-locked to screenOrientation=portrait.
- allowBackup=true, and the backup rules come only from expo-secure-store, so files/VidoraXDownloads is included in Auto Backup.
bugs.userImpact: Extra permission warnings and Play review friction. The player has to fight the portrait lock for landscape fullscreen. Once downloads exceed the 25 MB Auto Backup quota, the app's cloud backups silently stop.

bugs.description: ID3 or ADTS headers (0xFF 0xFx) are classified as 'mp3'. KIND_TO_CONTAINER maps mp3 to 'unknown' (extension.ts:21), so packed-audio HLS (.aac segments) keeps the worker's .ts name and gets MIME video/mp2t.
bugs.userImpact: Audio-only HLS downloads get the wrong extension and MIME, and are exported to the wrong collection.

overEngineering.description:
About 2,700 lines to rename a file, open it, share it, copy it to MediaStore and delete it.
- The descriptor is rebuilt at least 4 times per action: apply-identity.ts:54 and :127, action-service.ts:87-116, export-service.ts:107.
- Naming has a 6-level evidence priority chain (naming.ts:145).
- Export uses a receipt 'transaction' model (receipt.ts begin/complete/fail/reconcile) whose reconcile path cannot work, because the pending markers are synthetic.
- Two barrels (index.ts, phase7c.ts) exist only so Node verify scripts can import pure code.
- There are two parallel open/share stacks: engine/file-actions.ts + media-file-actions.ts, and completed-file/action-service.ts.
- The managed-path check is repeated in JS (assertManagedDownloadPath 3–4 times per action) and again in Kotlin.

Three delivery backends (native module, expo-notifications, Expo Go no-op), two permission adapters (expo-notifications, PermissionsAndroid), an MMKV-persisted dedupe store, deep-link pending-target plumbing with auth and exists probes, and an FGS summary publisher with aggregate-progress and throttle-controller modules. All of that serves roughly: show a progress bar and a done notification. The FGS half has no native counterpart.

About 380 lines across 5 files for 4 preferences. Values are persisted three ways (individual MMKV keys, a versioned JSON envelope, and the Zustand store), with heuristics to reconcile them. persist.ts:100 treats a stored value equal to the default as unset, and publishDownloadSettingsFromStore (policy.ts:106-127) guesses which source wins. One Zustand store with MMKV persistence would do the job.

planner.ts and verifier.ts re-check what the parser already guarantees: duplicate index sets are checked twice, maxSegments three times, and init presence twice. Types carry deprecated alias fields (uri/url, duration/durationSeconds). A separate persist-gate module handles what is essentially a timestamp comparison.

analyze/format.ts (484 lines) and quality/normalize.ts (526) plus quality/format.ts (246) each do container, MIME, label and size normalization in different shapes: MediaAnalysisResult → MediaAnalysisVariant → DownloadQualityOption → CreateDownloadFromQualityInput → SelectedQualityMetadata → ApiCreateDownloadPayload. That is five DTOs for one selected URL.

mp4-box-classify.ts plus requireStandaloneMp4 is an elaborate heuristic built to reject IG/TikTok init segments. It rejects legitimate CMAF output, and checking whether the file has at least one decodable track with duration > 0 via MediaExtractor after muxing would be both simpler and stronger.

32 of the 125 scripts/verify-*.ts files import these modules. Many exports exist only for them, and module structure was bent around them: lazy require('react-native') in native-download-notifications.ts:32 and deep-link.ts:24, and 'pure barrel' comments. There is no Jest; the *.smoke.mjs files are placeholders or duplicated logic.

deadCode: src/downloads/notifications/fgs-summary.ts, aggregate-progress.ts, throttle-controller.ts: no-ops at runtime. The only consumer is the ensure-bridge publisher, whose updateSummary needs controller.updateNotificationSummary from the nonexistent VidoraXDownloadForeground native module.
src/downloads/engine/hls/__tests__/hls.smoke.mjs: only prints a console.log pointing at a verify script.

src/downloads/quality/__tests__/quality.smoke.mjs and phase3-integration.smoke.mjs: re-declare copies of production logic (e.g. QUALITY_LADDER) instead of importing it, and no package script runs them.
src/downloads/completed-file/phase7c.ts: barrel that exists only for Node verifiers.
completed-file/export/public-name.ts `nextCollisionSafePublicName`: referenced only from a verify script.
completed-file/export/export-service.ts `resolveExportActionsForId` (276) and `forgetExportReceiptAfterPrivateDelete` (299): no references at all.
completed-file/action-service.ts `createCompletedFileContentUri` (462; verify-only), `peekCompletedLocalUri` (482) and `resolveCompletedFileActionsForId` (248): the last two have no references.
completed-file/native-file-actions.ts `nativeCanOpenContentUri` plus Kotlin `VidoraFileActionsModule.canOpenContentUri`: unused.
completed-file/export/native-media-export.ts `nativeGetSdkInt` plus Kotlin `VidoraMediaExportModule.getSdkInt`: unused.
completed-file/uri-safety.ts `isUnsafeCallerPath`: verify-only.
completed-file/delete/plan.ts `classifyCompletedFilePresence`: no references outside barrels.
notifications/dedupe.ts `shouldEmitTerminalNotification`: deprecated and unused.
engine/hls/quality.ts `describeHlsVariants` and planner.ts `orderedAssemblyEntries`: verify-only.
completed-file/export/export-service.ts `reconcilePendingExports` (250-274): wired at bootstrap, but a no-op because every pending marker is synthetic 'pending:' and gets skipped.
engine/hls/worker.ts:14: unused import of verifyDownloadedMediaContent. segment-transfer.ts:267: unused attemptStartBytes. apply-identity.ts:106: unused error binding (eslint warnings).
engine/file-actions.ts and media-file-actions.ts: a legacy parallel open/share path that duplicates completed-file/action-service.ts (still exported from engine/index.ts).
capabilityGaps: AES-128 HLS decryption (key URI + IV / media-sequence IV). This is the most common non-DRM protection on arbitrary video sites, and it is rejected at playlist.ts:225-230. SAMPLE-AES is also rejected.

Separate audio renditions (EXT-X-MEDIA TYPE=AUDIO), DASH representations and split progressive video+audio tracks (the Instagram/YouTube pattern) all need muxing. No MediaMuxer, MediaExtractor, Media3 Transformer or ffmpeg exists, so the output is either silent or refused.
Any DASH (.mpd) support: SegmentTemplate, SegmentBase or SegmentList.
Remuxing MPEG-TS to fast-start MP4 for Gallery, external-player and seek compatibility.
EXT-X-BYTERANGE and single-file HLS, EXT-X-GAP, multiple init maps, and live/EVENT recording.
Parallel segment downloads (currently strictly sequential), and VODs longer than 2,500 segments.
Background execution that survives leaving the app or process death: no foreground service, user-initiated data transfer job, WorkManager, or Media3 DownloadService.
Codec-aware variant selection (avoid HEVC/AV1/Dolby Vision on unsupported devices) and honoring the user's chosen variant when a master URL is enqueued.
Local metadata extraction: thumbnail frame, duration, width/height. No MediaStore DURATION/RESOLUTION/DATE_TAKEN is written on export.

Organized public storage: auto-save to Movies/VidoraX/<Platform>, a user-selectable folder, or albums by site. Today the library lives only in the app sandbox, is wiped on uninstall or 'Clear storage', and 'Save to device' doubles storage with a copy.
Audio-only extraction (m4a/mp3) from muxed or HLS sources.
File-level duplicate detection (content fingerprint or size+duration). Only a browser-level URL fingerprint dedupe exists.
Unicode-preserving filenames.
Notification actions (pause, resume, cancel) and a single summary notification.
iOS export (export-service.ts:74 returns UNSUPPORTED).
audits.crossSubsystemCoupling:
HLS WORKER
- Only engine/manager.ts:2886 constructs it, typed through `AnyTransferWorker` (manager.ts:145). The manager calls `run`, `pause`, `cancel`, `holdForNetworkPolicy`, `waitUntilSettled(Bounded)`, `getPauseSettleGeneration`, `isActive` and `activeDownloadId`, and uses `instanceof HlsTransferWorker` (628, 2930) for Wi-Fi policy branching.
- It shares engine-internal contracts: EnqueueInput and LocalDownloadRecord.hlsTransfer (persisted in AsyncStorage), EngineEvent (the `completed` event's mimeType/container is consumed by bind-engine-to-store.ts:138-140), StallWatchdog, worker-settle barriers, synchronizer backend status sync, and ephemeral-target-headers/download-session-meta for cookie headers per segment.
- Replacing it with a native downloader means reimplementing that worker interface as a native-backed adapter, or replacing manager.ts's worker model outright, which is recommended.

COMPLETED-FILE
- apply-identity.ts is imported by both engine/worker.ts:88 (progressive) and engine/hls/worker.ts:65. extension.ts depends on media-detection/resource/video-resource (VIDEO_FORMATS).
- Screens load the services lazily by path: useLibraryScreen.ts:417-496, useDownloadsScreen.ts:338-357, useDownloadDetailsScreen.ts:240-262 and PlayerScreen.tsx:105 use action-service, export-service and delete-service. action-errors keys feed i18n. library-format.ts uses formatContainerLabel.
- The services depend on useDownloadsStore, downloadEngine.refreshCompletedLocalFile/remove, storage/services/catalog-persist, and the MMKV receipt key.

NOTIFICATIONS
- Initialized from bootstrap/app-initializer.ts:162, AppLockGate.tsx:39-66, ProtectedRouteGuard.tsx:24, ensure-recovery-listener.ts:29 and the settings screen. delete-service.ts:49 calls dismissActive.
- Depends on the downloadEngine event, progress and queue subscriptions, useDownloadsStore, and execution/coordinator.
- Loosely coupled, so it is easy to replace.

SETTINGS
- Read by engine manager (Wi-Fi policy, concurrency), store/settings/state.ts (DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_SETTINGS), services/auth/settings.service.ts and the settings screen hook.
- Replacing it means keeping `getDownloadSettings` and `subscribeDownloadSettings` semantics.

ANALYZE AND QUALITY
- analyze feeds screens/downloads/quality (useQualitySelection, the sheet, the loading state) and browser/media-actions/useBrowserMediaAction.
- media-detection services import analyze/format helpers (isNonMediaDocumentMime and others) and analyze-from-verification. engine/transfer-timeouts.ts imports LOCAL_ANALYZE constants.
- quality feeds the quality sheet UI, browser-media-download.service.ts and verified-quality-options.ts. toCreateDownloadInput's output shape feeds store/downloads/actions.ts (resolveCreateStreamType at :56-63, :803) and the backend POST /downloads payload.

TYPES
- types/request-context is imported by 10+ media-detection files. It is types only, so moving it is trivial.

KOTLIN
- Modules are hand-registered in MainApplication.kt:25-30 and addressed by string name through NativeModules. The JS wrappers degrade to null or no-op if a module is missing, which is how the missing FGS module went unnoticed.

WHAT BREAKS ON REPLACEMENT
- The persisted LocalDownloadRecord schema.
- MMKV keys: export receipts, notification dedupe, settings envelope.
- The `completed` event fields.
- The file-location contract `filesDir/VidoraXDownloads/{id}/`, which is also hardcoded in Kotlin at VidoraMediaExportModule.kt:323.
audits.recommendations:
TARGET DESIGN

Replace the JavaScript transfer and format core with one native Android download module built on Media3. expo-video already ships androidx.media3 exoplayer, exoplayer-hls, exoplayer-dash and datasource-okhttp (node_modules/expo-video/android/build.gradle:22-27), so the dependency cost is small. Keep JS as a thin client.

1. NATIVE DOWNLOADS: `VidoraDownloadsModule` + `VidoraDownloadService`
   - Use Media3 offline: `DownloadManager` with `HlsDownloader`/`DashDownloader`/`ProgressiveDownloader`, a `SimpleCache`, an OkHttp `DataSource.Factory` carrying per-request cookie/referer headers, and parallel segments.
   - Media3 gives you, without writing them yourself: AES-128 HLS, DASH, byte-range, resume from cached spans (fixes the truncated-segment bug), retries, and requirements such as Wi-Fi-only via `Requirements.NETWORK_UNMETERED`.
   - Run it inside a `DownloadService` subclass declared with `android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync"`, plus FOREGROUND_SERVICE and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC permissions. On API 34+ consider user-initiated data transfer jobs (JobScheduler `setUserInitiated`), because dataSync FGS is time-limited on Android 15+.
   - `DownloadNotificationHelper` gives one ongoing notification with progress. Add Pause and Cancel actions.
   - JS API:
     - `enqueue({id, kind:'progressive'|'hls'|'dash'|'split', url, audioUrl?, variant?:{bandwidth,height,codecs}, headers, title, platform})`
     - `pause(id)`, `resume(id)`, `cancel(id)`, `remove(id)`
     - Events: `progress{id, bytes, percent, speed}`, `state{id, state, error}`, `completed{id, contentUri, displayName, mime, sizeBytes, durationMs, width, height, thumbnailPath}`.

2. MUX/FINALIZE STEP, run after the download completes:
   - Add `androidx.media3:media3-transformer` at the same version, or use `MediaExtractor` + `MediaMuxer`.
   - Read the video (and separate audio) tracks from `CacheDataSource`.
   - Transmux without re-encoding to fast-start MP4, or M4A for audio-only.
   - This covers TS→MP4, CMAF/fMP4→MP4, HLS EXT-X-MEDIA audio + video, DASH video+audio, and IG-style split progressive tracks.
   - Validate with MediaExtractor: at least one video track (or one audio track for audio-only), duration > 0. Delete the heuristic mp4-box-classify.ts gate. Keep media-signature.ts only as a fast HTML/JSON rejection for progressive responses.
   - Extract a thumbnail (`MediaMetadataRetriever.getFrameAtTime`, stored in `cacheDir/thumbs/{id}.jpg`) and duration/width/height.
   - Refuse DRM (Widevine/PlayReady/FairPlay KEYFORMAT, encv/pssh) with a clear UNSUPPORTED_DRM. Give DASH, live and encrypted streams distinct, honest codes.

3. STORAGE AND ORGANIZATION:
   - Write the muxed file directly into MediaStore as the single canonical copy: RELATIVE_PATH `Movies/VidoraX/<Platform or site>/` (`Music/VidoraX/` for audio), IS_PENDING=1 until muxing finishes, then set DURATION, WIDTH, HEIGHT and DATE_TAKEN and publish. Reuse the VidoraMediaExportModule.kt:163-234 logic. No storage permission is needed on API 29+.
   - Offer an optional 'Private vault' setting that keeps files in `filesDir` (excluded from backup) instead.
   - Catalog: one row per downloadId in the existing store/MMKV: {contentUri, displayName, mime, size, durationMs, w, h, thumbnailPath, platform, sourcePageUrl, fingerprint}.
   - Filenames: `<title> [<height>p].mp4`, using a Unicode-preserving sanitizer that strips only `/\\:*?"<>|`, control characters and leading dots, capped at about 120 bytes. Let MediaStore auto-suffix collisions.
   - Dedupe: compare media fingerprint + duration + size before enqueueing.

4. OPEN/SHARE/DELETE:
   - Pass the MediaStore contentUri directly to the existing VidoraFileActionsModule. Relax its authority check to MediaStore or the provider, and remove `grantReadToSendTargets`.
   - Delete via `ContentResolver.delete` on owned rows; on API 30+ use `MediaStore.createDeleteRequest` for rows the app no longer owns after a reinstall.
   - Collapse action-service, export-service, delete-service, receipts and the phase barrels into one `library-actions.ts` of about 200 lines.

5. JS LAYERS:
   - Keep playlist.ts and fetch-playlist.ts for on-device quality analysis. Extend them to parse EXT-X-MEDIA so variants with a separate audio group are shown as 'video + audio (merged)', and to read KEY METHOD=AES-128 as supported.
   - Pass the exact chosen variant (bandwidth/height/codecs) to native, and filter codecs with `MediaCodecList`.
   - Route `.mpd` to a real DASH analyzer, e.g. Media3 `DashManifestParser` via a native `analyze(url, headers)` method, instead of the HLS path.
   - Notifications: delete service.ts, dedupe, fgs-summary, aggregate-progress and throttle-controller. Keep the preference toggle. Request POST_NOTIFICATIONS from the first Download tap, as a user gesture.
   - Settings: a single Zustand store persisted to one MMKV JSON key. Delete the dual keys, the envelope and the reconcile heuristics.
   - Manifest: remove SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE. Add the FGS permissions and service. Drop the portrait lock, or have the player unlock orientation at runtime. Add backup rules excluding the vault.

6. TESTS: delete the 32 verify scripts that target these modules. Add Jest unit tests (playlist parser fixtures, filename sanitizer, extension/MIME mapping) and one instrumented Android test that downloads a local HLS fixture (TS, CMAF with styp, AES-128, separate audio) and asserts the muxed MP4 has video and audio tracks.

STOPGAPS if the JS HLS worker must ship before the rewrite:
- (a) Download each segment to `segment-N.part` and `File.move` it to `segment-N` only after success. In the reuse check, delete any leftover `.part` files.
- (b) Assemble straight into `final.part` and `File.move` it to the final name. Remove copyHlsAssembledFile. Yield between chunks with `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))` every ~16 chunks, or do the concat in Kotlin.
- (c) For HLS finalization, validate with `requireStandaloneMp4: false`, or drop the `types.has('styp')` MEDIA_FRAGMENT rule.
- (d) Move assertEnoughDiskSpace inside the try block with an estimate of about 3x bandwidth×duration, and add a catch in manager.ts:2937 that calls fail.
- (e) Parse EXT-X-MEDIA and fail with an explicit 'separate audio track not supported' error instead of saving silent video.

audits.purpose:
This subsystem saves and displays downloaded videos, and also stores browser data. SQLite (vidorax.db, schema v2) has these tables: downloads_catalog (download job plus media metadata), media_folders, url_favorites, browser_history, bookmarks, recent_searches, recent_urls.

The Library screen never reads SQLite. Whenever something relevant changes, it rebuilds a 'canonical library' in JS by joining six sources:
1. the downloads zustand store, which is really a paged, filtered cache for the Downloads screen
2. the download engine's single AsyncStorage JSON value holding every per-download record (the only place the file path is saved)
3. live transfer snapshots
4. a module-level Set of favorite ids
5. an MMKV-persisted cache of folder assignments
6. MMKV playback-progress keys, one per video

It then hides anything whose file does not verify on disk, using synchronous expo-file-system checks with a 30s cache. storage-manager scans the app sandbox for the Storage screen and clears Paths.cache.

Answers to the key questions:
- **Source of truth:** there is no single one.
- **Drift:** the library can and does drift from reality (see bugs).
- **Schema:** it has title, source_url (the media stream URL), platform, thumbnail_url, file_size (stored as TEXT), resolution as a 'WxH' string, created_at and downloaded_at. It has no file path, no page URL, no width/height, no local thumbnail and no watch progress. The duration column is never written.
- **Thumbnails:** never generated. The app stores the page's remote og:image, or a Google favicon URL when there is none.
- **List performance:** a plain FlatList (no FlashList) over a library assembled entirely in memory, with a wrong fixed row height.
audits.architecture:
Size in scope: src/library ~2.0k lines, src/storage ~4.9k, src/store without downloads ~3.4k, src/storage-manager 0.6k, src/screens/library 2.2k, src/screens/storage 0.5k.

WHERE ONE DOWNLOADED VIDEO LIVES (id = download uuid):
(a) SQLite downloads_catalog row (src/storage/sqlite/schema.ts:91-117; src/storage/repositories/download-catalog.repository.ts). Columns: title, source_url (the resolved stream URL, see downloads/quality/to-create-input.ts:187), platform, thumbnail_url, file_name, folder_id, file_size TEXT, status, progress, quality, resolution, bitrate, retry/worker/error fields, favorite, mime_type, duration (never written), downloaded_at, created_at, updated_at. There is no local path column.
(b) AsyncStorage key 'vidorax.downloads.engine.v1'. One JSON map of every LocalDownloadRecord {localUri, localState, remoteStatus, totalBytes, hls/multiRange resume state} (src/downloads/engine/persistence.ts). The whole map is rewritten on each of ~31 upsert call sites.
(c) Filesystem: Documents/VidoraXDownloads/<id>/<fileName>, with .part, .rangepart, .hls and .mranges next to it (src/downloads/engine/file-paths.ts:9-70).
(d) MMKV:
- playback progress under 'vidorax.playback.v1:local:<id>' (src/playback/persistence.ts)
- zustand-persist mirrors of the folders list and of folderIdByMediaId (src/store/organization/folders.ts, folder-assignments.ts)
- library view mode
- seed/migration flags
(e) url_favorites table keyed by source URL, plus the catalog 'favorite' column.

In-memory only:
- useDownloadsStore (not persisted). itemsById holds the current Downloads query page plus in-flight rows; transferById holds live transfer state.
- useLibraryStore: query UI state, availabilityById, sourceRevision.
- favoriteMediaIdCache Set (src/storage/services/catalog-persist.ts:7).
- availabilityCache and playbackUriById Maps (src/library/repository.ts:54-55).

ENTRY POINTS:
- src/bootstrap/configure-storage.ts picks MMKV, then AsyncStorage, then in-memory as the zustand persist adapter.
- src/bootstrap/app-initializer.ts:46-52 calls initializeSqlite. The client.ts singleton runs the migrations.ts user_version ladder (0 to 2) and sets WAL/foreign_keys pragmas.
- app-initializer.ts:103-150 runs on every launch: ensureDownloadCatalogSeeded, refreshFavoriteMediaIdCache, then loads the first 50 catalog rows into the downloads store.
- app-initializer.ts:164-182 wires ensureLibraryCompletionBridge and bindPlaybackPersistence.

LIBRARY FLOW: LibraryScreen.tsx calls useLibraryScreen.ts (575 lines).
1. On focus: listLocalRecords(), then reconcileAvailability() (src/library/repository.ts:369-407), which calls assessLocalFile synchronously against the filesystem.
2. A useMemo runs assembleCanonicalItems (src/library/assemble.ts:222-288): collectCandidateIds, then mergeSource, then mapToMediaLibraryItem (src/library/mapper.ts).
3. enrichLibraryWithPlayback adds progress from MMKV, read through react-query hooks in src/playback/hooks.ts.
4. applyLibraryQuery (src/library/query.ts) keeps available items only, then applies product filters, search and sort.
5. LibraryList renders a FlatList (list or 2-column grid) of LibraryCard / LibraryGridTile. Continue Watching is a separate horizontal FlatList rendered above it.

Item actions (open/share/save/delete) lazy-import the completed-file services. Engine 'completed'/'removed' events go through src/library/ensure-completion-bridge.ts, which invalidates the cache, patches availability and bumps sourceRevision; the hook effect then reloads.

STORAGE SCREEN: StorageScreen.tsx uses useStorageManager.ts, which calls storage-scanner.service.ts (synchronous recursive walk), device-storage.service.ts, storage-locations.service.ts and cache-cleanup.service.ts (deletes everything under Paths.cache).

OTHER STORES IN SCOPE:
- settings/theme/app: zustand persist over MMKV, plus duplicate explicit MMKV keys written by actions and re-synced at boot.
- history/bookmarks/recent-searches: SQLite via src/storage/services and repositories.
- favorites: url_favorites plus optimistic sequence/pending maps.
- organization/folders and folder-assignments: SQLite plus MMKV mirrors.
audits.endToEndTrace:
MAIN FLOW: download completes, appears in Library, user plays it, then deletes it.

1. CREATE. src/store/downloads/actions.ts:771 awaits downloadCatalogRepository.upsert (SQLite row, status QUEUED). Then :794 upsertItem adds it to the store and :797 calls downloadEngine.enqueue.

2. FINALIZE. src/downloads/engine/worker.ts:1466-1489 (HLS: hls/worker.ts:959) writes the AsyncStorage record {localUri, localState 'complete', remoteStatus 'COMPLETED'} and emits 'completed'.

3. STORE AND CATALOG. src/downloads/bind-engine-to-store.ts:123-155 patches the item to COMPLETED with fileSize and downloadedAt, and sets a transfer snapshot. patchItem (actions.ts:593) then calls persistDownloadCatalogItem without awaiting it (src/storage/services/catalog-persist.ts:22-38). That call does a read-then-full-row UPDATE, and its errors are swallowed.

4. LIBRARY BRIDGE. src/library/ensure-completion-bridge.ts:40-90 invalidates the cache and runs reconcileAvailability([id]), which calls assessLocalFile (src/downloads/engine/local-file-state.ts:48) synchronously. It then patches availability and bumps sourceRevision.

5. RELOAD. src/screens/library/hooks/useLibraryScreen.ts:278-283 reacts to sourceRevision and runs loadLocalAndReconcile (:225-245). That re-reads the whole AsyncStorage value and re-checks every candidate on disk (30s TTL).

6. ASSEMBLE. useLibraryScreen.ts:129-158 calls assembleCanonicalItems. Title, thumbnail, quality, resolution and folder come ONLY from useDownloadsStore.itemsById (src/library/assemble.ts:131-156). Duration is always null (:137, because remoteById is always {}). Thumbnails are kept only if http(s) (src/library/mapper.ts:145-165).
   >> BREAKS HERE: itemsById is a Downloads-screen page cache. Only 50 rows are loaded at boot (app-initializer.ts:128-131), load(1) rebuilds it from 20 rows (actions.ts:390-392), and setStatusFilter/setSort reset it to {} (actions.ts:348-381). Any video outside that window falls back to the engine record: file name only, no thumbnail, folder = Unfiled, downloadedAt = record.updatedAt, which changes on every record write.

7. QUERY AND RENDER. applyLibraryQuery (src/library/query.ts:281-300) drops everything not 'available' (:37-41), so missing files are silently hidden. LibraryList.tsx:87-121 renders a FlatList with a fixed 96px getItemLayout that is wrong for variable-height cards.

8. PLAY. openPlayer(id) leads to resolvePlaybackSource (src/player/resolve-playback-source.ts:112). It calls getLocalRecord from the AsyncStorage value; if there is no record it throws MEDIA_NOT_FOUND (:143-148). The display title comes from the downloads store only (resolve-playback-source.runtime.ts:63-67).
   >> BREAKS HERE if the AsyncStorage value was lost: the card still shows, because a directory scan finds the file, but play fails.

9. PROGRESS. The playback coordinator calls savePlaybackState, one MMKV key per video (src/playback/persistence.ts:172-205). A react-query invalidation then changes the Library's playbackById memo (useLibraryScreen.ts:163-175).

10. DELETE. Long-press opens the sheet, then deleteCompletedFileFromVidoraX runs (src/downloads/completed-file/delete/delete-service.ts:78-155):
- deleteDownloadFiles
- downloadEngine.remove (src/downloads/engine/manager.ts:1946-1964): removes the record and emits 'removed', and the bridge deletes the MMKV playback key
- removeDownloadCatalogItem, not awaited, errors swallowed (catalog-persist.ts:82-87)
- dropFromDownloadsStore
   >> FRAGILE: success is reported even if the SQLite delete fails. The folder-assignment MMKV entry and the url_favorites row are never cleaned.
audits.verdictRationale:
Rewrite the data layer; keep the solid pieces. Individually, the storage primitives mostly work: the SQLite client and migration ladder, the repositories, MMKV access, the per-download file layout, and saving playback progress to MMKV.

The downloaded-media library has no source of truth. Metadata is in SQLite without a file path. The path and state are in one AsyncStorage value that can be wiped. The Library's titles and thumbnails come from an in-memory page cache owned by the Downloads screen. Favorites live in three places, folders in SQLite plus two MMKV mirrors, and progress in MMKV. The Library re-joins all of these in JS, so it drifts in ways you can see:
- metadata disappears when the Downloads filter changes or past 50 items
- videos disappear or cannot play if the AsyncStorage value is lost
- duration is never saved
- thumbnails are never generated and often fall back to favicons

Replacing this join is cheaper than patching it. The replacement is one SQL media table that holds the file path, metadata and progress, read by a thin query hook with FlashList.

- **Keep:** the SQLite bootstrap, file-path layout and path guard, the pure query/sort helpers, and the card/tile UI.
- **Refactor:** storage-manager, and the settings/theme/app persistence (currently dual-written).
- **Delete:** the dead and verify-only code, the vestigial cloud-sync plumbing, and the optimistic folder/favorite mirrors.

keepWorthy.why: Small, correct singleton open. It clears the cached promise when init fails so a later call can retry, exposes init error and ready state, and has a transaction helper. The right base for a schema v3.
user_version migration ladder that sets pragmas (WAL, foreign_keys) outside a transaction, as expo-sqlite requires. Easy to extend with a v3 step.

One directory per download id under Documents/VidoraXDownloads, same-directory .part commit with a size check, verifyCompletedFile, and assertManagedDownloadPath to block path traversal. A clean layout to keep as the on-disk organization, storing relative paths in SQLite.
Pure, deterministic filter and sort. Sort keys are computed once, missing values go last, ties break by id. Fully unit-testable; can serve as the in-memory fallback or the SQL ORDER BY reference.

Defensive pure normalizers (normalizeResolution, normalizeIsoDate, normalizeMimeType with extension fallback, resolveDisplayName) that are worth reusing. Only normalizeThumbnailUri needs to start accepting local file:// thumbnails.

Per-video progress saved as shape-validated JSON in MMKV, with progress percent computed on save and an injectable adapter for tests. Works today; the core save/load/delete can stay while the cloud-namespace migration and pendingSync/clientRevision are dropped (or progress moves into the media table).
Tiny pure join of playback summaries onto library items by id. Correct and trivially testable.
Straightforward folder CRUD with a unique normalized name, duplicate-name validation and typed errors. Keep; add a FOREIGN KEY ON DELETE SET NULL from media.

Memoized row using expo-image with recyclingKey and disk cache, fallback icon on load failure, disabled state for missing files, and complete accessibility labels. Reusable once fed from SQL rows with local thumbnails.
Same qualities as LibraryCard for grid mode. Reusable with FlashList and a numColumns grid.
Lazy require of react-native-mmkv with an Expo Go guard and a recorded reason when unavailable, so a missing native module never crashes at import time. Solid.
Small, correct free/total/used disk snapshot with null-safe handling. Keep; just move readAvailableDiskBytes out of screens/home.

bugs.description:
The Library reads title, thumbnail, quality, resolution and folder from useDownloadsStore.itemsById (assemble.ts:131-156). That map is only a paged, filtered cache for the Downloads screen, not the catalog:
- bootstrap loads just 50 rows (src/bootstrap/app-initializer.ts:128-131)
- Downloads load(1) rebuilds it from a 20-row page (src/store/downloads/actions.ts:390-392; state.ts DOWNLOADS_PAGE_SIZE=20)
- setStatusFilter and setSort reset it to {} (actions.ts:348-381; called from src/screens/downloads/hooks/useDownloadsScreen.ts:146,218,231)
Any completed video outside the current page falls back to the engine record: file name as title, no thumbnail, folderId null, downloadedAt = record.updatedAt. The Library never queries SQLite, so it cannot recover the real metadata.
bugs.userImpact: With more than 50 downloads, or after changing the Downloads filter or sort (e.g. to Failed), Library cards lose titles and thumbnails (raw file names and a generic icon), quality chips vanish, the folder filter puts everything in Unfiled, and ordering changes. The player title also falls back to the file name. It stays that way until the Downloads list happens to page those rows back in.

bugs.description: The only saved copy of each download's file path and state is one AsyncStorage value holding every record, rewritten in full on each upsert. readAll() (226-253) turns any getItem or JSON.parse failure into memoryCache = {}, and the next writeAll() (255-265) saves that empty map, erasing every record. writeAll also swallows setItem failures, so records can silently exist only in memory. On Android, an AsyncStorage row that outgrows the ~2 MB CursorWindow cannot be read, and this layout (HLS/multi-range state per record, completed records never pruned) grows toward that limit. SQLite has no path column to recover from (schema.ts:93-117). Plausible rather than reproduced: it depends on the value growing or being corrupted.
bugs.userImpact: Every download can lose its record at once. Library items outside the store page disappear. Items still in the store keep showing, but tapping play fails with 'This video could not be found in your library' (src/player/resolve-playback-source.ts:143-148). Open, Share and Save to device break. The video files stay on disk as orphans nothing in the UI can delete.

bugs.description:
upsert() reads the row with getById, then writes all 21 columns back from that snapshot, across separate awaits and without a transaction. Concurrent writers to the same id can interleave, and the later UPDATE writes back a stale favorite, folder_id or duration. The writers are:
- setFavorite (src/store/favorites/actions.ts:562)
- setFolderId (src/store/organization/folder-assignments.ts:121)
- persistDownloadCatalogItem, fired from every durable patchItem and even from read paths: fetchOne calls upsertItem (actions.ts:830-835), and so does src/screens/favorites/hooks/useFavoritesScreen.ts:50-52
For a new id, two concurrent INSERTs collide on the primary key and the error is swallowed (catalog-persist.ts:36-38). Plausible race, not reproduced.
bugs.userImpact: A favorite toggle or 'move to folder' can silently revert if it coincides with a download completing or with opening Download Details or Favorites. No error is shown.

bugs.description:
removeDownloadCatalogItem (src/storage/services/catalog-persist.ts:82-87) is not awaited and swallows its own error, so the surrounding try/catch and the DELETE_CATALOG_FAILED path can never run, and delete always reports success. Cleanup is spread across separate non-atomic writes:
- the SQLite row
- the engine record (engine.remove, failure swallowed at :127-131)
- the MMKV playback key (via the 'removed' event)
- the MMKV folderIdByMediaId entry (never cleaned)
- the url_favorites row (never cleaned)
bugs.userImpact: If the catalog delete fails, the 'deleted' video comes back after a restart as a Completed row in Downloads with no file behind it (Library hides it as missing). Stale folder and favorite entries pile up.

bugs.description:
Duration is never recorded or shown:
- mergeSource reads duration only from `remote`, which is always {} (src/library/repository.ts:240; useLibraryScreen.ts:136)
- DownloadItem has no duration field (normalizeDownloadItem, src/store/downloads/actions.ts:151-220)
- downloadItemToCatalogInput only writes duration through an extras argument that no caller passes (download-catalog.repository.ts:144,169)
So downloads_catalog.duration is NULL for every row.
bugs.userImpact: No length shown on any Library card or tile. Continue Watching has to back-compute length from progress. Sorting or filtering by length is impossible.

bugs.description: No thumbnail is ever generated from the downloaded file: nothing in src or android/ uses expo-video-thumbnails or MediaMetadataRetriever. The catalog stores the page's og:image or poster URL, or a Google favicon URL when there is none (to-create-input.ts:89-97). normalizeThumbnailUri (src/library/mapper.ts:145-165) drops every non-http(s) URI, so even a local file:// thumbnail could not be shown. Social CDN image URLs are signed and expire. Storage > Clear cache deletes all of Paths.cache, including expo-image's disk cache (src/storage-manager/services/cache-cleanup.service.ts:32-53).
bugs.userImpact: Many videos show a stretched 128px site favicon or a blank icon. Instagram and TikTok thumbnails break once the signed URL expires or the cache is cleared, and never come back. Rendering the Library also sends the list of sites the user downloads from to Google's favicon service.

bugs.description: getItemLayout assumes every list row is exactly listRowHeight = 96 (src/screens/library/theme/library-tokens.ts). A LibraryCard (LibraryCard.tsx:72-137) has 24px of vertical padding, a title of up to 2 lines, an optional file-name line, a meta line of up to 2 lines and an optional 'file unavailable' line, so most rows are taller than 96px.
bugs.userImpact: Scroll positions are computed wrong. Combined with removeClippedSubviews this gives blank gaps or clipped and overlapping rows, jumpy fast scrolling, and scroll position not restoring correctly.

bugs.description: For videos outside the store page, downloadedAt falls back to record.updatedAt. upsertLocalRecord overwrites updatedAt with the current time on every write (src/downloads/engine/persistence.ts:283-286), and that includes refreshCompletedLocalFile (src/downloads/engine/manager.ts:485-520). That function is called by Open, Share and Save (completed-file/action-service.ts:138, export/export-service.ts:88, engine/media-file-actions.ts), and for up to 8 completed rows each time the Downloads screen regains focus (useDownloadsScreen.ts:160-172).
bugs.userImpact: Opening or sharing an older video can move it to the top of Newest and into the Recently Downloaded filter, and its shown download date changes.

bugs.description: An item counts as favorite if any of three sources says so: catalog favorite ids (a module-level Set), url_favorites matched on the download's sourceUrl, or the Favorites store. sourceUrl is a media stream URL, so page-level favorites rarely match, and two downloads that share a stream URL both show a heart. Removing a favorite from the Favorites screen (favorites actions remove, then urlFavoriteRepository.delete) never clears downloads_catalog.favorite. The favoriteMediaIds memo (useLibraryScreen.ts:116-119) depends on urlIndex, catalogIdentity and sourceRevision, not on the Set that refreshFavoriteMediaIdCache replaces asynchronously, so an un-favorite can stay stale. Plausible, not reproduced.
bugs.userImpact: Hearts and the Favorites filter in the Library disagree with the Favorites screen. Removing a favorite may leave the video in the Library's Favorites filter.

bugs.description: markInitialized() runs in `finally`, in the same batch as setError, and `status` only returns 'error' when !initialized (:293). So the LibraryErrorState branch (LibraryScreen.tsx:253-258) can never render. A SQLite init failure is not surfaced at all, because the Library never touches SQLite.
bugs.userImpact: A failed load shows the 'No downloads yet' empty state instead of an error with a retry button.

bugs.description: `initialized` is in the useFocusEffect callback deps (:272) and in the sourceRevision effect deps (:283). The first open therefore runs loadLocalAndReconcile two or three times: on focus, again when initialized flips, and again if a completion bumped sourceRevision earlier in the session. Each run re-reads the whole AsyncStorage value, sets a new localRecords array (forcing full re-assembly) and runs synchronous File.exists / size / .rangepart checks per candidate on the JS thread. eslint also reports two errors here: react-hooks/purity (Date.now inside useMemo, :186) and react-hooks/set-state-in-effect (:282).
bugs.userImpact: A janky first open, and redundant work that grows with library size.

bugs.description: ContinueWatchingSection is rendered as a sibling above the FlatList instead of as its ListHeaderComponent.
bugs.userImpact: The carousel permanently takes about 220px at the top, never scrolls away, and pull-to-refresh only works on the list below it.

bugs.description: setFilter('folder') pre-selects folderId = 'unfiled' before the folder sheet opens (useLibraryScreen.ts:336-343), so dismissing the sheet leaves an Unfiled filter applied silently. Quality is picked from its own chip without setting filter = 'quality', yet setFilter clears quality for any other filter. Switching, say, Favorites to Recently Downloaded silently drops the chosen quality.
bugs.userImpact: Filters change without the user asking. A 'This folder is empty' state can appear just from dismissing a sheet.

bugs.description:
Several problems in the storage scan and cache clear:
- every file in a download directory that isn't .rangepart counts as 'videos', including in-progress .part files
- both arms of the directory branch (101-107) add to tempBytes, so the conditional does nothing
- imagesBytes is hard-coded to 0 (:170) while a 'Thumbnails' location card is shown
- the recursive scan and clearVidoraXCache run as synchronous JSI calls on the JS thread (setTimeout(0) does not move work off it), and the scan reruns on every Storage screen focus
- storage-manager imports from screens/home utils (device-storage.service.ts:3, storage-summary.service.ts:2-7)
bugs.userImpact: The storage breakdown is misleading, and the UI freezes on devices with large caches or many downloads.

bugs.description:
Three schema issues:
- file_size is TEXT, which forces BigInt parsing in the mapper, query and selectors and makes SQL SUM or ORDER BY size impossible
- folder_id has no FOREIGN KEY even though PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON is set, so folder delete depends on a manual clearFolderAssignments call (src/store/organization/folders.ts:164)
- list() puts user text into LIKE without escaping % and _ (download-catalog.repository.ts:215-222)
bugs.userImpact: Mostly latent: size sorting has to be done in JS, orphaned folder ids are possible if the app dies mid-delete, and searches containing % or _ match unexpected rows.

bugs.description: The 'one-time' Phase 1A seed runs on every launch (app-initializer.ts:116-124), doing listAllIds plus a full read of the engine's AsyncStorage value. Its storeItems input is always empty because useDownloadsStore is not persisted and only gets hydrated afterwards (app-initializer.ts:128). Rows seeded from engine records get title = file name and createdAt = record.updatedAt.
bugs.userImpact: Extra startup I/O before first render, with no benefit on installs that have already been migrated.

bugs.description: browser_history has no retention limit. Rows are only merged within a dedup window, deleted by id, or wiped with clear-all. recent_urls and recent_searches are trimmed to 50, but history is not.
bugs.userImpact: The history table and history screen grow indefinitely, and frequently-visited and suggestion queries slow down over time.

overEngineering.area: src/library/* canonical assembly (repository.ts, assemble.ts, mapper.ts, eligibility.ts, availability-ttl.ts, diagnostics.ts, ~1.3k lines)
overEngineering.description: Re-derives the library on every change by joining five in-memory sources and checking the filesystem, instead of querying SQLite for completed rows. It carries leftover cloud-enrichment plumbing (MediaMetadataRemoteItem/remoteById, always {}), a playbackUriById map nobody reads, and dependency injection via configureLibraryRepository called from two places (the bridge and the screen hook).

overEngineering.area: Favorites (catalog.favorite column + url_favorites table + src/store/favorites 727-line actions + favoriteMediaIdCache Set)
overEngineering.description: Four overlapping favorite mechanisms, with optimistic mutation sequence numbers and pending/inFlight maps, for a local SQLite write that takes milliseconds.

An optimistic folder-assignment store with mutationSeq/pending/inFlightDesired maps, persisted to MMKV, mirroring a single-column SQLite update. syncFromRemoteAssignments targets a backend that no longer exists, and useFoldersStore keeps a second MMKV copy of the media_folders table.

overEngineering.area: Settings/theme/app persistence (src/store/settings, theme, app, src/storage/mmkv/preferences.ts, bootstrap syncMmkvFromStores, persist-sync.ts)
overEngineering.description: Values are dual-written to zustand-persist (MMKV) and to separate explicit MMKV keys, reconciled at boot, with skipHydration, rehydrateAndWait, syncAppStoreFromDisk and a 3s polling loop in awaitOnboardingPersisted. These all work around the persist adapter being configured after the stores are created. The app also uses three storage engines (SQLite, MMKV, AsyncStorage), plus an in-memory fallback.

overEngineering.area: src/playback persistence stack (coordinator.ts 969 lines, domain/merge.ts, reconcile.ts, persistence.ts migration)
overEngineering.description: Remote-merge reconciliation, pendingSync/clientRevision, backend sync intervals and a cloud-to-local namespace migration, all for progress that is local-only now.
BigInt parsing across the mapper, query sort keys, store selectors and repository for byte counts that fit safely in a JS number and should be an SQLite INTEGER.
A 316-line migration shim with separate first-run and fast paths that runs on every launch.
Six 'location' cards, two of them template paths like '{VidoraXDownloads}/{id}/.hls/', that the user cannot act on.
A barrel re-exporting ~100 selectors, most of them unused. Screens subscribe with inline selectors instead.
