audits.crossSubsystemCoupling:
Tight and two-way between library, downloads store and engine.

What the Library depends on:
- downloads-store internals: itemsById, transferById, selectDownloadCatalogIdentitySignature, selectLibraryTransferSignature
- engine persistence (listLocalRecords/getLocalRecord from AsyncStorage) and engine local-file-state/file-paths
- favorites store urlIndex, folders and folder-assignments stores
- playback react-query hooks and MMKV persistence
- navigation intents
- completed-file action/export/delete services

What depends on this subsystem:
- Player: src/player/resolve-playback-source.runtime.ts and use-player-session.ts use reconcileAvailability, invalidateLibraryAvailability, isCompletedStatus, isTempOrWorkspaceArtifact, normalizeMimeType and resolveDisplayName, and read title/MIME from the downloads store.
- Downloads store: src/store/downloads/actions.ts is built on downloadCatalogRepository (list/upsert/getById) and catalog-persist.
- Other callers: the Favorites screen searches the catalog by sourceUrl; DownloadDetailsScreen uses the folder stores; delete-service uses removeDownloadCatalogItem.
- Bootstrap: app-initializer seeds the catalog, hydrates the first 50 rows and wires the completion and playback bridges.
- Home dashboard: uses storage-manager buildHomeStorageSummary, while storage-manager imports back from screens/home utils (a layering inversion).
- Browser: suggestions and history recording use historyService/bookmarkService/recentSearchService.
- Most screens use useSettingsStore/useThemeStore/useAppStore.
- About 18 verify scripts import library/storage/playback persistence.

Replacing the catalog and library layer would break: downloads store load/applyPage/create, the favorites flows, folder move/delete, delete-service, bootstrap seeding and hydration, the player's source resolution, and the verify scripts.

The engine's AsyncStorage records are the real path authority. The persistence rewrite therefore has to happen together with the downloads subsystem, which should write file path, size and metadata into the same SQL media row at finalize. Browser history, bookmarks and recent searches are loosely coupled (browser only) and can be kept separately.
audits.recommendations:
TARGET: SQLite is the single source of truth for downloaded media. MMKV holds only prefs and flags. Zustand holds only UI state and live transfer progress. AsyncStorage is removed.

1) SCHEMA v3 (migration from v2). Timestamps are epoch ms INTEGER, sizes are INTEGER, paths are relative to Paths.document.
CREATE TABLE media(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('queued','downloading','paused','failed','cancelled','completed','deleting')),
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_site TEXT NOT NULL,
  page_url TEXT,
  media_url TEXT NOT NULL,
  file_rel_path TEXT,
  file_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  mime_type TEXT,
  container TEXT,
  size_bytes INTEGER,
  duration_ms INTEGER,
  width INTEGER,
  height INTEGER,
  bitrate INTEGER,
  thumb_rel_path TEXT,
  remote_thumb_url TEXT,
  folder_id TEXT REFERENCES folders(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  favorite INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  position_ms INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_played_at INTEGER,
  watched INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  error_code TEXT,
  error_message TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  completed_at INTEGER,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
Indexes: (status, completed_at DESC), (folder_id, completed_at DESC), (source_site, completed_at DESC), (last_played_at DESC).
Engine resume state (range validators, HLS segment index, multi-range parts) goes in a download_jobs(id PK REFERENCES media ON DELETE CASCADE, state_json TEXT, updated_at) table, written in its own row, never one blob.

2) ONE REPOSITORY (src/storage/media.repository.ts). Every mutation is a targeted UPDATE, never read-modify-write:
- create, markProgress (in memory only)
- finalize(id, {fileRelPath, sizeBytes, mime, container, durationMs, width, height, thumbRelPath}), one UPDATE in a transaction
- setFavorite, moveToFolder, savePosition (throttled ~5s plus flush on pause, unmount and app background)
- markDeleting, delete
- query({status:'completed', folderId?, site?, favorite?, inProgress?, search?, sort, limit, offset})
The repository bumps a mediaVersion counter, or uses expo-sqlite addDatabaseChangeListener with enableChangeListener. No writes from read paths.

3) FINALIZE PIPELINE, owned by the downloads subsystem but writing here:
- verify the file (reuse verifyCompletedFile)
- probe metadata with expo-video or a ~50-line Kotlin MediaMetadataRetriever module: duration, width, height, rotation
- grab a frame at ~10% of duration (expo-video-thumbnails or Kotlin getFrameAtTime) into VidoraXDownloads/<id>/thumb.jpg
- call mediaRepository.finalize, then emit one 'media-changed' event
- a background backfill queue fills thumb and duration for older completed rows that lack them

4) LIBRARY SCREEN. useMediaQuery(params) runs repository.query through react-query keyed on mediaVersion. Render with @shopify/flash-list (list, and grid via numColumns 2-3), with Continue Watching as ListHeaderComponent (query: position_ms>0 AND watched=0 ORDER BY last_played_at DESC). Card thumbnail is file://thumb_rel_path, falling back to remote_thumb_url, falling back to an icon, never a favicon. Search uses title/source_site LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' (FTS5 later if needed). Groups: All, Favorites, In progress, per-site chips from SELECT DISTINCT source_site, Folders. Reuse the LibraryCard/LibraryGridTile visuals and the query.ts comparators only where an in-memory sort is still needed. Delete useLibraryScreen's six-source join, library/repository.ts, assemble.ts, ensure-completion-bridge.ts, the availability TTL cache, favoriteMediaIdCache, folder-assignments store, the folders MMKV mirror, and url_favorites for media (url_favorites/bookmarks stay only for browser pages).

5) PLAYER. Resolve by id from media.file_rel_path (one SELECT plus a File.exists check). If the file is missing, UPDATE status to a 'missing' flag and show 'File missing - Remove?' instead of hiding the row. Progress goes to media.position_ms/last_played_at/watched. Drop the per-video MMKV keys, the namespace migration, pendingSync/clientRevision/remote merge, and shrink the coordinator to throttled save plus flush.

6) DELETE AND JANITOR.
- Delete: UPDATE status='deleting', then remove directory VidoraXDownloads/<id>, then DELETE FROM media (cascades download_jobs), all awaited, with errors surfaced.
- On startup (idle): finish any 'deleting' rows; remove directories whose id has no row; flag completed rows whose file is missing; delete stale .part/.hls/.mranges for rows not in an active status.

7) STORAGE SCREEN. Videos = SQL SUM(size_bytes) WHERE status='completed'. Temp and orphans = one async directory walk off the render path. Actions: Clear cache (thumbnails now live in documents, so this is safe), Delete partial files, Remove orphans. Move readAvailableDiskBytes into storage-manager.

8) SETTINGS/THEME/APP. Import configure-storage before any store module (first import in entry.js) so zustand persist over MMKV hydrates synchronously. Then delete the explicit MMKV preference/theme writes, syncMmkvFromStores, skipHydration/rehydrateAndWait/awaitOnboardingPersisted polling. Native readers use the same MMKV keys.

9) MIGRATION.
- v3 copies downloads_catalog into media.
- It reads the engine AsyncStorage value once to fill file_rel_path/size. If that value is unreadable, it scans VidoraXDownloads/<id>/ and picks the single file that isn't .part/.rangepart/thumb.
- source_site comes from platform/host; page_url stays NULL for legacy rows.
- Keep the old tables until v4, then drop them.

10) TESTS. Put SQL behind a tiny adapter interface so repository and query logic run in Jest against better-sqlite3. Unit-test finalize, delete/janitor and query building. Retire the verify-*.ts scripts for this area.

audits.purpose: This subsystem is the in-app player for downloaded files. It routes /player/[id] to PlayerScreen. It looks up the local file from the download record, loads it into an expo-video `useVideoPlayer` with `replaceAsync`, and shows a cover until the first frame paints. The screen has custom chrome: top bar, play/±10s/mute/speed, a scrub timeline, and speed and orientation sheets. It also has gestures (double-tap seek in the centre, left-strip brightness, right-strip system volume) and in-app immersive fullscreen (orientation lock plus hidden system bars). Playback progress goes out as events on a global event bus to a persistence coordinator that writes JSON to MMKV. Library, Home and Watch History read that data for Continue Watching, and the player reads it for auto-resume.
audits.architecture:
ENTRY POINT: src/app/(app)/player/[id].tsx just re-exports PlayerScreen. Every list opens the player with openPlayer(mediaId) (src/navigation/helpers/open-player.ts:18), which pushes `/player/<encoded downloadId>`.

SCREEN (src/screens/player/PlayerScreen.tsx, 593 lines): composes 9 hooks.
- usePlayerSession (src/player/use-player-session.ts, 872 lines) owns:
  - the expo-video player and all session state;
  - 17 refs used as staleness guards (resolveGenRef, armedGenerationRef, loadArmedRef, firstFrameAcceptedGenRef, lastAssignedUri/GenerationRef, mountedRef, a `cancelled` flag);
  - a 12s PreparationWatchdog;
  - the first-frame "composition-synced reveal" (first-frame-state.ts, deferred with requestAnimationFrame);
  - pausing on app background;
  - a controller wrapper (player-controller.ts: adaptVideoPlayer + createPlayerController);
  - emitting playback events.
- useResumePrompt (src/playback/use-resume-prompt.ts) reads MMKV and seeks once.
- useFullscreenLifecycle (use-fullscreen-lifecycle.ts + fullscreen-state.ts) drives module-global orientation-controller.ts and system-bars.ts singletons. Their native adapters are injected by player-chrome.runtime.ts.
- usePlayerBrightness → useBrightnessControl (expo-brightness).
- usePlayerVolume → android-media-volume.adapter.ts → native VidoraMediaVolumeModule.kt (STREAM_MUSIC).
- usePlayerOrientation.
- usePlayerSideGestures (drives the HUD).
- useControlsVisibility (wraps the ControlsVisibilityController class).

UI COMPONENTS (src/screens/player/components): PlayerVideoSurface (VideoView plus three side-by-side GestureDetector strips at 25/50/25% width), PlayerTopBar, PlayerControls, PlayerTimeline (RNGH Pan+Tap scrub with preview), SeekFeedback, PlayerAdjustmentHud, PlaybackSpeedSheet, OrientationSheet. ResumePlaybackSheet is unused.

SOURCE RESOLUTION: resolve-playback-source.ts is a pure function with dependency injection. The `.runtime.ts` file wires in downloads-engine getLocalRecord/assessLocalFile/verifyCompletedFile/assertManagedDownloadPath, library availability helpers, and useDownloadsStore for title and MIME type.

PERSISTENCE:
- The session emits playbackStarted, positionChanged (≤1/s), paused, completed and playerExited into a module-level Set (src/player/playback-events.ts).
- There is exactly one subscriber, bound at bootstrap: app-initializer.ts:177-181 → src/playback/bind-playback-persistence.ts → PlaybackPersistenceCoordinator (src/playback/coordinator.ts, 969 lines).
- The coordinator writes `vidorax.playback.v1:local:<mediaId>` JSON through persistence.ts (MMKV, silently falling back to an in-memory Map) at most every 5s and on pause/exit/background/complete. It also invalidates the react-query ['playback'] keys.
- src/playback/hooks.ts feeds useLibraryScreen, useHomeDashboard and WatchHistoryScreen.
- About half the coordinator is a cloud-sync engine (revisions, 401/403/404/409 handling, reconnect waves, remote reconcile) that production never runs, because bind passes sync: null.

STATE OWNERSHIP:
- Session state is screen-local React state, updated about every 350ms by timeUpdate, which re-renders the whole screen.
- Orientation and system-bar lock state are mutable module globals.
- Resume data lives in MMKV.

NATIVE: VidoraMediaVolumeModule.kt and PlayerNativePackage.kt are committed in android/ and duplicated byte-for-byte in native/android/player/. scripts/apply-player-native-modules.js (postinstall) copies them and string-patches MainApplication.kt, which already registers the package.
audits.endToEndTrace:
1. OPEN: A list row calls openPlayer(id) (open-player.ts:18). PlayerScreen mounts, parseRouteMediaId (media-id.ts:36) validates the id, and usePlayerSession(mediaId) starts.
2. CREATE: `useVideoPlayer(null, …)` (use-player-session.ts:135-141) sets loop, interval, rate and volume. Nothing in the load path ever calls play().
3. RESOLVE:
   - The resolve effect (273) bumps the generation, creates the watchdog, sets phase 'resolving' and starts the 12s timer (321).
   - resolvePlaybackSource (327 → resolve-playback-source.ts:112-267) runs synchronous file-system checks and returns {uri, displayName, mimeType}. The MIME type is never used.
4. LOAD: `await player.replaceAsync({uri, contentType:'auto'})` (357). On Android the promise resolves right after prepare() on the main queue (expo-video VideoModule.kt:377-381). The load is then marked armed (375-376); if status is already readyToPlay, isReady is set (378-394).
5. READY: statusChange readyToPlay (550-570) clears the watchdog and sets isReady=true. isLoading stays true "until first frame".
6. RESUME: The useResumePrompt effect (use-resume-prompt.ts:127-160) sees isReady and calls controller.seekTo(savedPosition) while the player is paused behind the cover.
7. FIRST FRAME:
   - VideoView onFirstFrameRender (PlayerVideoSurface.tsx:202) → markFirstFrameRendered (use-player-session.ts:214-270) → next requestAnimationFrame → completeSurfaceReveal → isSurfaceRevealed.
   - The cover disappears (PlayerScreen.tsx:151-154, 402) and controls render (437).
   - BREAKS: expo-video only emits this event from ExoPlayer onRenderedFirstFrame (VideoView.kt:327-332). An audio-only file, or a video whose track ExoPlayer deselects, never paints a frame. The watchdog was already cleared at step 5, so the "Preparing" cover stays forever with no controls or timeline and gestures disabled.
8. BRIGHTNESS PERMISSION (runs at mount, in parallel):
   - useBrightnessControl (use-brightness-control.ts:26-35) calls Brightness.requestPermissionsAsync(). On Android that is WRITE_SETTINGS, which expo-modules-core handles by launching Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_WRITE_SETTINGS (PermissionsService.kt:167-187, 354-361).
   - WRITE_SETTINGS is not in the manifest, so it is never granted. The user is thrown to system Settings; the app backgrounds and the session pauses (481-524).
   - On return, available=false and the effect re-runs (deps [available]), requesting again.
9. PLAY: The user must tap Play: onPlayPause (PlayerScreen.tsx:229-245) → controller.play → player.play. playingChange (588-628) sets isPlaying and emits playbackStarted; coordinator.startPlayback (coordinator.ts:220-276) writes lastPlayedAt.
10. CONTROLS: Force-visible ends and bump() schedules the 3s auto-hide (controls-visibility.ts:62-70, 113-124). When the controls hide, the timeline dock (PlayerScreen.tsx:465-489), which is a flex sibling of the stage, unmounts. The video stage grows, so the video visibly resizes on every show/hide.
11. PROGRESS: timeUpdate every 350ms (630-666) calls setSession, re-rendering the whole screen. positionChanged (≤1/s) → coordinator.updatePosition → MMKV write at most every 5s.
12. GESTURES:
   - Centre 50%: Exclusive(doubleTap, singleTap) gives ±10s or toggles controls. This works, but single taps lag while waiting for the double-tap to fail.
   - Left strip: the brightness pan is disabled (step 8).
   - Right strip: the volume pan changes device STREAM_MUSIC. A plain tap on a strip triggers onBegin, which shows the HUD; onEnd never fires, so the HUD stays up (use-player-side-gestures.ts:148-156, PlayerVideoSurface.tsx:157-171). The strips have no tap gesture, so tapping the outer half of the video never toggles controls.
13. FULLSCREEN: toggleFullscreen → lock landscape + hide bars (use-fullscreen-lifecycle.ts:80-102) → the layout switches to absoluteFill with no safe-area edges. This works.
14. END: playToEnd (668-700) sets isCompleted and completionEmittedRef. Rewind or double-tap afterwards does not clear isCompleted, while ExoPlayer resumes playing. A second end is ignored (681), leaving a Play button that does nothing in STATE_ENDED (VideoModule.kt:259-262).
15. EXIT:
   - Back → leavePlayer (PlayerScreen.tsx:177-191): controller.pause emits paused, and the coordinator persists the correct position. Then restorePresentation → router.back.
   - On unmount, React runs passive cleanups in hook order. useVideoPlayer's useReleasingSharedObject cleanup releases the player first; SharedObject.cpp release() nulls the JS native state synchronously.
   - The session exit cleanup (use-player-session.ts:436-462) then reads player.currentTime. The read throws, is caught, and becomes 0, so playerExited(positionSeconds: 0) is emitted.
   - coordinator.exit (coordinator.ts:402-432) accepts 0 as valid and flushSync persists position 0.
   - BREAKS: the saved resume position is overwritten with 0 on every normal exit.
16. REOPEN: useResumePrompt loads position 0; isResumeEligible needs ≥15s, so there is no resume. The item drops out of Continue Watching (continue-watching.ts:21-26). A position only survives if the app is backgrounded or killed before the screen unmounts.
17. NOT PRESENT: PiP (expo-video plugin has no options; VideoView has no allowsPictureInPicture), background audio (the session force-pauses on background), next/previous (the route carries a single id), and subtitle or audio-track selection.
audits.verdictRationale:
Most of the core user flows are broken or fragile at runtime:
- Resume position is overwritten with 0 on every exit, which also breaks Continue Watching.
- Every player open bounces the user to Android's "Modify system settings" screen, and the brightness gesture is permanently disabled.
- Audio-only downloads, which the download pipeline produces, hang forever on "Preparing" with no controls.
- Playback never starts on its own.
- Side-strip taps leave a stuck HUD and do not toggle controls.
- The completed state breaks after seeking back from the end.
- The video resizes every time the controls auto-hide.

These are wiring and state-model problems spread across an 872-line session hook, a 593-line screen and a 969-line persistence coordinator. They are layered with 7 overlapping staleness mechanisms (one, `isCurrentPlayerSession`, compares a ref to itself), a two-phase first-frame reveal on top of expo-video's own first-frame workaround, a pass-through controller adapter, module-global orientation and system-bar singletons with injectable adapters, and a cloud-sync engine that production never runs. Almost all of that indirection exists so Node "verify" scripts can import pieces, and those scripts mostly assert source-text `includes()`.

A clean expo-video SDK 57 player needs roughly 800-1,200 lines, not ~8,600. Patching bug-by-bug inside this structure would keep the complexity that caused the bugs.

It is not a delete-everything situation. Several small pure modules and one native module are correct and should be carried into the rewrite (see keepWorthy): the source resolver, error codes, media-id validation, seek/format/rate helpers, the progress/completion/resume rules, the MMKV storage format (so existing progress survives), the controls auto-hide rules, the timeline scrub approach, the in-app immersive fullscreen approach, and VidoraMediaVolumeModule.

keepWorthy.why: Solid defensive resolver. It requires the record id to match, requires completed status, rejects temp/workspace artifacts and partial files, asserts the path is inside the managed download dir, and verifies size. Missing files map to FILE_UNAVAILABLE with an availability reconcile. Keep the logic; the dependency-injection seam and the .runtime.ts binder can collapse into direct imports.

A clear PlayerErrorCode set used by localization (localizePlayerError) and support (getPlayerSupportContext), with a recoverability rule and a conservative native-error classifier. Keep the codes so localization and support do not change.
Small, correct route-param validation that rejects paths, schemes, traversal, encoded separators and over-long ids. Good security hygiene for a file-backed player.

Tiny, correct pure helpers: seek clamping that never invents an upper bound, mm:ss/h:mm:ss formatting, the allowed rate list, and mute/unmute that remembers the last audible volume. Easy to unit-test and reuse.

Correct, simple product rules: resume only at ≥15s and not near the end; completed at ≥95% or ≤30s remaining when duration ≥60s; Continue Watching eligibility. Library and Home already depend on them (useLibraryScreen, home-derive).

The `vidorax.playback.v1:local:<mediaId>` JSON format with shape validation is reasonable and already holds users' watch history. Keep the format and the load/save/list functions. Drop the cloud-namespace migration and the per-call require/in-memory fallback.

The auto-hide rules are correct. Controls stay visible when paused, seeking, a sheet is open, loading, errored or completed; interaction restarts a single 3s timer. The logic can shrink to a ~30-line hook, but the semantics are right.

The scrub interaction is basically right: RNGH Pan onBegin/onUpdate/onEnd plus onFinalize cancel, exclusive with Tap-to-seek, with a preview value committed on release. Only the placement (layout-shifting dock) and styling need rework.

In-app immersive fullscreen keeps the same VideoView and player: lock landscape with expo-screen-orientation, hide status and navigation bars, restore on back/error/unmount. That is the right approach on Android with expo-video and it works. Keep the approach; drop the fullscreen state machine and module-global adapters, and switch to NavigationBar.setHidden (setVisibilityAsync is deprecated in v57).

Small and correct: STREAM_MUSIC read/write, and a VOLUME_CHANGED broadcast receiver registered with RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED on API 33+ and unregistered in invalidate(). Worth keeping for MX-Player-style volume swipes, ideally moved to a local Expo module so it survives prebuild. It should not back the mute button.

The error screen offers localized title and message, Retry only for recoverable codes, and an 'Open with' external-app fallback for UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA/PLAYBACK_FAILED. That fallback matters for an 'any format' downloader and is worth preserving.

bugs.description: The exit cleanup (lines 436-462) reads `player.currentTime` after the player is already released. useVideoPlayer is declared first (line 135), so its unmount cleanup runs first, and React runs passive cleanups in hook order. That cleanup (expo-modules-core useReleasingSharedObject) calls release(), which nulls the JS native state synchronously (common/cpp/SharedObject.cpp). The later currentTime read throws, is caught, and becomes 0, so the hook emits `playerExited` with positionSeconds 0. PlaybackPersistenceCoordinator.exit (src/playback/coordinator.ts:402-432) accepts 0 as valid (isValidProgressNumbers(0, d) is true), and flushSync('exit') overwrites the correct position that the preceding 'paused' flush had saved.
bugs.userImpact: Every normal exit (back button or chrome back) resets the saved position to 0. Reopening never resumes, and the item disappears from Continue Watching and Home shelves (position < 15s). Progress only survives if the app is backgrounded or killed while the player is still mounted.

bugs.description: Brightness.requestPermissionsAsync() runs on every mount. On Android it requests WRITE_SETTINGS (expo-brightness BrightnessModule.kt:26-27). expo-modules-core PermissionsService.askForPermissions then launches Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_WRITE_SETTINGS with startActivity whenever Settings.System.canWrite() is false (PermissionsService.kt:167-187, 354-361). WRITE_SETTINGS is declared in neither app.json, the app manifest, nor expo-brightness's manifest, so it can never be granted. The result is setAvailable(false). The effect depends on [available], so it re-runs and calls requestPermissionsAsync a second time. The permission is not even needed: setBrightnessAsync only changes window brightness.
bugs.userImpact: Opening any video kicks the user out to Android's 'Modify system settings' page, possibly twice. The player pauses because the app backgrounds, and the brightness swipe never works.

bugs.description: The startup cover, controls, timeline and gestures are all gated on isSurfaceRevealed, which is only set after VideoView onFirstFrameRender (PlayerScreen.tsx:151-154, 379, 437, 465; first-frame-state.ts:31-39). The preparation watchdog is cleared on readyToPlay (use-player-session.ts:379, 551), before any frame renders. expo-video Android emits onFirstFrameRender only from ExoPlayer onRenderedFirstFrame (VideoView.kt:327-332). The download pipeline produces audio-only files (useQualitySelection.ts:772 'audio_only', quality/normalize.ts:309), and nothing stops them from reaching openPlayer. Videos whose video track ExoPlayer deselects (e.g. an unsupported HEVC/AV1 profile) also never render a frame.
bugs.userImpact: Audio downloads and some video files sit on a 'Preparing…' spinner forever. There is no play button, no timeline, no timeout and no error; the only way out is Back.

bugs.description: The load path never starts playback. useVideoPlayer's setup (135-141) and the replaceAsync flow (357-397) never call play(), and the resume seek (use-resume-prompt.ts:106) only seeks. The only play() calls are the user-driven PlayerScreen.tsx:237 and replay (778).
bugs.userImpact: Every time a video is opened it shows a paused frame with controls, and the user has to press Play. Combined with the first-frame bug above, audio files can never be played at all.

bugs.description: The side-strip pans start their interaction in `.onBegin` and finish it only in `.onEnd` (brightness 139-147, volume 163-171). RNGH calls onBegin on touch-down, before activation, but calls onEnd only for gestures that became ACTIVE. A tap or horizontal swipe on the right 25% strip therefore runs onVolumePanBegin: refresh() then showHud sets the HUD visible (use-player-side-gestures.ts:148-156). onVolumePanEnd, and so scheduleHide, never runs, and activeKindRef stays 'volume'. The strips also have no Tap gesture, so single taps there never toggle controls. startLevelRef is shared by brightness and volume and assigned asynchronously after refresh() (118-121, 152-155), so the first onUpdate events can use the previous gesture's start level.
bugs.userImpact: Tapping near the right edge makes the volume HUD appear and stay on screen. Tapping the outer half of the video does nothing to the controls, and a volume swipe can jump the device volume at its start.

bugs.description: The completed state is inconsistent after the end of the video. completionEmittedRef is only reset by replay, retry or a new resolve (769, 786, 277). After playToEnd sets isCompleted (686-694), rewind-10 and double-tap (PlayerScreen.tsx:247-261, 323-333) call seekBy without clearing isCompleted. ExoPlayer keeps playWhenReady=true and resumes, while the UI still shows the Replay button and controls are pinned (controls-visibility.ts:27). Scrubbing clears isCompleted (800), but the second playToEnd is ignored at 681. That leaves a Play button whose play() does nothing in STATE_ENDED (expo-video VideoModule.kt:259-262), and expo-video reports ENDED as 'idle', which the session ignores.
bugs.userImpact: After a video ends, rewinding shows Replay while it plays with the controls stuck on screen. Scrubbing back and letting it end again leaves a Play button that does nothing.

bugs.description: The timeline dock is a flex sibling rendered below the `stage` view (flex:1, styles 579-582), and only while controls are visible. Each show/hide changes the stage height, so VideoView re-lays out and rescales, and onSurfaceLayout updates surfaceHeight (385-389).
bugs.userImpact: The video visibly jumps and resizes every time the controls appear or auto-hide after 3s, in both inline and fullscreen modes.

bugs.description: When the native module is available, the mute button (PlayerScreen.tsx:268-275) calls usePlayerVolume.toggleMute, which sets the device STREAM_MUSIC volume to 0 (VidoraMediaVolumeModule.kt:57-80). Meanwhile PlayerScreen forces the player's own volume back to 1 (128-133). Because applySnapshot also runs maybeBoundaryHaptic (57), haptics fire on hardware volume-key changes. writingRef (97-102) is a single boolean cleared by the first write that resolves while later writes are still in flight, so broadcast snapshots overwrite the level mid-drag.
bugs.userImpact: Tapping mute in the player silences the whole phone's media volume, and it stays at 0 after leaving the player. The volume icon jitters during swipes, and stray haptic ticks happen when the user presses hardware volume keys.

bugs.description: refresh is memoized on [control, level], and `useEffect(() => void refresh(), [refresh])` (51-53) plus the AppState subscription (55-62) re-run on every level change. During a pan this fires Brightness.getBrightnessAsync() for every update, racing the in-flight setBrightnessAsync. Separately, the session re-renders the whole screen every 350ms through timeUpdate (use-player-session.ts:648). usePlayerSession is not auto-memoized because the React Compiler skips it (eslint react-hooks/immutability errors at 273 and 357). setLevel and showHud each call their own maybeBoundaryHaptic copy, giving double haptic ticks. ESLint reports 6 errors in this scope.
bugs.userImpact: Extra native calls and re-renders during playback and gestures cause possible HUD and brightness jitter and double haptic ticks at 0/50/100%. This is latent today because brightness is disabled by the permission bug.

bugs.description: onFirstFrameRender is a one-shot event: expo-video deduplicates it per media item in FirstFrameEventGenerator.kt:79-86. markFirstFrameRendered drops it unless loadArmedRef is true (214-225), and loadArmedRef is only set after `await player.replaceAsync` resolves. Ordering normally holds, because Android resolves the promise right after prepare(). But there is no fallback, such as re-checking `player.status` or a timeout, if the event is ever dropped.
bugs.userImpact: A rare but unrecoverable 'Preparing' cover if the first-frame event lands before the load is armed.

bugs.description: getAdapter() re-requires the MMKV helper modules on every read and write (31-63). If getMmkvInstance() returns null it silently switches to a process-local Map, so progress is 'saved' but lost on restart with no warning.
bugs.userImpact: In environments where MMKV init fails, watch progress and Continue Watching silently disappear after an app restart.

bugs.description: Several user-facing strings are hard-coded English: 'Speed'/'Muted' (484-485), the SeekFeedback accessibility labels (SeekFeedback.tsx:53) and the PlayerAdjustmentHud labels (54-55). The speed label is also shown twice: PlayerControls.tsx:120-124 and the dock caption. The double-tap feedback timer (PlayerScreen.tsx:335-341) does not restart on repeated same-side taps and shows no cumulative seek amount. player-chrome.runtime.ts:49/60 uses NavigationBar.setVisibilityAsync, which is deprecated in expo-navigation-bar 57.
bugs.userImpact: Unlocalized text, cluttered duplicated labels, and double-tap feedback that disappears while the user keeps tapping.

overEngineering.description: Seven overlapping mechanisms (resolveGenRef, armedGenerationRef, loadArmedRef, firstFrameAcceptedGenRef, lastAssignedUriRef/lastAssignedGenerationRef, mountedRef, a `cancelled` closure flag) plus session-generation.ts. They guard against media switches that cannot happen, because the route id is fixed for the screen's lifetime and a new item pushes a new screen. isCurrentPlayerSession is always called with capturedGeneration and currentGeneration both set to resolveGenRef.current (540-546, 589-597, 631-638, 669-677), so the generation check compares a value with itself.

A hasFirstFrame + isSurfaceRevealed two-step with an injectable requestAnimationFrame scheduler, a FirstFrameStartupPhase enum that is never used, and exports like shouldRevealSurfaceInSameTurnAsFirstFrameEvent() { return false }. All of it sits on top of expo-video's own FirstFrameEventGenerator, which already waits for the SurfaceView layout, and it creates the audio-only deadlock.

A PlayerEngineAdapter plus a PlayerController with a disposed guard, wrapping one-line expo-video property sets. Because externalLifecycle is true, dispose() just pauses. The raw player is still passed to VideoView and used directly throughout the session hook, so the 'UI must not call engine methods' boundary is not real.
A 57-line class with injectable timers around a single setTimeout. It is also cleared at the wrong moment (readyToPlay), so it does not cover the real stuck case.

Module-global singletons with injectable adapters, transitionGen counters, and activeLock/immersive flags that no app code reads (getOrientationLockKind and isSystemBarsImmersive are only exported). Add a pure enter/exit phase machine whose `phase` PlayerScreen never uses. About 250 lines for 'lock landscape + hide bars, then restore'.
configureResolvePlaybackSourceDeps and a lazily bound runtime file exist only so Node verify scripts can import the resolver without native modules.

overEngineering.area: PlaybackPersistenceCoordinator + event bus + binder (src/playback/coordinator.ts, bind-playback-persistence.ts, player/playback-events.ts, domain/reconcile.ts, domain/merge.ts)
overEngineering.description: A 969-line cloud-sync coordinator: client revisions, in-flight coalescing, retry on 401/403/404/409, reconnect waves capped at 25, remote reconcile with replay-downgrade rules, and resetForLogout in an app that has no auth. Production binds sync: null and no network subscription (bind-playback-persistence.ts:79,85), and setSyncTransport has zero callers, so runRemoteSync, reconcilePendingOnReconnect and scheduleRemoteSync (~450 lines) are unreachable. The actual job is 'save {position, duration, completed, lastPlayedAt} for an id every few seconds and on pause/exit'.

A pending/resume/start_over/dismissed state machine with chooseResume, chooseStartOver, dismiss and resumeLabel, all kept for a Resume sheet that was removed (ResumePlaybackSheet is unused and PlayerScreen ignores the return value). What remains is 'seek once to the saved position when ready'.

maybeBoundaryHaptic is copied three times (use-player-side-gestures.ts:32, use-player-volume.ts:13, use-player-brightness.ts:8). brightnessFromSwipe duplicates levelFromSwipeDelta. formatPlaybackTime exists in both src/player/format-time.ts and src/playback/domain/format.ts.

src/player/index.ts exports ~100 symbols, largely for Node verify scripts ('Node verify safety'). 27 verify scripts import player/playback internals. The player-specific ones mostly assert source text: verify-player-first-frame-stability.ts has 41 `.includes(` checks on file contents. They pin implementation details instead of behaviour.

scripts/apply-player-native-modules.js copies byte-identical Kotlin from native/android/player into the committed android/ tree and string-patches MainApplication.kt, which already registers the package. It is redundant today and fragile after `expo prebuild --clean`.

deadCode: src/screens/player/components/ResumePlaybackSheet.tsx — zero importers
src/playback/use-resume-prompt.ts return surface (visible, resumeLabel, candidate, decision, chooseResume, chooseStartOver, dismiss) — PlayerScreen ignores the return value

src/player/first-frame-state.ts: shouldShowStartupCoverWhileBuffering, shouldRevealSurfaceInSameTurnAsFirstFrameEvent (returns false), resetFirstFrameForNewSource, initialStartupRevealState, the FirstFrameStartupPhase type — used only by scripts/verify-player-first-frame-stability.ts or nowhere
src/player/session-generation.ts — its generation comparison is a no-op as called

src/playback/coordinator.ts remote path: runRemoteSync (728-968), reconcilePendingOnReconnect (456-556), scheduleRemoteSync (669-698), setSyncTransport, resetForLogout, getActiveState — unreachable because production binds sync: null and no network subscription
src/playback/domain/reconcile.ts and the remote DTO half of domain/merge.ts (fromRemote, remoteDtoToSummary, mergePlaybackSummariesByMediaId) — always called with remote=null
src/playback/persistence.ts migratePlaybackKeysToLocalNamespace — one-time cloud-namespace migration from the old auth era, run on every boot and short-circuited by a flag
src/playback/hooks.ts: usePlaybackDetail and resolvePlaybackSummary have no consumers; usePlaybackHistoryInfiniteQuery pretends to be infinite (hasNextPage false)
src/playback/constants.ts: PLAYBACK_BACKEND_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS, PLAYBACK_RECONNECT_SYNC_BATCH_LIMIT, PLAYBACK_CLIENT_TIMESTAMP_MAX_FUTURE_MS — only used by the dead sync path
src/player/types.ts: PlayerSessionState.fullscreen (never updated), errorMessage (UI uses localizePlayerError instead)
src/player/errors.ts: titleForPlayerError and the English USER_MESSAGES/ERROR_TITLES — superseded by localization
src/player/use-player-session.ts: exported mute/unmute (only toggleMute is used)
src/player/player-controller.ts: PlayerEngineAdapter.seekBy and release (the controller never calls them)
src/player/orientation-controller.ts getOrientationLockKind, src/player/system-bars.ts isSystemBarsImmersive, and the reset*ForTests helpers

src/player/app-lifecycle-policy.ts shouldTreatAsBackground; src/player/level-gesture.ts levelFromTapY and clampLevel; src/player/double-tap-seek.ts resolveDoubleTapSide; src/player/gesture-zones.ts resolveSideGestureZone — app code never calls them
src/player/adapters/android-media-volume.adapter.ts isAndroidMediaVolumeAvailable; src/player/resolve-playback-source.runtime.ts resetPlaybackSourceRuntimeBinding
src/player/fullscreen-state.ts `phase` field — returned by useFullscreenLifecycle but unused
native/android/player/VidoraMediaVolumeModule.kt and PlayerNativePackage.kt — byte-identical duplicates of the committed android/ copies
scripts/apply-player-native-modules.js — redundant postinstall step (package already registered)

Verify scripts that exist to exercise this subsystem: scripts/verify-player-first-frame-stability.ts, verify-player-level-controls.ts, verify-player-chrome-features.ts, verify-resume-regressions.ts, verify-week8-day2-stage1/2/3.ts, verify-week8-day3-phase1/2/3.ts, verify-playback-sync-final.ts (27 scripts in total reference player/playback)
capabilityGaps: No autoplay on open, and no 'autoplay next' when a video ends.
No next/previous or queue: openPlayer(mediaId) carries a single id and the player has no notion of library, history or folder ordering.

No Picture-in-Picture. app.json lists the expo-video plugin without supportsPictureInPicture, VideoView sets no allowsPictureInPicture or startsPictureInPictureAutomatically, and the session force-pauses on background, which would kill PiP anyway.
No background audio or lock-screen/notification media controls: staysActiveInBackground, showNowPlayingNotification and the plugin's supportsBackgroundPlayback are all unused.

No subtitle or audio-track selection, even though expo-video 57 exposes availableSubtitleTracks/subtitleTrack and availableAudioTracks/audioTrack. No sidecar subtitle loading either (the v57 API support for external tracks needs checking).
No audio-only playback UI. The download pipeline produces audio-only files, but the player deadlocks on them.
No handling of formats the device cannot decode beyond a generic error plus 'Open with'. The resolved mimeType is ignored and there is no codec pre-check or explanation.
No working brightness gesture on Android (permission bug), and window brightness is not restored with restoreSystemBrightnessAsync.

No aspect/zoom control (contentFit fixed to 'contain'), no pinch-to-zoom/fill, no screen lock mode, no long-press 2x speed, no horizontal swipe-to-seek. Double-tap seek only works in the centre 50% of the width.
No auto-fullscreen on landscape rotation; the orientation preference resets every session (restoreOrientation sets DEFAULT).
No per-video or global persisted playback speed, and no seek-preview thumbnails (expo-video has generateThumbnailsAsync).
No real automated tests. There are no jest/RNTL tests for the session, gesture or persistence behaviour; the verify scripts mostly grep source text.
audits.crossSubsystemCoupling:
INBOUND (callers):
- openPlayer(mediaId) (src/navigation/helpers/open-player.ts) is used by LibraryScreen/useLibraryScreen, ContinueWatchingSection, HomeRecentlyWatched, HomeRecentDownloads, HomeContinueWatching, WatchHistoryScreen and DownloadDetailsScreen.
- playerPath(id) is also produced by downloads/completed-file/action-service.ts playCompletedFile.
- Contract to preserve: the route `/player/[id]` where id is the downloadId.

PLAYBACK DATA CONSUMERS:
- useContinueWatchingQuery and useRecentPlaybackQuery (useHomeDashboard, useLibraryScreen).
- usePlaybackHistoryInfiniteQuery (WatchHistoryScreen).
- enrichLibraryWithPlayback and buildPlaybackSummaryMap (useLibraryScreen).
- isContinueWatchingEligible (home-derive, useLibraryScreen).
- formatResumeLabel (home-derive, ContinueWatchingSection).
- Contracts to preserve: the MMKV key format `vidorax.playback.v1:local:<mediaId>`, the PlaybackState/PlaybackSummary shape, and invalidation of the react-query ['playback'] keys on save boundaries. The coordinator, event bus and binder are internal and can be swapped freely; bootstrap loads them through guarded dynamic imports (app-initializer.ts:75-78, 177-181).

OUTBOUND (dependencies):
- The resolver depends on the downloads engine (getLocalRecord, assessLocalFile, verifyCompletedFile, assertManagedDownloadPath), useDownloadsStore (title/mimeType), and the library (invalidateLibraryAvailability, reconcileAvailability, isCompletedStatus, isTempOrWorkspaceArtifact, normalizeMimeType, resolveDisplayName). This is the only tight coupling, and it is correct.
- The error screen uses downloads/completed-file/action-service openCompletedFile ('Open with'), localization localizePlayerError (keyed by PlayerErrorCode) and support getPlayerSupportContext (keyed by PlayerErrorCode).

NATIVE: MainApplication.kt registers PlayerNativePackage, which only the volume hook uses.

VERIFY SCRIPTS: 27 scripts import player/playback internals and would break. That is acceptable; they should be deleted with the old code.

REPLACEMENT RISK: Low as long as four things stay stable: the route shape, the PlayerErrorCode names (or the localization/support mapping), the playback storage format, and the react-query invalidation. Nothing outside the player imports use-player-session, the first-frame/generation logic, the fullscreen/orientation singletons, or the gesture hooks.

publicInterfaces.name: openPlayer(mediaId)
publicInterfaces.usedBy: LibraryScreen/useLibraryScreen, ContinueWatchingSection, HomeRecentlyWatched, HomeRecentDownloads, HomeContinueWatching, WatchHistoryScreen, DownloadDetailsScreen

audits.recommendations:
TARGET: one feature folder of about 10 files and roughly 1,000 lines, built directly on expo-video SDK 57, with no event bus, dependency-injection seams or module-global singletons.

1. src/features/player/PlayerScreen.tsx (~200 lines)
- Read the id, then `const src = usePlaybackSource(id)`. That hook wraps the existing resolveSourceresolvePlaybackSource logic with direct imports and returns {uri, title, mimeType, isAudio} or a PlayerErrorCode.
- Read the saved state synchronously: `loadPlaybackState('local', id)`.
- Create the player: `useVideoPlayer(src ? {uri: src.uri, metadata:{title}} : null, p => { p.timeUpdateEventInterval = 0.5; p.showNowPlayingNotification = true; p.staysActiveInBackground = settings.backgroundAudio; })`.
- On the first `statusChange` to readyToPlay:
  - if isResumeEligible(saved), set `p.currentTime = saved.positionSeconds`;
  - call `p.play()` (autoplay).
- Derive coarse state with `useEvent(player, 'statusChange' | 'playingChange')` from 'expo'.
- Keep position in a ref, plus a throttled or Reanimated shared value for the timeline, so the screen does not re-render 3x/s.
- Error UI: keep today's (localized, Retry, 'Open with').

2. usePlaybackProgress(player, mediaId) (~80 lines), replacing coordinator.ts, playback-events.ts, bind-playback-persistence.ts, reconcile.ts and the migration.
- On timeUpdate, store lastPositionRef and lastDurationRef.
- Call savePlaybackState('local', …) every 5s while playing, on playingChange(false), on AppState background, and on playToEnd with completed:true.
- On unmount, save using lastPositionRef and NEVER read `player` in cleanup. This fixes the reset-to-0 bug.
- Set lastPlayedAt on first play.
- Invalidate ['playback'] queries on pause, exit and complete.
- Keep the key format and PlaybackState JSON; keep domain/progress, completion, resume and continue-watching as they are.

3. Startup cover
- Show it only while status is 'loading' and there has been neither readyToPlay nor a first frame.
- Dismiss it on onFirstFrameRender OR readyToPlay+300ms OR audio-only (src.isAudio, or `player.availableVideoTracks.length === 0` at the `sourceLoad` event). Show an audio artwork/waveform layout for audio.
- Never gate controls on the first frame. Apply a 12s timeout only while status stays 'loading'.

4. PlayerOverlay.tsx
- Put the top bar, centre controls and bottom timeline all in one absoluteFill layer over the VideoView, faded with Reanimated opacity and `pointerEvents` toggling. Do not mount/unmount, so there is no layout shift.
- Auto-hide with a ~30-line useAutoHide(isPlaying, isScrubbing, sheetOpen) hook that keeps the ControlsVisibilityController semantics.
- Mute sets `player.muted`, not system volume. Put speed and subtitles/audio tracks into one settings sheet built from player.availableSubtitleTracks/availableAudioTracks.

5. usePlayerGestures (one GestureDetector over the whole surface)
- `Gesture.Race(pan, Gesture.Exclusive(doubleTap, singleTap))`.
- doubleTap: x < width/2 seeks -10s, otherwise +10s, with cumulative '+20s' feedback that resets its timer on each tap.
- singleTap toggles the overlay.
- pan decides its axis in onStart:
  - vertical on the left half: window brightness via `Brightness.setBrightnessAsync` with NO permission request, and `Brightness.restoreSystemBrightnessAsync()` on blur/unmount;
  - vertical on the right half: device volume through the kept VidoraMediaVolume module;
  - horizontal: scrub seek with a preview.
- Use onStart/onUpdate/onFinalize, not onBegin/onEnd. Keep the HUD in shared values and use one haptic helper.
- Optional: long-press for 2x speed and pinch to toggle contentFit contain/cover.

6. useImmersiveFullscreen (~60 lines)
- Keep today's approach: ScreenOrientation.lockAsync(LANDSCAPE) + NavigationBar.setHidden(true) + setStatusBarHidden(true), with restore in useFocusEffect cleanup and on error.
- Auto-enter when the device rotates to landscape (ScreenOrientation.addOrientationChangeListener).
- Drop fullscreen-state.ts, orientation-controller.ts, system-bars.ts and player-chrome.runtime.ts.

7. PiP and background
- app.json: `["expo-video", {"supportsPictureInPicture": true, "supportsBackgroundPlayback": true}]`.
- VideoView: `allowsPictureInPicture startsPictureInPictureAutomatically`. Hide the overlay on onPictureInPictureStart.
- On AppState background, pause only when neither PiP nor background audio is active.

8. Queue / next-previous
- A tiny zustand `playQueue` store ({ids, index}) set by the list screen before navigating, e.g. `openPlayer(id, {queueIds})`.
- Next/prev buttons plus optional autoplay-next on playToEnd use `player.replaceAsync` + `router.setParams({id})`, so the same screen and VideoView are reused.

9. Completion
- Derive `isEnded` from playToEnd, and clear it on any seek or play.
- Make Play at the end call `player.replay()`, which exists on Android in expo-video 57 (VideoModule.kt:329-334).

10. Native module
- Move VidoraMediaVolumeModule into a local Expo module (modules/vidorax-media-volume with expo-module.config.json) so autolinking survives prebuild.
- Delete native/android/player and scripts/apply-player-native-modules.js.

11. Delete
- session-generation.ts, first-frame-state.ts, preparation-watchdog.ts, player-controller.ts, resolve-playback-source.runtime.ts DI, playback-events.ts, coordinator.ts, bind-playback-persistence.ts, domain/reconcile.ts, the remote half of merge.ts, the cloud migration (after one more release that still runs it), use-resume-prompt.ts, ResumePlaybackSheet.tsx, the player/index.ts barrel, and the related verify scripts.
- Keep: media-id.ts, errors.ts codes, seek/format-time/playback-rates helpers, the playback domain rules, and PlayerTimeline's scrub logic (restyled for the overlay).

12. Tests
- Add jest + @testing-library/react-native with a fake expo-video player (an event emitter with currentTime/status).
- Test usePlaybackProgress: saves on pause and unmount, never saves 0 after a release, marks completed.
- Test resume/autoplay ordering, gesture axis and zone math, and the pure domain rules.
- Run everything against docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0/sdk/video before merging.

audits.subsystem: ui-core (src/app, navigation, providers, bootstrap, theme, components, hooks, constants, api, screens/downloads, screens/home, screens/settings, package.json deps)
audits.purpose: This subsystem is the app shell. It holds the expo-router route tree and the root provider stack. It runs the startup sequence, which initializes stores, SQLite, the download engine and notifications, then shows a branded splash and three onboarding pages before the Browser tab. It also owns the theme and component design system, and the Downloads (list, queue, details), Settings and legacy Home screens. It hosts the shared "quality selection" sheet, which turns an analyzed media result into a download job for the Browser tab. src/api no longer talks to any backend. It is a leftover DTO and type file that now serves as the domain model for downloads.
audits.architecture:
ENTRY: package.json main -> src/entry.js. Before expo-router boots it imports three modules:
- bootstrap/configure-storage.ts (Zustand persist adapter: MMKV, falling back to AsyncStorage, then in-memory).
- bootstrap/defer-initial-linking.ts (monkeypatches RN Linking.getInitialURL).
- bootstrap/patch-expo-router-linking.ts (mutates the internal CJS module 'expo-router/build/link/linking').
Then src/app/+native-intent.ts delays the initial path by a triple requestAnimationFrame (after-navigation-ready.ts).

ROOT: src/app/_layout.tsx wraps everything in AppProvider (providers/app-provider.tsx:52-79). That is 11 nested wrappers:
- GestureHandlerRootView, SafeAreaProvider, ErrorBoundary
- QueryProvider (react-query, used only by 4 local playback hooks)
- AppInitializerProvider, LocalizationProvider
- SessionProvider (does nothing)
- AppLaunchGate (hides the native splash once fonts and init are ready)
- AppPaperProvider plus Portal.Host, NavigationThemeProvider
- BottomSheetModalProvider (gorhom; nothing uses it)
RootNavigator renders Stack[(auth),(app)] and InitialRouteRedirect. unstable_settings.initialRouteName is '(auth)' (navigation/config/initial-route.ts:4).

BOOTSTRAP: hooks/use-app-initializer.ts -> bootstrap/app-initializer.ts:40-213. It awaits about 15 steps in series:
- rehydrate app, theme and settings stores (the settings store twice)
- initializeSqlite, syncAppStoreFromDisk, hydrateDownloadSettings, MMKV sync
- playback key migration, SecureStore auth-secret cleanup
- catalog seed, favorites cache, first page of downloads from SQLite
- bindDownloadEngineToStore, recovery listener, notification bridge, library bridge, playback persistence, reconcilePendingExports
Then appStore.initialize() runs, and the function always returns '/splash' (resolve-initial-route.ts:7).

GROUPS:
- (auth)/_layout: splash, then onboarding. OnboardingRouteGuard never skips; the sequence replays on every cold start.
- (app)/_layout: ProtectedRouteGuard (blank View until initialized), then AppLockGate (security), then a Stack of 18 registered screens with memoized header options.
- (app)/(tabs)/_layout: QualitySelectionProvider wraps Tabs [browser, downloads, library, settings, plus a hidden index that redirects to /browser]. It also calls useTabExitBackHandler.

DOWNLOAD SHEET (state owner):
- screens/downloads/quality/QualitySelectionProvider.tsx is a singleton at the tab root. It owns useQualitySelection.ts (856 lines: URL validation, direct vs page classification, page-resolution sessions, SPA freeze/epoch checks, pre-download gate plus refresh/regate, social identity keys, store.create). It renders QualitySelectionSheet (an RN Modal).
- It talks to the Browser through module-level buses (download-created-bus.ts, browser-load-bridge.ts) and reaches directly into browser stores/services and media-detection services.

DOWNLOADS:
- DownloadsScreen -> useDownloadsScreen (store via storage/hooks useDownloads) -> DownloadsList (SectionList or FlatList) -> DownloadCard (per-id Zustand selectors).
- QueueScreen -> useQueueScreen (downloadEngine.subscribeQueue).
- DownloadDetailsScreen (1240 lines, 17 useState) -> useDownloadDetailsScreen, plus inline folder CRUD, file rename, file-actions sheet and favorites.

SETTINGS: SettingsScreen, 7 sections. useSettingsScreen runs a serialized promise queue around synchronous Zustand writes in services/auth/settings.service.ts. DownloadSettingsScreen -> useDownloadSettingsScreen.

THEME:
- src/theme: colors.ts (light/logo/dark palettes), typography.ts (Inter/Poppins), spacing, radius, elevation, icons, opacity. useTheme reads the Zustand theme store.
- Extras: intro-palette, onboarding-surfaces, startup-theme (MMKV read before first paint), contrast.ts, a Paper MD3 theme mapping (providers/paper-theme.ts), and 7 per-screen token files (about 390 lines total) that mostly re-alias theme tokens.

COMPONENTS:
- base: Box, Text, Pressable, and Icon (renders through react-native-paper's Icon, i.e. MaterialCommunityIcons).
- Buttons: Button, IconButton.
- Overlays: ActionSheetModal (RN Modal, unmounted when hidden), AppModal (Paper Portal wrapped around an RN Modal), ConfirmModal.
- Layout and states: SafeAreaScreen/Screen, ScreenHeader, EmptyState, ErrorState, Skeleton, ProgressBar, inputs.

NAVIGATION: 40+ files.
- In use: route constants (route-paths, route-names), navigation.ts and safe-navigation.ts (router wrappers with fallback), open-player.ts, the guards, and the back-handler hooks.
- Mostly dead: route-access lists, route-groups, modules/* route maps, linking.ts, deep-link.ts, startup-splash-sequence.ts.

API: src/api/types.ts has 85 exported types; only 21 are used outside src/api (DownloadItem, DownloadStatus, MediaAnalysisResult and similar, across 40 importers). src/api/errors.ts defines ApiError, which is never constructed.
audits.endToEndTrace:
FLOW 1: COLD START
1. entry.js:8-11 installs two linking monkeypatches. _layout.tsx:22 calls preventAutoHideAsync.
2. AppProvider -> use-app-initializer.ts:20 -> runAppInitializer. The initial URL is the root '/' (expo-router/build/link/linking.js:77 getRootURL).
3. Because root initialRouteName is '(auth)' (_layout.tsx:24, initial-route.ts:4), expo-router's getStateFromPath inserts the (auth) route underneath the matched (app) route (fork/getStateFromPath.js findInitialRoute/createStateObject). The (auth) stack, and therefore SplashScreen with its own exit timer, is likely mounted underneath.
4. (app)/_layout ProtectedRouteGuard.tsx:38-45 shows a blank View.
5. app-initializer.ts:208 calls appStore.initialize() BEFORE the promise resolves. The guard opens, (tabs)/index.tsx:10 <Redirect href="/browser"> fires, and BrowserScreen plus its WebView mount.
6. Then isReady flips. InitialRouteRedirect.tsx:41 calls replace('/splash'), tearing (app) back down.
7. SplashScreen.tsx:60-66 waits minVisibleMs 3600 + holdAtComplete 250 (timings.ts:27-30), plays a 750 ms exit, then calls router.replace('/onboarding') (SplashScreen.tsx:52; resolve-post-splash-route.ts:17 is unconditional).
8. OnboardingScreen.tsx:64-74 requires Continue x3 or Skip, then :47 replace('/browser').
Where it is fragile: several competing replace() calls, a splash probably mounted underneath with its own timer, and monkeypatches of expo-router internals that exist to suppress mount-race warnings. It costs about 4.6 s plus taps on every launch. Code-traced; confirm on device.

FLOW 2: DOWNLOAD FROM BROWSER
1. BrowserScreen.tsx:156-175 handleRequestDownload -> useQualitySelection.openWithAnalysis (:487) or openWithUrl (:520).
2. runAnalyze (:348). For a direct URL: analyzeMediaUrl -> applyAnalysis (:331). applyAnalysis runs selectVerifiedStandaloneQualities (:333), which silently drops any variant that needs muxing, so many social videos land in phase 'empty'.
3. For a page URL: startPageMediaResolution -> onPageResolutionHandoff, which navigates to the Browser (QualitySelectionProvider.tsx:52-66). Later usePendingMediaResolution.onResolved (:76-101) -> openWithAnalysis or browserMediaActionService.handoffVerified.
4. Confirm -> confirmDownload (:617) -> isQualityFreezeStillCurrent (:80-112) -> runPreDownloadGate (:676) -> refreshMediaFromPage and regate on a refreshable failure (:683-732) -> useDownloadsStore.create (:790) -> onDownloadCreated -> notifyQualitySelectionDownloadCreated.
5. Two listeners receive it: useBrowserMediaAction.ts:180 (marks the CTA consumed) and DownloadsScreen.tsx:58 (toast).
6. Then close({consumed:true}) (:809).
Where it breaks: the only visible success toast lives in the Downloads tab screen, not in the Browser where the user tapped. It is hidden, or never registered if Downloads was never opened.

FLOW 3: "PASTE LINK" FROM DOWNLOADS
1. The DownloadsScreen.tsx:200-208 header button, labelled 'Paste link' (en.ts:428), and the empty-state CTA (:262-266) call qualitySelection.open.
2. useQualitySelection.ts:289-292 only runs navigation.navigate('/browser'). Nothing is pasted or analyzed.
3. The sheet's URL input (QualitySelectionSheet.tsx:314-383) is reachable only after a failed analyze. Its footer "Open Browser" button (:128-141) only calls close().

FLOW 4: DOWNLOADS LIST -> DETAILS
1. DownloadsList -> DownloadCard.onPress -> useDownloadsScreen.openDetails (:376) -> push /downloads/:id.
2. useDownloadDetailsScreen.ts:51-153 reads the store and runs fetchOne.
3. runAction (:277) handles pause/resume/cancel/retry/open/share. 'remove' opens DownloadDeleteDialog -> confirmDelete (:337) -> remove -> goBack.
4. Folder picker, manage folders and rename are inline in DownloadDetailsScreen.tsx:587-869 and 1014-1237.
5. If the item leaves the store after load, status falls through to 'loading' (:449).

FLOW 5: ANDROID BACK ON THE BROWSER TAB
1. TabsLayout useTabExitBackHandler ((tabs)/_layout.tsx:31; use-tab-exit-back-handler.ts:15-34) and BrowserScreen useBrowserHardwareBack (BrowserScreen.tsx:145; useBrowserHardwareBack.ts:38-41) both register through useAndroidBackHandler, which uses useFocusEffect -> React.useEffect (expo-router/build/react-navigation/core/useFocusEffect.js:61).
2. Both hooks gate `enabled` on the same pathname, so they re-register in the same commit. Child effects run before parent effects, so the TabsLayout handler is added last.
3. RN BackHandler calls the last-registered handler first (BackHandler.android.js:30).
4. On /browser the tab-exit handler always returns true. goBackForTab never runs: the user sees 'Press back again to exit' on any web page, and a second press exits the app.
audits.verdictRationale:
Worth keeping: the presentational layer.
- The base primitives (Box, Text, Pressable, Button, IconButton) are small and token-driven, and handle RTL and accessibility. About 140 files use them.
- ActionSheetModal and ConfirmModal work around Android's transparent-Modal touch bug by unmounting when hidden.
- The Downloads list, card and queue are well built: per-id store subscriptions, tuned FlatList settings, expo-image recycling, and a thin queue observer.
- Route files in src/app are 1 to 10 lines each.

Needs a rewrite or deletion: the shell and controller code around that layer. It is over-engineered and broken in user-visible ways.
1. Every cold start forces about 4.6 s of splash plus three onboarding pages.
2. Startup routing fights itself: an index redirect, InitialRouteRedirect, a splash mounted underneath via initialRouteName, and three monkeypatches of RN/expo-router internals to hide the resulting races.
3. Hardware back on the Browser tab is taken by the tab-exit handler, so web back-navigation never runs.
4. "Paste link" silently switches tabs instead of pasting.
5. The download success toast renders on a different tab from where the user tapped Download.
6. useQualitySelection is an 856-line hook fusing UI state with browser/SPA freeze logic.
7. DownloadDetailsScreen is 1240 lines with folder management bolted on.

Dead weight:
- Most of navigation/ is unused (modules, linking, deep-link, guards, splash-sequence helpers).
- About 10 components have no importers.
- src/screens/home (1583 lines) is unreachable.
- 64 of 85 src/api types are unused, and ApiError is never constructed.
- @expo/ui, react-hook-form, @hookform/resolvers, zod, expo-symbols and expo-web-browser have no importers; @gorhom/bottom-sheet is only wired to unused code.

Lint in this scope: 2 errors and 3 warnings. The code saturates manual memo/useCallback even though React Compiler is enabled. There are no tests, only verify scripts.

keepWorthy.why: Small, token-driven, RTL-aware primitives with a sensible prop API. About 140 files depend on them. Easy to keep as the design-system foundation.
Consistent variants and sizes, loading and disabled states, and correct accessibilityState. Reused widely.
A simple, controlled RN Modal sheet that unmounts when hidden, avoiding Android's transparent-Modal touch interception. It is the right replacement for gorhom here.
A clean confirm dialog API. Only its base AppModal needs the Paper Portal wrapper removed.

keepWorthy.file: src/components/common/EmptyState.tsx, ErrorState.tsx, ProgressBar.tsx, Skeleton.tsx, SafeAreaScreen.tsx; src/components/headers/ScreenHeader.tsx; src/components/common/error-boundary.tsx
keepWorthy.why: Widely used, simple building blocks for consistent screen states and headers.

keepWorthy.file: src/theme/colors.ts, spacing.ts, radius.ts, typography.ts, index.ts, src/hooks/use-theme.ts
keepWorthy.why: A coherent, small token set with a single theme source (the Zustand store). Palettes can be trimmed, but the structure is right.

Each card subscribes to its own item and transfer by id, so progress ticks don't re-render siblings. The FlatList/SectionList is tuned and uses expo-image recyclingKey and disk cache. The layout needs simplifying, but the performance pattern is correct.
A thin observer of the engine's queue snapshot. It never starts workers, derives actions from resolveDownloadRuntimeActions, and is easy to reason about.
One place for navigation calls, with safe fallbacks and typed path builders (downloadDetailsPath, playerPath). Small and used everywhere.
Thin 1-10 line route files that delegate to screens, which is the right expo-router pattern to keep.
Small, defensive and correct. Persist-adapter selection with a hydration timeout is reasonable startup plumbing.

bugs.description: Two global BackHandler listeners compete: the TabsLayout tab-exit handler (src/app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:31) and BrowserScreen's useBrowserHardwareBack (src/browser/BrowserScreen.tsx:145). Both register through useFocusEffect -> useEffect, gated on the same pathname, so they re-register in the same commit. Parent effects run after child effects, so the tab-exit handler is registered last. RN BackHandler invokes the last-registered handler first (node_modules/react-native/Libraries/Utilities/BackHandler.android.js:30). On /browser the tab-exit handler always returns true (lines 17-31), so goBackForTab never runs. Code-traced; confirm on device.
bugs.userImpact: Pressing Android back on any web page in the in-app browser does not go back. It shows 'Press back again to exit', and a second press closes the app. This breaks basic browsing on the core tab.

bugs.description: Every cold start is routed to /splash (resolve-initial-route.ts:7), then unconditionally to /onboarding, whose guard deliberately never skips (OnboardingRouteGuard.tsx:10-30). The splash enforces minVisibleMs 3600 + holdAtComplete 250 + a 750 ms exit (screens/splash/animations/timings.ts:27-30; SplashScreen.tsx:60-66). Onboarding then needs Continue x3 or Skip (OnboardingScreen.tsx:64-74). A persisted onboardingComplete flag is ignored by design.
bugs.userImpact: About 5 seconds plus at least one tap before the browser is usable, on every app launch, including when the user just wants to download a copied link.

bugs.description: Cold-start routing race. The root URL '/' matches (tabs)/index, which redirects to /browser as soon as ProtectedRouteGuard opens. The guard opens on appStore.initialize() at bootstrap/app-initializer.ts:208, before the initializer promise resolves. Then InitialRouteRedirect.tsx:41 replaces with /splash. Also, root unstable_settings.initialRouteName '(auth)' (navigation/config/initial-route.ts:4) makes expo-router insert (auth), with SplashScreen and its self-navigating exit timer, beneath (app) in the initial state. patch-expo-router-linking.ts:28 require()s the internal module 'expo-router/build/link/linking' to suppress resulting mount-race warnings; that will break silently on a router upgrade. Code-traced; confirm on device.
bugs.userImpact: BrowserScreen and its WebView mount and are torn down on each launch, possibly with duplicate splash/onboarding transitions or flicker. Startup is slower, and future Expo upgrades risk regressions.

bugs.description: open() only calls navigation.navigate('/browser'). DownloadsScreen's header 'Paste link' button (DownloadsScreen.tsx:200-208, label en.ts:428) and the empty-state CTA (:262-266) are wired to it. No clipboard read or URL analysis happens. The sheet's URL input (QualitySelectionSheet.tsx:314-383) is only reachable after a failed analyze.
bugs.userImpact: A user with a copied Instagram or TikTok link taps 'Paste link' and lands on the browser home with nothing pasted. The most direct path to the owner's main goal doesn't exist.

bugs.description: The 'Added to Downloads' toast listener (registerQualitySelectionDownloadListener) and the toast view live inside the Downloads tab screen. Downloads are normally confirmed from the Browser tab (BrowserScreen.tsx:156-175), where the toast is not rendered. If the Downloads tab was never opened, nothing is registered at all.
bugs.userImpact: After tapping Download in the browser, the sheet closes with no visible confirmation (only a screen-reader announcement). Users can't tell whether anything happened.

bugs.description: About 15 steps are awaited in series and the whole UI stays gated until they finish: SQLite, catalog seeding, first-page list, engine binding and reconcilePendingExports (:193-196). Only the store hydration steps have a timeout (wait-for-hydration.ts:9). Every failure is caught, and the catches only console.warn under __DEV__ (:64-67, :146-150, :202-206). In a release build a failed download-engine import or bind leaves the app running with no engine and no user-visible error.
bugs.userImpact: Slow cold start that grows with library size. In release, a bootstrap failure makes downloads silently never start or progress, with nothing shown to the user.

bugs.description: The status memo falls through to 'loading' when the item is no longer in the store after the initial load (bootstrapping=false, loadError=null, missing=false). The load effect (:93-153) depends only on [downloadId, fetchOne], so it never re-checks. The same fallthrough briefly renders the skeleton during confirmDelete before goBack (:346-349).
bugs.userImpact: If a download is removed elsewhere while its details screen is open (a notification cancel, storage cleanup, the Library), the screen shows a loading skeleton forever.

bugs.description: In the idle/failed input state, the primary footer button is titled t('home.openBrowser') ('Open Browser') but its onPress only calls close(). It never navigates.
bugs.userImpact: After a failed analyze the main button just dismisses the sheet, despite its label. Retrying is only possible through the small inline error card.

bugs.description: confirmRenameFile sends the raw typed text to renameMediaFileOnDevice (downloads/engine/media-file-actions.ts:104-130 moves the file to exactly `safeName`). It then patches both fileName and title to that text. The UI does nothing to preserve the original extension. Needs a check of whether assertSafeLogicalFileName re-appends one.
bugs.userImpact: Renaming 'clip.mp4' to 'My clip' can leave a file with no extension. External open or share and the Format row then fail, and the title gets overwritten too.

bugs.description: The useState initializer calls hydrateDownloadSettings(), a store write, during render. The effect at :124 calls setState synchronously (eslint react-hooks/set-state-in-effect error). The same lint error appears in the dead src/screens/home/hooks/useHomeDashboard.ts:66. These are the 2 lint errors in this scope; React Compiler is enabled in app.json.
bugs.userImpact: Possible 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' warnings and extra renders when opening Download Settings.

bugs.description: Synchronous local Zustand writes (updateThemePreference and updateLanguagePreference in services/auth/settings.service.ts:26-34) are wrapped in a serialized promise queue that toggles `saving` and shows a success banner. `saving` disables the Appearance, General and Privacy sections (SettingsScreen.tsx:69, 81, 98).
bugs.userImpact: Every theme or language tap flashes a 'saved' banner and briefly disables the whole Settings screen, which is noisy for an instant local change.

There are hard-coded English strings in an app that ships Urdu (src/localization/ur.ts) with RTL support:
