bugs.description: A 'system' preference is collapsed to 'light' and the OS color scheme is never followed, even though app.json sets userInterfaceStyle 'automatic'. The default theme is 'logo' (white content, red chrome), but the native splash backgroundColor is #1A2517, a dark olive (app.json expo-splash-screen).
bugs.userImpact: The app ignores system dark mode. There is a visible color jump from the olive native splash to the white/red JS UI at launch.

bugs.description: An RN Modal is wrapped inside a react-native-paper Portal, so the content goes to Portal.Host at the app root and then into a native dialog as well. DownloadDetailsScreen stacks a ConfirmModal (delete folder, :1224) on top of the open manage-folders AppModal (:1085). File-actions 'Delete' (:846-851) closes one Modal and opens another in the same commit.
bugs.userImpact: Fragile dialog layering: stacked native dialogs and back-button handling across them are error-prone on Android. There is no functional reason for the Portal.

bugs.description: The duration is read via `(item as any).duration`, which suggests DownloadItem has no duration field.
bugs.userImpact: The Duration info row is most likely never shown.

overEngineering.description: Files involved: bootstrap/defer-initial-linking.ts (monkeypatches RN Linking), bootstrap/patch-expo-router-linking.ts (mutates an expo-router internal module), after-navigation-ready.ts (triple rAF), app/+native-intent.ts, InitialRouteRedirect.tsx, resolve-initial-route.ts, resolve-post-splash-route.ts, resolve-fallback-route.ts and startup-splash-sequence.ts (pure functions only referenced by verify scripts). All of it exists to force a cinematic splash through a routing setup that races itself. A native splash held until a minimal init, plus a one-time onboarding gate, would replace every one of these files.

11 nested wrappers in providers/app-provider.tsx:
- SessionProvider does nothing.
- BottomSheetModalProvider serves an unused gorhom BottomSheet.
- PaperProvider plus Portal.Host plus a 107-line MD3 theme mapping exist only so Paper's Icon, Portal and the error-fallback Button render.
- QueryProvider serves 4 local MMKV-backed playback queries.
- AppLaunchGate is just an effect.

Most of it is unused or duplicates what expo-router's file routes and typedRoutes already provide:
- route-access lists, route-groups, route-names (including a deprecated appRouteNames)
- modules/* route maps for 10 features
- linking.ts config that expo-router ignores
- deep-link.ts, get-root-group-for-route.ts, secondary-routes.ts
- GuestRouteGuard, and createModal/Push/Replace/TransparentHeaderOptions

One React hook mixes:
- sheet UI state
- URL classification and page-resolution sessions
- browser SPA freeze and navigation-epoch validation
- pre-download gate plus page refresh/regate
- social content identity keys
- store job creation
It uses module-level listener buses (download-created-bus.ts, browser-load-bridge.ts) to dodge import cycles, and the sheet reaches into browser stores from the tab root. None of it is testable without rendering, and the triple setPhase calls (:388-390, :449-453) show state-machine noise.

A details screen with 17 useState hooks that also contains a full folder manager (create/rename/delete), a file-rename dialog, a folder picker, a favorites toggle, and a file-actions menu duplicating the primary and secondary action buttons already on the screen.

On top of the core tokens there are 3 palettes (light/logo/dark), intro-palette.ts, onboarding-surfaces.ts, startup-theme.ts and contrast.ts. There are also 7 per-screen token files (downloads, settings, library, history, bookmarks, favorites, home; about 390 lines) that mostly re-alias theme.colors and spacing, making styling inconsistent across screens.

useSettingsScreen returns vestigial API-shaped fields (status, loading, refreshing, initialized, error: null) and serializes synchronous writes through a promise queue. Preference writers live in services/auth/ even though no auth exists. SettingsStaggerItem animates every section on mount. There is a whole SettingsComingSoonBadge feature that nothing uses.

app.json enables experiments.reactCompiler, yet nearly every component and hook wraps everything in memo, useCallback and useMemo. For example DownloadsScreen.tsx:105-176 has 9 trivial useCallback wrappers around void promise calls, and (app)/_layout.tsx:28-75 has 12 separate useMemo header-options objects.

bootstrap/cleanup-obsolete-auth.ts dynamically require()s MMKV flags and SecureStore to delete tokens from a removed auth system, and onboarding-persist-debug.ts async dev logging is awaited in the bootstrap, splash and onboarding paths.

deadCode: src/screens/home/** (1583 lines): HomeScreen is unreachable because (tabs)/index.tsx redirects and src/screens/index.ts has no importers. Only utils/home-derive.ts and utils/home-local-index.ts are used, by storage-manager, and should move there.
src/screens/placeholder/** and the src/screens/index.ts barrel (no importers).

src/api/types.ts: 64 of 85 exported types are unused outside src/api (all backend *Request/*Response/*Params DTOs). src/api/errors.ts ApiError is never constructed, so every isApiError branch is dead (useDownloadDetailsScreen.ts:136,359,424; screens/settings/utils/map-settings-error.ts; store/bookmarks|history|favorites actions; localization/errors.ts).

src/navigation/modules/** (10 route maps), navigation/config/linking.ts, navigation/config/modal-options.ts, navigation/helpers/deep-link.ts, get-root-group-for-route.ts, constants/secondary-routes.ts, guards/GuestRouteGuard.tsx, route-names appRouteNames, createModalScreenOptions, createPushScreenOptions, createReplaceScreenOptions, createTransparentHeaderOptions, resetNavigation, isProtectedRoute and isGuestRoute (reachable only via the dead deep-link.ts). Each is only defined and re-exported.
src/navigation/SessionProvider.tsx (returns children, no behavior).
src/navigation/helpers/startup-splash-sequence.ts: referenced only by scripts/verify-* .
src/hooks/use-color-scheme.ts and use-color-scheme.web.ts (no importers).
src/theme/contrast.ts (only used by verify scripts).
src/constants/environment.ts featureFlags (EXPO_PUBLIC_ENABLE_* never read) and src/constants/routes.ts alias.

src/components with zero importers: buttons/LoadingButton.tsx, buttons/TextButton.tsx, cards/SettingCard.tsx, cards/VideoCard.tsx, common/Badge.tsx, common/Section.tsx, headers/SearchHeader.tsx, inputs/OTPField.tsx and inputs/PasswordField.tsx (auth leftovers), bottom-sheets/BottomSheet.tsx (gorhom), and the ActionSheet component in bottom-sheets/ActionSheet.tsx (only its ActionSheetItem type is imported). headers/AppHeader appears to be used only by the dead PlaceholderScreen.
src/screens/settings/components/SettingsComingSoonBadge.tsx and the SettingsRow `comingSoon` prop (no caller passes it).
src/bootstrap/onboarding-persist-debug.ts (dev-only logging) and src/bootstrap/cleanup-obsolete-auth.ts (auth system is gone; keep one release at most).

package.json dependencies with zero importers: @expo/ui, react-hook-form, @hookform/resolvers, zod, expo-symbols, expo-web-browser (present only as an app.json plugin). @gorhom/bottom-sheet is only used by the dead BottomSheet.tsx and the unused BottomSheetModalProvider. react-native-web and react-dom are only needed for the web target of an Android-first app. NOT dead despite zero direct imports: @expo/vector-icons is the only installed MaterialCommunityIcons provider behind react-native-paper's Icon (node_modules/react-native-paper/src/components/MaterialCommunityIcon.tsx:45), and react-native-worklets and react-native-nitro-modules are peer dependencies.
About 125 package.json verify:* scripts (week/day/phase names) pointing at scripts/verify-*.ts; none of them are real tests.
capabilityGaps: No real 'paste or share a link, then download' entry point. The Downloads 'Paste link' button only switches tabs. There is no Android share-intent (ACTION_SEND text/plain) handling in src/app or +native-intent.ts, and no clipboard-link detection when the app comes to the foreground.

The quality sheet silently filters to verified standalone (already muxed) variants (useQualitySelection.ts:333 selectVerifiedStandaloneQualities). Separate video+audio DASH and HLS alternate-audio variants are never shown, not even as disabled with a reason, so Instagram, TikTok and YouTube HD typically end up in 'no downloadable format'.
No global download feedback surface (snackbar or mini progress bar) visible from the Browser tab. The success toast is on the Downloads tab.

Organization is weak for 'stored very cleanly': folders exist only as a modal inside a single download's details screen (DownloadDetailsScreen.tsx:1085-1222). There is no bulk select, move or delete, and no grouping by platform or source. The Downloads list only filters by status and sorts newest/oldest (DownloadsHeaderControls.tsx:19-31).

The information architecture overlaps. Downloads lists completed items with Open/Share/Remove, and there are also separate Library, Favorites, Bookmarks, History and Watch-History screens, so the same media shows up in several places.
Theme can't follow system dark mode (theme-preference.ts:30-32) even though app.json declares automatic.
Startup can't open straight into the app: the splash plus onboarding sequence runs on every launch, and deep links and notifications land behind it.
No UI test coverage. The large hooks (useQualitySelection, useDownloadDetailsScreen, useDownloadsScreen) would need rendering to test; only string-matching verify scripts exist.
App-level Android config is stale for a downloader: READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permissions (ignored on API 33+), orientation locked to portrait app-wide, and predictiveBackGestureEnabled false.
audits.crossSubsystemCoupling:
- **Navigation and design system are load-bearing everywhere.** Browser, Library, Player, Storage-Manager, Support, notifications and the download engine's notification bridge all import src/navigation (routePaths, navigation, openPlayer, downloadDetailsPath) and components/base plus useTheme (about 140 files). Keep those public APIs stable and swap the internals.
- **src/api/types.ts is the de-facto download domain model.** DownloadItem, DownloadStatus, DownloadWorkerState, MediaAnalysisResult and MediaAnalysisVariant are imported by 40 files: downloads/engine, analyze, reconciliation, storage repositories and catalog services, media-detection resolution services, browser media-actions, store/downloads, favorites and folders, and library. Move these types to src/downloads/types (or similar) with a codemod; don't delete them.
- **The quality-selection controller is tightly bound both ways.**
  - It reaches into: browser (useBrowserStore, pendingNavigationService, browserMediaActionService freeze/epoch/selection-lock APIs), media-detection (pendingMediaResolutionService, startPageMediaResolution, runPreDownloadGate, refreshMediaFromPage, socialPageContextStore, generalPageMediaContextStore, usePendingMediaResolution) and useDownloadsStore.create.
  - Things that depend on it: BrowserScreen.tsx:152-175 needs its context (openWithUrl, openWithAnalysis); useBrowserMediaAction.ts:180-203 needs the created/closed buses; BrowserScreen registers loadUrl through browser-load-bridge.
  - Replacing it has to be co-designed with the browser and detection audits.
- **Downloads screen helpers are shared.** screens/downloads/utils/download-format.ts and theme/downloads-tokens.ts are imported by screens/library/utils/library-format.ts and screens/favorites/utils/favorite-format.ts. storage-manager imports screens/home/utils, which is a wrong-direction dependency.
- **runAppInitializer is the only place that wires the download engine.** It calls downloadAppLifecycle.ensureAttached, bindDownloadEngineToStore, ensureDownloadRecoveryListener, ensureDownloadNotificationBridge, ensureLibraryCompletionBridge, bindPlaybackPersistence and reconcilePendingExports. ProtectedRouteGuard.tsx:16-36 calls setNotificationNavigationReady. Removing or reshaping bootstrap without moving these calls leaves downloads, notifications and library sync dead.
- **Security:** AppLockGate (security/app-lock) is mounted in (app)/_layout.tsx, and Settings PrivacySection routes to the app-lock screens.
- **react-native-paper is only needed for rendering.** It is load-bearing through components/base/Icon.tsx, navigation/components/TabBarIcon.tsx (MaterialDesignIcons names are used everywhere), AppModal's Portal and error-fallback.tsx. Swapping to @expo/vector-icons MaterialCommunityIcons is roughly a 4-file change if icon names stay the same.
- **Storage adapter:** the Zustand persist storage chosen in bootstrap/configure-storage.ts must load before any store module that other subsystems import.
audits.recommendations:
1) STARTUP (rewrite)
- Delete the /splash and every-launch onboarding path, InitialRouteRedirect, resolve-*-route, startup-splash-sequence, defer-initial-linking.ts, patch-expo-router-linking.ts, after-navigation-ready.ts and (tabs)/index.tsx.
- Keep expo-splash-screen's native splash until a minimal synchronous-ish init: storage adapter, theme and settings hydration, fonts. Budget under 300 ms, with a hard timeout.
- Render (tabs) directly. In the tabs layout set `initialRouteName='browser'`; in the root layout use `unstable_settings={ anchor: '(app)' }`.
- Show onboarding once, gated by a persisted onboardingComplete flag, using a Stack.Protected guard in the root layout.
- Move catalog seeding, first-page load, export reconciliation, notification bridge and playback binding to a post-first-frame `startBackgroundServices()` called from the tabs layout effect.
- Surface a non-dev error state (banner) if engine binding fails.

2) ROUTES / IA
Root providers: GestureHandlerRootView, SafeAreaProvider, ErrorBoundary, Localization, a navigation ThemeProvider, a Snackbar host, and AppLockGate. The route tree:
- (tabs): browser | downloads | library | settings
  - downloads: active and queued transfers plus the last few completed, with 'See all in Library'.
  - library: all completed media, folders, favorites, player entry.
- stack: downloads/[id], player/[id], settings/download, settings/storage, settings/app-lock/*, legal/*.
Remove navigation/modules, linking.ts, deep-link.ts, route-access, route-groups, GuestRouteGuard, SessionProvider, and the duplicated route-names constants. Rely on typedRoutes and one `routes.ts` of path builders.

3) BACK HANDLING
There must be exactly one owner. useBrowserHardwareBack handles web back and returns false at browser home. Implement double-back-to-exit inside that same hook, only when at home, and delete useTabExitBackHandler.

4) ADD-DOWNLOAD FLOW (rewrite with the browser/detection owners)
- Service: `src/downloads/offer/resolveDownloadOffer(input: {url} | {analysis, requestContext}) -> Promise<DownloadOffer>`. A pure, testable service that holds analyze, gate and refresh. It returns all variants with a `requiresMux` flag rather than filtering silently.
- Store: `useDownloadSheetStore` (Zustand) with an explicit state union `{idle} | {analyzing,url} | {choosing,offer,selectedId} | {creating} | {error,message}`. Actions: openWithUrl, openWithOffer, select, confirm, close. It emits `lastCreated` for a global snackbar ('Added to Downloads · View').
- UI: a single `<DownloadSheet/>` mounted at root, a presentational rewrite of QualitySelectionSheet.
- Delete download-created-bus.ts, browser-load-bridge.ts and QualitySelectionProvider.
- Make 'Paste link' real: read the clipboard or accept typed input, then openWithUrl.
- Add Android share-intent handling (text/plain URL) that routes into openWithUrl.

5) DOWNLOADS UI (refactor)
- Keep DownloadCard's per-id subscription pattern, DownloadsList, QueueScreen and QueueActiveRow.
- Simplify the card to thumbnail, title, a meta/progress line, one primary icon action, and an overflow menu (ActionSheetModal), instead of a column of 3-4 round buttons.
- Header: search and a filter chip row only. Move Queue into a section of the Downloads tab, and Favorites into Library.
- Cut DownloadDetailsScreen to under 300 lines: hero, status and progress, primary action, info rows. Rename, move and delete go in an ActionSheetModal plus a small `RenameFileDialog` that keeps the extension.
- Move folder management to a Library/Folders screen.
- Fix the status fallthrough to 'missing'.

6) DESIGN SYSTEM (keep and trim)
- Keep: Box, Text, Pressable, Button, IconButton, ActionSheetModal, ConfirmModal (on a plain RN Modal), EmptyState, ErrorState, ProgressBar, Skeleton, ScreenHeader, SafeAreaScreen.
- Change Icon.tsx and TabBarIcon.tsx to `@expo/vector-icons/MaterialCommunityIcons`. Rewrite error-fallback with in-house Button and Text.
- Then remove react-native-paper, paper-provider.tsx and paper-theme.ts.
- Delete gorhom BottomSheet and its provider, the unused components, and the 7 per-screen token files (add semantic status colors like `status.downloading.bg` to theme.colors instead).
- Go to 2 schemes following the system (light/dark) plus a brand accent; drop the 'logo' chrome mode, or make it an accent option.

7) SETTINGS (refactor)
- One screen with sections: Appearance (System/Light/Dark), Language, Downloads (Wi-Fi only, concurrency, notifications), Storage, App Lock, About/Legal.
- Write straight to store actions, with no saving/feedback queue. Move services/auth/settings.service.ts into store/settings actions.
- Remove the stagger animations and the ComingSoon badge.
- Fix the render-time hydrateDownloadSettings call.

8) DELETE / MOVE
- src/api: move the 21 used types to src/downloads/types.ts and src/media/types.ts via a codemod; drop ApiError and every isApiError branch.
- src/screens/home: move its two utils to storage-manager.
- Also delete: src/screens/placeholder, hooks/use-color-scheme*, constants/environment featureFlags, theme/contrast.ts, onboarding-persist-debug.ts.
- cleanup-obsolete-auth.ts: remove after one release.
- QueryProvider: drop it, or keep react-query only if playback actually benefits.
- Remove dependencies @expo/ui, react-hook-form, @hookform/resolvers, zod, expo-symbols, expo-web-browser (and its plugin), @gorhom/bottom-sheet, and react-native-paper after the icon swap. Remove react-native-web and react-dom if web is dropped, and lucide-react-native if onboarding is simplified. Keep @expo/vector-icons.
- Replace ~125 verify:* scripts with a small Jest suite for pure services (offer resolution, download-format, route builders) plus a few component tests.

9) HYGIENE
- Move all hard-coded strings into en.ts and ur.ts, and add an eslint rule against raw JSX string literals.
- Stop hand-writing memo, useCallback and useMemo (React Compiler is on).
- Fix the 2 set-state-in-effect lint errors in this scope.
- Align the native splash color with the theme background and follow the OS color scheme.

audits.subsystem: ui-peripheral (splash, onboarding, app lock, localization, history/bookmarks/favorites/watch-history, legal/about/support, services, graphics, scripts/, docs/)
audits.purpose:
Everything around the core downloader:
- **Launch:** a branded splash and a 3-page animated intro (Gateway → Trust → Library) that play on every cold start.
- **App lock:** a 4-digit PIN with a recovery code, change-PIN and code-rotation screens, stored in SecureStore.
- **Localization:** English and Urdu with partial RTL.
- **Lists:** browser history, bookmarks, favorites and watch-history screens.
- **Legal/support:** in-app Privacy/Terms/About, an FAQ/support hub, and a Report Problem form.
- **Services:** local settings writers and the React Query client.

It also includes 125 verify-*.ts scripts (54.7K lines) and 91 docs files.
audits.architecture:
About 23.6K lines of TypeScript in scope. The main lines, by feature:
- onboarding 5.1K
- localization 4.4K
- app lock 3.1K + 0.8K screens
- support 2.8K
- legal 1.6K
- splash 1.1K
- graphics 1.2K
- history/favorites/bookmarks ~1K each

**LAUNCH**
- `src/app/_layout.tsx` gets `initialRoute` from `useAppInitializer` → `runAppInitializer` (`src/bootstrap/app-initializer.ts:40-214`). That returns `resolveInitialRoute()`, which is hardcoded to `'/splash'` (`src/navigation/helpers/resolve-initial-route.ts:7-9`).
- `InitialRouteRedirect` (`src/navigation/components/InitialRouteRedirect.tsx`) replaces whatever path was resolved with that route.
- The `(auth)` group has two routes:
  - `splash.tsx` → `src/screens/splash/SplashScreen.tsx`. It uses `animations/useSplashSequence.ts` (16 hand-declared shared values) and `hooks/useSplashExitGate.ts`, then exits via `resolvePostSplashRoute()`, hardcoded to `'/onboarding'`.
  - `onboarding.tsx` → `OnboardingRouteGuard` → `src/screens/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.tsx`. Page index is local state. Each of gateway/, trust/ and library/ has its own animations/timings/styles/constants/components folders. Gateway renders `src/components/graphics/PlatformHubGraphic`.
- `completeOnboarding` writes `onboardingComplete` into `store/app` (zustand persist), then polls disk (`store/app/persist-sync.ts:25-38`). **No routing code reads this flag.**

**APP LOCK** (`src/security/app-lock`), in strict layers:
1. `app-lock.constants` / `types`
2. `app-lock.crypto`: SHA-256 via expo-crypto; injectable for tests.
3. `app-lock.storage`: one JSON record in SecureStore under key `vidorax.appLock.v1`, classified as missing / valid / corrupt_enabled / discardable / read_error.
4. `app-lock-policy`: fail-closed bootstrap decision.
5. `app-lock-throttle`: pure functions.
6. `app-lock.service`: module-level singletons (`cachedRecord`, `activeSetup`, `activeRecoveryRotation`, `recoveryAuthGranted`, eight in-flight promise guards).
7. `app-lock.store`: zustand UI state (`status` DISABLED/LOCKED/UNLOCKED, `gateMode`, `formEpoch`, plaintext `pendingRecoveryCode`).

On top of the layers:
- `AppLockGate` wraps the whole `(app)` Stack (`src/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:78-79`). It runs bootstrap, shows a spinner, an integrity-error screen, or the lock overlay over mounted children. It also installs the download-notification auth probe.
- `use-app-lock-lifecycle` locks on any active→non-active AppState change.
- UI: `AppLockScreen`, `AppLockForgotFlow`, `AppLockPinInput`.
- Settings → `PrivacySection` pushes 4 routes → `src/screens/security/*` (setup, disable, change PIN, rotate recovery).

**LOCALIZATION**
- `en.ts` is the source-of-truth type. `ur.ts` is typed `CatalogStrings<typeof en>`, so key parity is compile-checked: 1,111 leaf keys each, 0 missing, 8 values identical to English.
- `translate.ts` pre-flattens both catalogs, falls back to English, then to a humanized key.
- The language value lives in `store/settings`; bootstrap binds it via `bindLanguageReader`.
- `LocalizationProvider` sits in `providers/app-provider.tsx`. `useTranslation` also subscribes on its own with `useSyncExternalStore`.
- `rtl.ts` gives JS-level opt-in mirroring only (no I18nManager).
- `errors.ts` maps download-engine, player and legacy API error codes to keys.

**LIST SCREENS** (history, bookmarks, favorites)
- Each is `Screen.tsx` + `hooks/use<X>Screen.ts` (screen model) + ~8 components + `theme/<x>-tokens.ts` + utils + constants.
- Data path: `storage/hooks/use-<x>.ts` (selector fan-out) → `store/<x>` (zustand, 1,767 lines combined) → SQLite services.
- History and bookmark taps go through `pendingNavigationService.set(url)` + `navigate('/browser')`. Favorite taps resolve sourceUrl → download id → `/downloads/[id]`.
- `watch-history` is a single 257-line file over `playback/hooks` `usePlaybackHistoryInfiniteQuery`.

**LEGAL / SUPPORT**
- `src/legal/config.ts` holds the contact config; both emails are null.
- `terms-content.ts` / `privacy-content.ts` are trees of i18n keys → `screens/legal/LegalDocumentView`, `AboutScreen`.
- `src/support` contains faq-content, categories, search, validation, diagnostics allowlist, the 308-line `support-context` route-param parser, and `support-service` (mailto).
- Screens: `screens/support/SupportScreen.tsx`, `ReportProblemScreen.tsx` (598 lines). The `(app)/support` route imports SupportScreen through a 5-line re-export shim in `screens/legal`.

**SERVICES**
- `services/auth/settings.service.ts`: local preference writers into settings/theme stores, plus a lazy require of `downloads/settings`. Nothing auth-related remains despite the name.
- `settings-validation.ts`: leftover mappers from the removed backend API.
- `services/query-client.ts`.

**SCRIPTS**
- 125 verify-*.ts, `_node-asset-stub.ts`, `tsconfig`, and two postinstall patchers: `apply-webview-media-hook.js` and `apply-player-native-modules.js`. **The two patchers are load-bearing** (package.json postinstall).
- 127 `verify:` npm scripts. All run via `npx tsx`, but tsx is not in devDependencies and not in `node_modules/.bin`. There is no CI (no .github or .husky).

**DOCS**
- 91 files: ~75 markdown phase/architecture/acceptance docs, 12 PNG evidence screenshots, 3 Maestro YAML flows, 1 log.
- Plus FREEZE markdown inside `src`: `LOCAL-ONLY-MIGRATION-FREEZE.md`, `WEEK85-PHASE5-FREEZE.md`, `legal/PHASE3-FREEZE.md`.
audits.endToEndTrace:
**FLOW 1: Cold start to usable app** (every launch)
1. `src/entry.js:9-12` → `src/app/_layout.tsx:22` (`preventAutoHideAsync`) → `AppProvider` (`src/providers/app-provider.tsx:52-78`).
2. `useAppInitializer` → `runAppInitializer` (`app-initializer.ts:40-214`) returns `'/splash'` (`resolve-initial-route.ts:8`).
3. `AppLaunchGate` hides the native splash once fonts and init are ready (`app-provider.tsx:24-37`).
4. `InitialRouteRedirect.tsx:27-42` calls `replace('/splash')` for any path other than `/splash`. **FRAGILE:** a cold-start deep link path is discarded here.
5. `SplashScreen.tsx:60-66` exits only when init is done AND 3,850 ms have passed, then plays a 750 ms exit (`timings.ts:27-30`).
6. `router.replace('/onboarding')` (`SplashScreen.tsx:51-53`, `resolve-post-splash-route.ts:17`).
7. `OnboardingRouteGuard` → `OnboardingScreen.tsx`. The user must tap Continue twice and then Get Started, or tap Skip (`OnboardingScreen.tsx:64-74`). The Library page plays its exit animation (`useLibrarySequence.ts:212-241`).
8. `navigateToHome` (`OnboardingScreen.tsx:35-48`) calls `completeOnboarding()`, then `awaitOnboardingPersisted()`, which polls disk every 50 ms for up to 3 s (`persist-sync.ts:25-38`), then `replace('/browser')`.
9. `(app)/_layout.tsx:78` → `ProtectedRouteGuard` → `AppLockGate` bootstrap (`AppLockGate.tsx:73-77`, `app-lock.store.ts:109-185`) shows a spinner while reading SecureStore. DISABLED shows the app; LOCKED shows `AppLockScreen`.

**BREAKS:** the persisted `onboardingComplete` is never read, so every launch costs about 5 s plus 3 taps. When App Lock is on, the PIN prompt comes only after all of that. Deep links are lost at step 4.

**FLOW 2: Enable App Lock**
1. `PrivacySection.tsx:27-35` pushes `/app-lock-setup`. The route effect calls `beginSetup` (`src/app/(app)/app-lock-setup.tsx:7-16`).
2. `AppLockSetupScreen` set → confirm → `store.prepareSetup` → `service.beginSetupPrepare` (`app-lock.service.ts:197-252`) creates salts, the recovery code and verifiers in memory.
3. Recovery step: copy, checkbox, `completeSetup` → `completeSetupCommit` writes SecureStore (`service.ts:254-291`) → UNLOCKED + `isEnabled` → `router.back()`.

**WORKS.** The lifecycle hook isn't subscribed while the lock is disabled (`use-app-lock-lifecycle.ts:17`), so leaving the app mid-setup is safe.

**FLOW 3: Background, then unlock**
1. AppState active → background → `lock()` (`use-app-lock-lifecycle.ts:24-26`, `app-lock.store.ts:192-216`) → `clearSensitiveEphemeralState()` (`service.ts:145-149`) → LOCKED.
2. `AppLockGate.tsx:127-155` puts an opaque overlay over the still-mounted Stack.
3. The 4th digit auto-submits (`AppLockPinInput.tsx:53-63`) → `unlockWithPin` (`service.ts:427-488`): throttle check → SHA-256 compare → clear throttle → UNLOCKED.

**WORKS** for plain unlock. **BREAKS** for:
- **Rotate recovery:** the user copies the new code and switches apps to save it. `lock()` cancels `activeRecoveryRotation`, and `AppLockRotateRecoveryScreen.tsx:43-50` backs out. The code the user saved is never committed.
- **Forgot-PIN:** backgrounding resets `lockedSurface` and `recoveryAuthGranted` (`store.ts:198-206`).
- **Every share, open-with or export picker** re-locks the app.

**FLOW 4: Browser history**
1. Browser header or overflow menu → `push('/history')` (`BrowserBookmarkControls.tsx:112`, `browser-menu-actions.ts:158`).
2. `HistoryScreen` → `useHistoryScreen` → `useBrowserHistory` auto-loads page 1 (`use-browser-history.ts:47-51`) → grouped by day.
3. Tapping an entry: `pendingNavigationService.set` + `navigate('/browser')` (`useHistoryScreen.ts:75-80`).

**PLAUSIBLY WORKS.** Search runs only on keyboard submit (`HistoryScreen.tsx:119-125`), unlike bookmarks and favorites.

**FLOW 5: Report a problem**
1. Settings `AboutSection.tsx:34` → `push('/report-problem')` → the 598-line form.
2. `handleSend` → `isAvailable` is false because both contact emails are null (`src/legal/config.ts:41-42`, `support-config.ts:18-24`) → `setStatus('unavailable')` and return (`ReportProblemScreen.tsx:149-152`).

**DEAD END in this build.**
audits.verdictRationale:
**Delete:**
- **Launch cinematics (splash + 3-page onboarding + graphics), ~7.4K lines.** They replay on every cold start by design, never read the onboarding flag they write, override cold-start deep links, and hide the lock screen behind ~5 s of animation. A downloader should open straight to the browser.
- **Report Problem and most of support, ~2.8K lines.** Inert: no contact email is configured, so nothing can be sent.
- **Verify scripts and docs.** Mostly source-text assertions (3,160 `.includes()` checks; 96 of 125 scripts read src file text) that freeze current behavior, including the bad launch flow. Nothing runs them (no CI, tsx not installed).

**Refactor:**
- **App lock.** Its pure core (storage classification, fail-closed policy, throttle, crypto) is solid and testable. The product layer, though, has a real lockout-risk bug (a rotated recovery code is dropped when the user leaves the app to save it). It re-locks on every share or open-with, and 4 routes plus 3.9K lines is far too heavy. Swapping to OS biometric/device-credential auth would remove the PIN and recovery-code risk entirely.
- **History, bookmarks and favorites screens.** They work, but are three near-identical ~1K-line folders.

**Keep:**
- Localization core (typed keys, full 1,111-key Urdu parity, English fallback).
- Watch history (right-sized).
- In-app legal documents.
- `query-client`.
- The two postinstall patch scripts.

keepWorthy.why: Pure, store-injectable (SecureStoreLike). Classifies the SecureStore payload into missing/valid/corrupt_enabled/discardable/read_error, and an enabled-but-corrupt record fails closed instead of silently disabling (lines 105-134). Keep if a PIN lock survives.
Tiny exhaustive bootstrap decision with a `never` check (lines 15-34). Correct fail-closed semantics.

Recovery-code generation uses correct rejection sampling over a 31-char unambiguous alphabet, ~128.8 bits (lines 145-162). Primitives are injectable, so it runs in Node. Only weakness: single SHA-256 over a 4-digit PIN, which is acknowledged in constants.
Pure, deterministic throttle policy taking `now` as input, so it is unit-testable. The escalation curve needs tuning, but the shape is good.

Small and correct: pre-flattened catalogs, English fallback with a one-time dev warning, humanized-key last resort, `{name}` interpolation. Language comes in via `bindLanguageReader`, so there is no React dependency.

`TranslationKey` is derived from the en catalog (FlattenKeys), and ur.ts is typed `CatalogStrings<typeof en>`. Key typos and missing Urdu keys fail tsc. Measured: 1,111/1,111 keys, only 8 identical to English.
A real, complete Urdu translation. If Urdu-speaking users matter, this is valuable work that is expensive to redo.
Pragmatic JS-level RTL helpers that avoid the I18nManager restart problem. RTL is opt-in per component, though.
Correct 'init done AND minimum time elapsed' gate with ref-guarded single fire and timer cleanup. Reusable if any min-visible gate is ever needed.
Correct OS reduce-motion subscription with cancellation and cleanup. Also imported by onboarding pages and the media-detection overlay, so move it to src/hooks before deleting splash.
Right-sized single file: infinite query, flags missing files via library availability, virtualized FlatList with sane batch settings. Only needs i18n fixes.

Solid screen-model hook: debounced search, per-item in-flight guard, resolves favorite → download id from the store first and then SQLite (lines 30-61), with unavailable-state tracking. A good template for one generic list-screen hook.
Clean status derivation (loading/error/empty/empty-search/ready) and delete/clear dialog state with busy guards. Reusable pattern.
`buildMailtoUrl` correctly encodes subject and body and sends only allowlisted fields. The whole support subsystem could shrink to this one function plus a configured email.
Data-driven legal document (section → i18n keys), rendered by one `LegalDocumentView`. Cheap way to meet the Play Store in-app policy requirement. Keep with privacy-content.ts.
Minimal, sensible React Query defaults for local-only caches (networkMode 'always', no refetch on focus). Used by playback and library.
Load-bearing: runs in npm postinstall to patch react-native-webview. Must survive any scripts/ purge, together with scripts/apply-player-native-modules.js.

One of the few verify scripts that is a real behavioral test: it imports persist code, uses in-memory storage, and asserts round-trips. Its logic-only cases, along with those in verify-app-lock-phase1/2, are worth porting to Jest before deleting scripts/.

bugs.description: A rotated recovery code is thrown away if the user leaves the app to save it. The rotate screen shows a Copy button (lines 151-159). Switching to a password manager or notes app triggers `use-app-lock-lifecycle.ts:24-26` → `lock()` (`app-lock.store.ts:192-216`) → `clearSensitiveEphemeralState()` → `cancelRecoveryRotationSession()` (`app-lock.service.ts:134-149`). The screen's LOCKED effect (lines 43-50) then also cancels and calls `router.back()`. The new code is never persisted; the old code stays the only valid one.
bugs.userImpact: The user saves a recovery code that doesn't work, possibly discarding the old one. If they later forget the PIN, recovery fails and the only escape is clearing app data (the en.ts `lostBothWarning` copy says so), which wipes their library.

bugs.description: Every cold start forces the full splash plus the 3-page onboarding. `resolvePostSplashRoute` always returns `/onboarding`. OnboardingScreen writes `onboardingComplete`, but no routing code reads it (it only appears in debug logging and the persist sync). Splash is held for at least 3,850 ms plus a 750 ms exit (`SplashScreen.tsx:60-66`, `timings.ts:27-30`). Onboarding needs 3 taps or Skip, then `awaitOnboardingPersisted` polls disk for up to 3 s (`persist-sync.ts:25-38`). `verify-startup-splash-runtime.ts` asserts this behavior is intended.
bugs.userImpact: About 5 s plus manual taps before the browser appears, on every launch. With App Lock enabled, the PIN prompt comes only after the whole intro.

bugs.description: Cold-start deep links are overwritten. Once navigation state exists, the component calls `replace(href)` whenever the current path isn't `/splash`, because `resolveInitialRoute` is always `/splash` (`resolve-initial-route.ts:8`). Onboarding then does `replace('/browser')`. The manifest declares VIEW (https, video/*, audio/*, */*), SEND (video/*, audio/*, */*) and `vidorax://` filters (AndroidManifest.xml lines 10-37, 55-60). Any path expo-router derives from such an intent on cold start is dropped. I found no JS or Kotlin consumer for SEND extras (grep for EXTRA_TEXT / share-intent found nothing); the intents owner should confirm.
bugs.userImpact: 'Open with VidoraX' or a `vidorax://` link from a notification or another app lands on the browser home after the intro, not on the intended target.

bugs.description: The app locks on every active→non-active transition with no grace period and no exemption for intentional handoffs. On Android, the share sheet, open-with/external player, SAF export picker and permission dialogs all pause the activity. Share, open and permission call sites exist in `src/downloads/completed-file/action-service.ts`, `src/downloads/engine/file-actions.ts` and `src/downloads/notifications/permission.ts`.
bugs.userImpact: With App Lock on, sharing a downloaded video, opening it in another player, exporting, or granting notification permission sends the user back to the PIN screen every time.

bugs.description: The Forgot-PIN flow is reset by backgrounding. While already LOCKED, `lock()` bumps `formEpoch`, sets `lockedSurface` back to 'unlock', and (via `clearSensitiveEphemeralState`) clears `recoveryAuthGranted`. `AppLockForgotFlow`'s formEpoch effect (`AppLockForgotFlow.tsx:42-48`) wipes the typed input.
bugs.userImpact: A user who switches to their password manager to fetch the recovery code comes back to the unlock screen and must start Forgot PIN over. The same happens between verifying the code and setting the new PIN.

bugs.description: Both `supportEmail` and `privacyEmail` are null, so `getSupportSubmissionMode()` is always 'unavailable' (`support-config.ts:18-24`). `ReportProblemScreen.handleSend` returns immediately with status 'unavailable' (`ReportProblemScreen.tsx:149-152`), and the SupportScreen contact rows are hidden (`SupportScreen.tsx:328`).
bugs.userImpact: The Report Problem form (598 lines, validation, diagnostics preview) can never send anything; users fill it in for nothing. There is no working support contact at all.

bugs.description: Weak brute-force protection. Delays plateau at 30 s from the 7th failure onward (`app-lock.constants.ts:28-34`), with no lockout growth. `retryAfter` is wall-clock epoch ms, so setting the device clock forward bypasses it. The verifier is one SHA-256 over a 4-digit PIN plus a 16-byte salt (`app-lock.crypto.ts:89-97`), recoverable in 10,000 hashes if the SecureStore blob is ever extracted (`constants.ts:9` admits 'not a strong offline KDF').
bugs.userImpact: Someone holding an unlocked-screen device can exhaust all PINs in under ~83 hours, or much faster by changing the clock. The lock also doesn't protect the downloaded files themselves, so it's UI privacy only.

bugs.description: Pending notification targets are flushed only when `status === 'UNLOCKED'` (lines 50-52 and 62-71). With App Lock disabled (the default), status is 'DISABLED', so the gate never flushes. Whether a cold-start notification tap still navigates depends on `@/downloads/notifications` handling an auth probe that returns true on its own. Plausible; the notifications auditor should verify.
bugs.userImpact: A possible lost navigation on tapping a 'download complete' notification for users without App Lock.

bugs.description: Bookmark search filters only the already-loaded page (`filterBookmarksLocally` over `items`) and forces `hasMore` false while a query is active (line 191). It also calls `setQuery` on a debounce (line 107); if the store's `setQuery` doesn't trigger a storage search, bookmarks beyond the first page can't be found (store actions not traced). Separately, History search runs only on keyboard submit (`useHistoryScreen.ts:59-68`, `HistoryScreen.tsx:119-125`), while Favorites and Bookmarks search as you type.
bugs.userImpact: Search results in lists look incomplete, and search behaves inconsistently across the three screens.

bugs.description: Hardcoded English strings in an app that ships Urdu: the 'Couldn't open this favorite.' error (useFavoritesScreen.ts:174), the 'Video' fallback title (WatchHistoryScreen.tsx:162), and WatchHistoryScreen showing `errors.network` for a purely local MMKV query failure (WatchHistoryScreen.tsx:203-206).
bugs.userImpact: Urdu users see English fragments, and local read failures are described as network errors.

bugs.description: The throttle countdown is computed once per render from `Date.now()`, and the timer effect only re-renders at expiry (lines 50-60). 'Try again in N seconds' never counts down. `AppLockDisableScreen.tsx:66-71` shows the generic `disableError` for 'throttled' instead of the too-many-attempts message.
bugs.userImpact: A frozen countdown, and a misleading error while throttled.

**1. Launch: delete the cinematics**
- Remove `src/screens/splash`, `src/screens/onboarding`, `src/components/graphics`, `src/app/(auth)`, `navigation/helpers/startup-splash-sequence.ts`, `resolve-post-splash-route.ts`, `OnboardingRouteGuard`, `bootstrap/onboarding-persist-debug.ts` and `awaitOnboardingPersisted`. That is ~7.4K lines.

**2. App lock: rebuild on OS auth (recommended)**
- Replace with `expo-local-authentication` (biometric + device PIN/pattern). State: `{ enabled: boolean; graceSeconds: number }` in the settings store.

- Don't clear rotation or forgot sessions on background; commit the rotated code before revealing Copy, or keep the session until explicit cancel.
- Add the grace period and handoff exemption.
- Escalate delays (e.g., doubling to 1 h) and count attempts independently of wall clock.
- Allow 6-digit PINs, or derive with native PBKDF2.
- Collapse the 4 routes into one settings sub-screen.

**3. Lists: consolidate history, bookmarks and favorites**
- Build one `PagedListScreen<T>` (header, search field, status switch, FlatList with refresh/pagination, confirm dialog) plus `usePagedStoreList(store, { searchMode: 'debounced' })`, with per-domain `renderRow` and `onOpen`.
- Delete the three per-screen token, skeleton, footer, empty and error component sets.
- Make all searches debounced, and query storage instead of filtering the loaded page.
- Consider replacing Favorites with a `starred` flag on library items (filtered in Library), since favorites only resolve back to downloads.
- Keep `WatchHistoryScreen` (fix i18n fallbacks) or fold it into a Library 'Recently watched' filter, which already exists per `secondary-destination-intent.ts`.

**4. Localization: keep, trim**
- Keep `en.ts`, `ur.ts`, `translate.ts`, `types.ts`, `config.ts`, `rtl.ts`.
- `useTranslation` should read context only (throw in dev if missing) instead of also subscribing.
- Replace `plurals.ts` prefix matching with explicit `{one, other}` keys or `Intl.PluralRules`.
- Drop `@/api` coupling in `errors.ts`.
- Decide on Urdu as a product call: it is complete today and cheap to keep, but every new string needs translation.

**5. Legal / About / Support: shrink**
- Keep `LegalDocumentView` + Privacy + Terms content and one About card (version, links).
- Delete update-check and rate-app code until a Play listing exists.
- Delete `ReportProblemScreen` and `src/support` except the FAQ content and `buildMailtoUrl`; merge the FAQ into one static Help screen with a 'Contact' mailto row shown only when an email is configured.
- Set a real support email, or drop the feature entirely.
- Remove the support-context param parser and the `@/support` imports in PlayerScreen and DownloadDetailsScreen.

**6. Services**
- Rename `services/auth` → `services/preferences`.
- Delete the API mapping functions.
- Keep `query-client`.

**7. Scripts**
- Delete all 125 `verify-*.ts`, `_node-asset-stub.ts`, `scripts/tsconfig.json` and the 127 `verify:` npm scripts. **Keep the two postinstall .js patchers.**
- Before deleting, port the logic-only cases (app-lock crypto/storage/throttle from verify-app-lock-phase1/2, verify-onboarding-persist-flow, and the pure detection/state-machine ones owned by other subsystems) into Jest via `jest-expo`, colocated as `*.test.ts`.
- Add one CI job: `tsc --noEmit`, `expo lint`, `jest`.
- Deletion costs nothing at runtime. It removes 3,160 string-presence assertions that would otherwise flag nearly every refactor and that currently enforce bugs such as the forced onboarding.

**8. Docs**
- Delete the phase and acceptance docs, evidence PNGs and logs, and the FREEZE markdown files in src.
- Replace them with one `ARCHITECTURE.md` describing the post-overhaul module map.
- Keep the Maestro YAML only if Maestro E2E is adopted as the real device-test layer.

research.report:
# How major sites deliver video to an Android WebView (2026), and a detection design for VidoraX

## 0. Summary

- **The big social sites (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X) put the playable URLs in JSON**, not in the `<video>` tag. The page receives that JSON through GraphQL/API responses or embeds it in the HTML.
  - In each case one of those URLs is a complete progressive MP4 with audio: `video_versions`, `browser_native_hd_url` / `progressive_urls`, `playAddr` / `bitrateInfo`, and X's `video/mp4` variants.
  - What the player actually streams is usually separate video and audio: DASH via MSE on Meta, split-audio HLS on X.
  - So the best strategy is to read the JSON the page already receives, inside the page, rather than sniffing media URLs.
- **VidoraX currently throws that JSON away.**
  - The native filter drops `/api`, `/graphql` and `.json` requests: `MediaNetworkBridge.kt:59-75` and `:221-245`.
  - The injected fetch/XHR hooks record only the URL and content-type, never the body: `src/media-detection/observers/injected-script.ts:516-562`.
  - The MSE hook only flags that a blob exists: `injected-script.ts:564-578`.
- **Many other sites (Reddit, Vimeo, Pinterest, split-audio HLS, generic DASH) need muxing.** FFmpegKit is retired and its binaries were pulled in April 2025. The practical on-device option is Media3's extractors plus `media3-muxer` (`Mp4Muxer`), which has been a standalone module since 1.8.0.
- **YouTube:** plain URL capture no longer works. Playback is SABR (POST requests with a protobuf body, UMP-framed responses) and needs PO tokens. Downloading also breaks YouTube's Terms of Service and is a Google Play policy risk. **Recommendation: refuse YouTube explicitly.**
- **MSE capture** (hooking `SourceBuffer.appendBuffer`) is the only universal fallback for obscured players. Its limits:
  - It needs the video to play through.
  - It gives two tracks that must be muxed.
  - It fails on DRM and on MSE running inside a worker.
  - On Android it needs real document-start, all-frames injection (`WebViewCompat.addDocumentStartJavaScript`) and a binary channel (`addWebMessageListener` with ArrayBuffer). The app has neither today.

---

## 1. Per-site table

"A/V split?" means the best-quality stream has separate audio and video tracks.

| Site | How it's delivered (2026) | Where the URLs live | A/V split? | Headers / cookies / login | Recommended extraction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Instagram** (reels, posts, stories) | DASH MPD: video H.264 (VP9 rolling out since Apr 23 2026), audio HE-AAC `mp4a.40.5`. Progressive MP4s also listed in `video_versions`. Player uses MSE (UNVERIFIED for the Android Chrome UA specifically). | GraphQL `/graphql/query` → `xdt_shortcode_media`; `/api/v1/media/{id}/info/` → `items[0].video_versions[]` and `video_dash_manifest` (inline MPD XML); embed page `video_url`; stories via `/feed/reels_media/` or GraphQL. | `video_versions`: usually has audio (yt-dlp sets `acodec: none` only when `has_audio == false`). DASH: always split. | API calls send `X-IG-App-ID: 936619743392459`, `X-ASBD-ID`, `X-FB-LSD`, `X-CSRFToken`. Since Jun 2026, anonymous API calls without a real browser TLS fingerprint are blocked. Stories and private posts need login. CDN URLs are signed (`oh` HMAC, `oe` hex expiry; TTL varies, UNVERIFIED). | Hook fetch/XHR response bodies in the page. Take the largest `video_versions` entry when `has_audio !== false`. Otherwise take best video and best audio from the MPD, download each representation, and mux. MSE capture is the fallback. **Don't replay the API from OkHttp** (fingerprint blocks). |
| **Facebook** (reels, watch, fb.watch) | Progressive (SD/HD, with audio) plus DASH (split) plus some HLS. Meta's player fetches ranges with `bytestart`/`byteend` query params instead of `Range` headers, to avoid CORS preflight. A Facebook engineer described this in 2017; UNVERIFIED that it still holds in 2026. | Legacy: `browser_native_hd_url` / `browser_native_sd_url`, `playable_url`, `playable_url_quality_hd` (`videoDeliveryLegacyFields`). Newer: `videoDeliveryResponseFragment/Result` → `progressive_urls[].progressive_url`, `dash_manifests[].manifest_xml`, `dash_manifest_urls`, `hls_playlist_urls`. Data sits in `<script data-sjs>` (ScheduledServerJS → `__bbox` → `RelayPrefetchedStreamCache`) and in `/api/graphql/` responses. | Progressive: no split (cobalt uses `browser_native_*` without muxing). DASH: split. | Login-walled content fails without a session; most 2026 "Cannot parse data" reports were in fact login-walled. Cookies come for free inside the WebView. | Scan `script[data-sjs]` and hook `/api/graphql/` bodies. Prefer HD progressive; use DASH plus mux only when progressive is missing or lower quality. |
| **TikTok** (mobile web) | Progressive MP4 on `v16/v19-webapp-prime.tiktok.com`. Some web playback reportedly goes through `blob:` / MSE (UNVERIFIED how much). | `<script id="__UNIVERSAL_DATA_FOR_REHYDRATION__">` → `__DEFAULT_SCOPE__["webapp.video-detail"].itemInfo.itemStruct.video`: `playAddr`, `downloadAddr`, `bitrateInfo[].PlayAddr.UrlList` with `CodecType` / `DataSize`. Feed pages load the same item structure over XHR (exact 2026 endpoint names UNVERIFIED). | No | The CDN URL carries `tk=tt_chain_token`, and the download **requires the `tt_chain_token` cookie** set during page load (per a yt-dlp maintainer). Send Referer (page) and the same UA. `downloadAddr` is watermarked; `playAddr` / `bitrateInfo` are not. `bytevc2` is unplayable. Since Aug–Sep 2026 TikTok serves JS challenges and blocks some TLS fingerprints. | Parse the rehydration JSON and hook item-list API bodies. Choose h264 at the highest bitrate (h265 if the device decodes it). Download natively with the WebView's cookies for that URL, Referer and UA. |
| **X / Twitter** | `video_info.variants[]` lists complete MP4s (`video/mp4`, with audio, with `bitrate`) and an HLS master (`application/x-mpegURL`). The HLS uses separate `EXT-X-MEDIA TYPE=AUDIO` renditions with fMP4/CMAF segments (`EXT-X-MAP`). The player streams HLS. | GraphQL `TweetDetail` / `TweetResultByRestId` (also timelines) → `extended_entities.media[].video_info.variants`; `cdn.syndication.twimg.com/tweet-result` is a fallback. | MP4 variants: no. HLS: yes. | Guest token plus bearer for anonymous API use. NSFW / age-restricted needs login. | Hook GraphQL response bodies and take the highest-bitrate `video/mp4` variant (no mux). Use HLS plus audio mux only if no MP4 exists. cobalt still uses MP4 variants in 2026. |
| **YouTube** (m.youtube.com) | SABR: POST to `serverAbrStreamingUrl` with a protobuf `VideoPlaybackAbrRequest`; response is UMP (`application/vnd.yt-ump`) with audio and video frames interleaved. The web client lost `adaptiveFormats` URLs in Feb 2025; `mweb` / `web_embedded` became SABR-only for some sessions in Sep 2026. | Not in usable URLs. HTTPS formats for `web`, `mweb`, `android`, `ios` need a GVS PO token. `android_vr` formats return 403 since 2026-08-17. | Yes (separate itags) | Session-bound PO tokens, signature / `n` JS challenges. Terms of Service forbid downloading. | **Refuse.** `shouldInterceptRequest` can't read POST bodies and UMP isn't a file. MSE capture would technically work for non-DRM videos but breaks YouTube's terms and risks Play policy. |
| **Reddit** (v.redd.it) | DASH (`DASHPlaylist.mpd`) and HLS (`HLSPlaylist.m3u8`). | Post JSON → `secure_media.reddit_video.{fallback_url, dash_url, hls_url}`. Audio at `CMAF_AUDIO_128.mp4` / `CMAF_AUDIO_64.mp4`; older posts use `DASH_AUDIO_*.mp4` or `audio.mp4`. | **Yes, always.** `fallback_url` is video-only. | None needed for public posts (NSFW needs `over18` / session). | Hook or fetch the post JSON (the app currently skips `.json`). Parse the MPD, download best video and audio, mux. |
| **Vimeo** | HLS on `vod-adaptive-ak.vimeocdn.com` / `skyfire.vimeocdn.com` with audio `GROUP-ID` renditions; segmented DASH (`master.json` / `playlist.json` with base64 init). Progressive often absent (UNVERIFIED how often). | `player.vimeo.com/video/{id}/config` or `window.playerConfig` → `request.files.{progressive,hls,dash}.cdns.{akfire_interconnect_quic,fastly_skyfire}.url`. | HLS/DASH: yes | The API needs login for yt-dlp again (Aug 2026), but in-browser playback works and grabbing the m3u8 from the network is the accepted workaround. Domain-restricted embeds need the embedding page as Referer. Unlisted videos need the `h=` hash. | Network-capture `playlist.m3u8` from the `player.vimeo.com` iframe, or read the config JSON inside the iframe. Run the HLS downloader and mux audio. Send the iframe's parent URL as Referer. |
| **Dailymotion** | HLS (fMP4); progressive `H264-WxH` URLs sometimes. | `/player/metadata/video/{xid}` → `qualities.auto[]` (`application/x-mpegURL`), fetched by the player iframe. | Reportedly muxed (UNVERIFIED) | Tokenised URLs; yt-dlp needs impersonation for m3u8 (anti-bot), so use the WebView's UA and cookies. | Capture the manifest from network requests or the metadata body; HLS downloader. |
| **Twitch** | Clips: progressive MP4. VODs: HLS via `usher.ttvnw.net/vod/{id}.m3u8?sig=…&token=…`. | GQL `gql.twitch.tv/gql` (Client-ID): clips `videoQualities[].sourceURL` plus `playbackAccessToken` sig/token; VODs `VideoPlaybackAccessToken`. | Clips: no. ## 2. Muxing, AES-128 and DRM matrix

| Needs A+V mux | No mux | May need HLS AES-128 decryption | DRM — must refuse |
|---|---|---|---|
| Instagram DASH (or `has_audio: false`) | Instagram `video_versions` (with audio) | Generic HLS sites with `#EXT-X-KEY:METHOD=AES-128`. Whole-segment AES-128-CBC with PKCS7. If `IV` is absent, the IV is the media sequence number, big-endian, left-padded to 16 bytes (RFC 8216 §4.3.2.4). Fetch the key URI with the same cookies and Referer. | EME / Widevine anywhere: `navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess` or `setMediaKeys` called |
| Facebook DASH-only cases | Facebook `browser_native_*` / `progressive_urls` | None of the named major platforms were verified to use AES-128 for public video (UNVERIFIED). | HLS `METHOD=SAMPLE-AES` or `KEYFORMAT` other than `identity` (e.g. Widevine `urn:uuid:edef8ba9-79d6-4ace-a3c8-27dcd51d21ed`) |
| Reddit (always) | TikTok `playAddr` | | DASH `<ContentProtection>` with a Widevine/PlayReady UUID; `pssh` / `tenc` / `encv` / `enca` boxes in init segments |
| X HLS (only if no MP4 variant) | X MP4 variants | | Android WebView plays Widevine only if the app grants `RESOURCE_PROTECTED_MEDIA_ID` in `onPermissionRequest`. Deny it and treat the request as a DRM signal. |
| Vimeo HLS/DASH, Pinterest HLS (likely), generic DASH | Twitch clips and VODs, Snapchat, LinkedIn, Dailymotion (reportedly) | | Paid streaming services |
| **Every MSE capture** (separate SourceBuffers) | Generic progressive | | |

**Mux engine.** FFmpegKit is retired (binaries pulled from Maven in April 2025). Use Media3 instead:

- **Parsing inputs:** Media3 extractors — `Mp4Extractor` / `FragmentedMp4Extractor` for fMP4/CMAF, `TsExtractor` for HLS TS, `MatroskaExtractor` for WebM.
- **Writing output:** `androidx.media3:media3-muxer` `Mp4Muxer`, copying samples without re-encoding. It accepts H.264, H.265, AV1 and VP9 video and AAC and Opus audio. `WebmMuxer` has existed since 1.9.0. Latest Media3 stable is 1.11.1 (2026-09-10).
- **Not Transformer:** its docs don't list HLS/DASH as inputs (UNVERIFIED), so don't depend on it.

## 3. Universal techniques, ranked by how many real downloads they produce

| Rank | Technique | What it covers | Main limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **In-page response-body hooks plus embedded-JSON scanners** (b, d) | Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X, Reddit, Pinterest, Snapchat, Twitch clips, Vimeo config, JW Delivery API. Best quality, audio included, no playback needed. | Needs a per-site adapter (a small pure function you can test with fixtures). Key names are fairly stable. Must run at document start in every frame. |
| 2 | **Native network observation** (a) plus an HLS/DASH downloader | Generic progressive files, manifests with obvious extensions or content types, Vimeo, Dailymotion, Twitch VOD HLS, iframe embeds | URL only: no request body, no response body, no response headers. Not called for `blob:` or `javascript:`, and only for the first URL of a redirect. Blind to SABR, POST APIs and URLs that only appear in JSON. |
| 3 | **MSE / SourceBuffer capture** (c) | Any non-DRM MSE player, however obscured (Meta byte-range DASH, custom manifests). The universal fallback. | Must play through; two tracks to mux; memory and IPC load. Fails with EME, with MSE inside a worker (Chrome 108+ `MediaSourceHandle`), and on `changeType` codec switches. Adaptive quality switches split the capture. |
| 4 | **DOM scraping** (d) | Simple sites, `og:video`, JSON-LD, `data-sources`, `__NEXT_DATA__` | Modern players show a `blob:` src, so there's nothing to scrape. |
| 5 | **Player-library APIs** | JW Player / hls.js / Shaka / video.js sites | Instances are rarely global; mostly adds detail to what rank 2 already finds. |

### (a) `shouldInterceptRequest`: what it sees

- **Seen:**
  - Frame navigations (only the initial URL of a redirect chain).
  - Subresources, including cross-origin iframe subresources (`isForMainFrame=false`).
  - Page `fetch` and XHR.
  - `<video>` progressive requests with a `Range` header. This is why Cordova had to add Range handling for seekable local video.
  - It is called on a non-UI thread, and for `data:` and `file:` URLs as well.
- **Not seen:**
  - `blob:`, `javascript:`, `file:///android_asset`; Chromium marks `blob:` as won't-fix.
  - WebSockets.
  - Requests made by service workers. Those go to the process-wide `ServiceWorkerClient.shouldInterceptRequest`, which has no WebView reference, so you can't tell which tab they came from.
- **Unknown:**
  - Requests from dedicated workers (UNVERIFIED).
  - Whether `getRequestHeaders()` includes `Cookie`. Cookies are probably added later in the network stack, so it likely doesn't (UNVERIFIED).
- **No body access:** there are no request bodies. Reading a response body means proxying the request yourself, which doubles traffic and breaks streaming. **Treat this hook as passive URL observation only.**

### (b) Fetch/XHR body hooks

- **Fetch:** wrap `window.fetch` and call `res.clone()` only when one of these matches:
  - the URL is on an allowlist (`/graphql`, `/api/`, `item_list`, `tweet-result`, `.json`, `config`), or
  - the content type is `json`, `mpegurl` or `dash+xml`.

  Cap body reads at around 5 MB and parse off the hot path with `requestIdleCallback`.
- **XHR:** read `responseText` or `response` on `load`.
- **Sniffing:** check bodies for `#EXTM3U` and `<MPD`.
- **Timing:** hooks must be installed before page scripts run, or the page keeps its own reference to the original `fetch`. On Android, react-native-webview's `injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded` is documented as not 100% reliable.

### (c) MSE capture, done the way browser extensions do it

- **Hooks:** patch `MediaSource.prototype.addSourceBuffer` (record mime and codecs) and `SourceBuffer.prototype.appendBuffer`.
  - **Copy every chunk.** Players reuse their buffers, so keeping the reference saves only the last segment.
  - Also hook `changeType`, `remove`, `abort`, the `timestampOffset` setter and `endOfStream`.
- **Injection:** do it at document start in the page's own JS context. That's how blob-downloader works (MAIN world, `document_start`).
- **Output:** one file per SourceBuffer; mux them afterwards.
- **Forcing buffering:**
  - Mute and set `playbackRate` to 16. That's Chrome's maximum; values above 16 throw `NotSupportedError`.
  - Autoplay (`mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction={false}`), seek to 0 and let it run.
  - Chrome's SourceBuffer quota is roughly 150 MB video / 12 MB audio on desktop and lower on low-memory devices. Players evict data, so capture must copy on append, not read the buffer later.
  - Split the capture at each new init segment (a quality switch) and keep the highest-quality complete run.
  - Where possible, pin top quality through the player API (hls.js `currentLevel`, Shaka `selectVariantTrack`); UNVERIFIED as a general technique.
- **Getting bytes out of the WebView:**
  - **Best:** `WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener` with ArrayBuffer (androidx.webkit 1.8.0+, feature `WEB_MESSAGE_ARRAY_BUFFER`). No base64, so about a third less memory. Listener injection respects origin rules and reports `isMainFrame`.
  - Chunk to 1–2 MB and gate on native acks through `JavaScriptReplyProxy` (chunk size is a conservative choice; IPC limits UNVERIFIED).
  - **Avoid `addJavascriptInterface`:** strings only (base64), synchronous, exposed to every frame with no origin checks.
  - **Avoid the React Native bridge:** strings only, and it goes through the RN JS thread.
  - **Don't use a localhost HTTP sink:** Private/Local Network Access rules may block it (UNVERIFIED).
- **Hazard:** react-native-webview registers its own `ReactNativeWebView` listener for all origins and calls `message.getData()` (`node_modules/react-native-webview/.../RNCWebView.java:256`, origins at `:262`). `getData()` throws `IllegalStateException` on an ArrayBuffer message. **Binary data must go to a separate listener object**, or the app risks crashing.

### (d) DOM scraping

Covered well by the existing observer (`og:video`, JSON-LD, preload links). Add:
- `__UNIVERSAL_DATA_FOR_REHYDRATION__`
- `__NEXT_DATA__`
- `script[data-sjs]`
- `video[data-sources]`
- re-scanning on `history.pushState` / `popstate`, because the social sites are single-page apps

### (e) Injecting into every frame on Android

- In react-native-webview, `injectedJavaScriptForMainFrameOnly=false` is iOS/macOS only per its docs.
- Its Android code stores the flag but never reads it (`RNCWebView.java:66-67`).
- `injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded` is run by `evaluateJavascript` from `onPageStarted` (`RNCWebViewClient.java:~86-91`, `RNCWebView.java:311-317`). That is main-frame only and races the page's scripts.
- The fix is `WebViewCompat.addDocumentStartJavaScript(webView, script, setOf("*"))`:
  - runs before any page script;
  - runs in any frame whose origin matches, including cross-origin iframes;
  - must be called before the first `loadUrl`;
  - does not reach workers.

## 4. Proposed detection architecture for VidoraX

### 4.1 Current state (from the code)

1. **The JSON sources are thrown away.**
   - `API_PATH` rejects `api|graphql|metadata` (`MediaNetworkBridge.kt:71-75`, `:242-245`).
   - `SKIP_PATH` rejects `.json` (`:59-63`, `:221-223`).
   - The JS hooks never read bodies (`injected-script.ts:516-562`).

   The app therefore can't see Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X or Reddit metadata. **Rewrite this part.**
2. **Meta CDN URLs are emitted raw.**
   - `instagramLooksMedia` accepts `/v/t` paths on `fbcdn` / `cdninstagram` (`:386-397`).
   - `canonicalizeObservedUrl` only rewrites YouTube `videoplayback` URLs (`:421-444`).
   - If Meta's player uses `bytestart`/`byteend`, those candidates are partial byte ranges. Even when complete, they're a single video-only or audio-only track, giving truncated or silent downloads (UNVERIFIED on a device).
3. **YouTube heuristics exist**: `itag=` in `:408-409`, `videoplayback` param stripping in `:425-428`. Remove them for policy reasons.
4. **Performance on WebView network threads.**
   - The postinstall patch does `Class.forName` + `getMethod` on **every** request (`scripts/apply-webview-media-hook.js:27-29`).
   - `observeRequestFrom` is `@Synchronized` (`MediaNetworkBridge.kt:132`), so every network thread queues behind one lock.
   - `instagramLooksMedia` compiles a new `Regex` on every call (`:392`).
   - Heavy feeds make hundreds of requests, so this slows page loads.
5. **Attribution gaps.**
   - Service-worker candidates pass `view=null` (`:356`) and get `webViewId = -1` (`:298`), so they can't be tied to a tab.
   - `pageUrl` is always null (`:297`).
6. **Injection** relies on `injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded` (`src/browser/components/BrowserContainer/BrowserWebView.tsx:636`): main-frame only and unreliable, as described in 3(e).

**Worth keeping:**
- The idea of an observe-only native hook.
- The ServiceWorkerClient observer.
- The DOM, `og:video` and JSON-LD scanners in `injected-script.ts`.
- Its active-video tracking.

### 4.2 Target design

```
WebView creation (one reflection call, not per request)
 ├─ addDocumentStartJavaScript(detector.js, ["*"])       // all frames, before page JS
 ├─ addWebMessageListener("__vdx", ["*"])                // JSON strings + ArrayBuffer chunks
 ├─ shouldInterceptRequest → lock-free enqueue(tabId, url, method, range?, isMainFrame, referer)
 ├─ ServiceWorkerClient    → enqueue(tab = match Referer/Origin to the tab's current origin)
 └─ onPermissionRequest(PROTECTED_MEDIA_ID) → deny + mark tab "DRM"

detector.js (per frame)
 ├─ NavTracker: pushState/replaceState/popstate → pageEpoch
 ├─ BodyTaps: fetch clone / XHR load on allowlist or json|mpegurl|dash+xml; sniff #EXTM3U/<MPD
 ├─ EmbeddedJson: rehydration / __NEXT_DATA__ / data-sjs / ld+json / og:video / data-sources
 ├─ SiteAdapters (pure fns, fixture-tested): ig, fb, tiktok, x, reddit, twitch, pinterest,
 │     snapchat, vimeo(config), jw(delivery) → MediaCandidate[]
 ├─ VideoTracker: <video> currentSrc (non-blob), MediaSource ↔ element map (createObjectURL/srcObject)
 ├─ DrmGuard: requestMediaKeySystemAccess / setMediaKeys → session.drm = true
 └─ MseCapture (only on user "Capture" or no-URL fallback, active video only):
       addSourceBuffer/appendBuffer/changeType/remove copies → __vdx ArrayBuffer chunks w/ ack window

Native Resolver (Kotlin, single worker thread)
 ├─ Candidate store per (tabId, pageEpoch); merge URL observations with adapter metadata
 ├─ Group → MediaItem{ variants: Progressive(AV) | Progressive(V)+Audio | HLS | DASH | MseCapture }
 ├─ Rank: progressive-with-audio (max res) > HLS/DASH best V + best A (mux) > MSE capture
 └─ Policy: refuse DRM, SAMPLE-AES/non-identity KEYFORMAT, youtube.com / googlevideo.com

Download engine (foreground service / WorkManager)
 ├─ Request = WebView UA + Referer(page or embedding frame) + CookieManager.getCookie(url)
 │    (TikTok: tt_chain_token must be present; never replay IG/TikTok APIs natively)
 ├─ Progressive: resumable ranged download (strip Meta bytestart/byteend — UNVERIFIED)
 ├─ HLS: master → variant + EXT-X-MEDIA audio; TS or fMP4 (EXT-X-MAP); BYTERANGE; AES-128
 ├─ DASH: SegmentBase (Meta/Reddit single file), SegmentTemplate $Number$/$Time$, SegmentList (Vimeo)
 ├─ Mux: Media3 extractors → media3-muxer Mp4Muxer (sample copy) → .mp4
 └─ Verify: re-extract output; duration > 0, video track present, audio if expected, else fail with reason
```

**MediaCandidate fields:**
- `tabId`, `pageEpoch`, `frameOrigin`, `isMainFrame`
- `site`, `assetId`
- `kind` (progressive / hls / dash / mse)
- `url`, `audioUrl?`
- `width`, `height`, `bitrate`, `codec`
- `hasAudio` (true / false / unknown)
- `watermarked`
- `drm` (none / suspected / confirmed)
- `expiresAt?`
- `requestContext` (referer, cookie domain)
- `provenance` (adapter / network / dom / mse)

### 4.3 Build order

1. **P0:**
   - Install at WebView creation (document-start script, `__vdx` listener, cached-method intercept hook with no lock).
   - Adapters for Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X and Reddit, plus DOM/embedded-JSON scanners.
   - Progressive downloader with cookies, Referer and UA.
   - DRM and YouTube refusal.
2. **P1:** HLS/DASH downloader (including AES-128) and the Media3 mux path. This covers Reddit, Vimeo, X-HLS, Pinterest, Twitch VODs and generic DASH.
3. **P2:** MSE capture, user-triggered on the active video, binary chunks through `__vdx`, muxed on completion.
4. **P3:** Player-API probes (JW, hls.js, Shaka, video.js).

**Testing:** save anonymised JSON, MPD and m3u8 fixtures per site. Adapters, playlist parsers and the resolver should be pure and unit-testable with those fixtures, replacing the 130 `verify-*.ts` scripts. Keep one end-to-end smoke test per site on a device.
